findings.title: Lab planner is seeded with a hand-written idea bank that names the winning transfer family; undisclosed
findings.claim: PAPER 84: 'A planner LLM reads a research state of at most 20,000 characters and proposes hypotheses as JSON'; PAPER 48-49: 'nearly all the gain was one feature family, the transfer of measured responses between related knockdowns'; PLAN 17: 'which system's features make it predict better'.
findings.problem: Every planner round in the lab arms carries an UNEXPLORED IDEA AREAS section built from an eleven-item hand-written idea bank whose second entry is 'perturbation similarity / nearest-neighbour response transfer', the family the Introduction credits with nearly all of the Adamson gain; EXPLORE mode tells the planner to pick from that list. program.md gives the package agent no list and tells it to 'think harder'. The paper describes the research state without this prior, so a lab-over-package result would be partly the idea bank's, and 'which system supplies the better features' is not a fair reading as written.
findings.evidence: genemila/research_state.py:20-32 IDEA_BANK = [("target co-expression", ...), ("perturbation similarity / nearest-neighbour response transfer", ...), ...]; :115 unexplored = [idea for idea, keys in ideas if not any(k in used_text for k in keys)]; :158 "unexplored_idea_areas": unexplored; :180-197 render_state; docs/PROMPTS.md:110 'EXPLORE: propose only new-feature hypotheses from biological idea areas not tried yet (see UNEXPLORED IDEA AREAS)'; tools/task_package/program.md:123-126 'If you run out of ideas, think harder'; README.md:104-105 'The gain is one idea. Nearly all of it is transfer'; grep idea bank in docs/PAPER_COMPARISON.md finds nothing.
findings.fix: Before the first paid call: disclose the idea bank in Methods (its eleven areas, hand-written, naming response transfer) and count it among the lab-only inputs; equalise by appending the same text to program.md (new hashes on #41) or by running the matched lab arm with an empty idea bank; or state that the foreign arms do not get it and read the comparison accordingly.

The package contains none of our features or prompts.' docs/PLAN_H_COMPARISON.md:13-18 (B.1, B.2, 'which system\'s features make it predict better'); :24 'A1 | block G\'s g1 runs ... | not re-run'; :26 'A2 | ... code `baa7dfd` from the checkout `gene-mila-baa7dfd`'; :77 image copies 'never `genemila/`, `configs/` or a prompt of the lab, protocol controls 6 and 7'; dated notes :247-384 say nothing about the idea bank. genemila/providers/mock.py:770 scripted-control template ('Similar perturbation transfer', 'explore', 'similar_pert_knn', 'kNN transfer: average response of training perturbations with similar (co-expressed) targets'). README.md:104-105 'The gain is one idea. Nearly all of it is transfer of the measured responses of training knockdowns whose targets share gene sets or protein-interaction neighbours with the new target.' `git log -S 'nearest-neighbour response transfer' -- genemila/research_state.py` → 7389e25 2026-10-03 'Build autonomous perturbation-prediction laboratory (phase 1-2)', the file's first commit. PR #70 (`git diff cfa8034..origin/claude/block-h-script-gaps --stat`): docs/PLAN_H_COMPARISON.md +22 (a 22:00 UTC note on the probe reset and the Biomni rate flag), block_h scripts, tests/test_block_h_scripts.py, tools/baselines/run_biomni.py; grep for idea bank/unexplored/think harder in the diff: nothing. The five files under review are byte-identical between cfa8034 and the checkout's HEAD (`git diff --stat` empty).
verdict.note: The core observation holds in the files: a fixed, hand-written eleven-item IDEA_BANK whose second entry names nearest-neighbour response transfer is rendered as UNEXPLORED IDEA AREAS in every planner round's state (build_state always emits it, render_state renders every key, planner.refill rebuilds it each round), program.md gives the package agents no list, and neither the PAPER's Methods (line 84 describes the state without it) nor PLAN_H nor PR #70 mention it. Four details are misread or overstated. (1) EXPLORE: the focus lines are appended only when several planner rounds run at once; planner_concurrency defaults to ceil(workers/6) = 1 for the 4-worker A1 and the 1-worker A2, so alive is 0 and focus is None (controller.py:112-113, :152, :174; PROMPTS.md:105 says 8 and 16 workers). The block H planner is shown the list every round but is never told to pick from it; the base prompt asks for ~65% 'new ideas' over the whole state. (2) 'Undisclosed' is true of the PAPER and PLAN_H, not of the repository: PROMPTS.md section 3 documents the section and NOVEL_FEATURE_NEEDS.md:40 names IDEA_BANK; and the PAPER (117-118) and protocol control 6 already state that the package carries none of the lab's prompts and that 'identical' means data, knowledge and feedback tiers. What is missing is the content of the lab's prior, not the fact of a prompt difference. (3) 'Names the winning family': the bank is in the lab's first commit (7389e25, 3 October 2026), before any Adamson result, so it is a design prior the lab started with, not a hint written from the result; the paper should still say the lab's planner had it. (4) The scripted control C0 also carries a kNN transfer template (mock.py:770), so only the package arms A3 and A4 lack the hint; C2 is hand-written. Of the three proposed fixes, 'run the matched lab arm with an empty idea bank' conflicts with the plan as fixed (A1 is block G's runs, not re-run; A2 is pinned to code baa7dfd so that it matches A1; a state-builder change would make A2 a new arm), and 'append the same text to program.md' conflicts with protocol control 6 and PLAN:77 (no lab prompt in the package) even though the hashes are not yet on #41; the third fix (disclose and read accordingly) is the one consistent with the design. Severity: major, not reject. The comparison stays a valid comparison of systems with their own prompts, which the protocol declares as a control and the paper half-states, but claim (2) cannot be read fairly until the Methods say what the lab's prior contains, so the sentence must land before submission and the dated note before the first A2 session.
verdict.corrected_fix: Before the first paid A2 session, add a dated note to docs/PLAN_H_COMPARISON.md and one sentence to the PAPER's 'The lab and the task package' (after line 84): every planner state carries an UNEXPLORED IDEA AREAS section drawn from a fixed eleven-area list in genemila/research_state.py (IDEA_BANK, unchanged since the lab's first commit, 7389e25, 3 October 2026), whose areas include nearest-neighbour response transfer, co-expression, regulatory networks, pathways, PCA programs, graph diffusion, partial correlation, expression transforms, knockdown magnitude, interactions and responsiveness; the package's program.md carries no such list (protocol control 6); the scripted control's templates include a kNN transfer hypothesis (genemila/providers/mock.py:770). Then count it among the lab-only inputs in the reading of claim (2) (PAPER 336-338) and in Limitations (PAPER 357, beside 'the lab's own package and keep rule shape every foreign arm'), and in Table 2 note which idea area each kept lab feature matches, so readers can see how much of the lab's output tracks the list. Do not edit program.md (control 6; the hashes go on #41 unchanged) and do not change A2's pinned code. If an ablation is wanted, it is a new arm ('A2 with IDEA_BANK = []'), added by a dated note with its own approval, never a replacement of A1 or A2.
verdict.reviewer_sentence: In every planning round the lab's planner is shown an UNEXPLORED IDEA AREAS list drawn from a fixed, hand-written bank of eleven biological idea areas (genemila/research_state.py, IDEA_BANK), one of which is nearest-neighbour response transfer, the family the Introduction credits with nearly all of the Adamson gain; the package agents' program.md gives no such list, and the Methods describe the research state without it. State this prior, note that it predates the Adamson results, and count it among the lab-only inputs when reading which system supplies the better features.

findings.title: 'Comparing autonomous research systems' overstates what runs: coding agents on this lab's harness
findings.claim: PAPER 8-9: 'Working title: ... comparing autonomous research systems on unseen genetic perturbations'; PAPER 351-353: 'here each is one more agent writing feature files on our package'.
findings.problem: Only the lab runs as a research system (planner, hypotheses, workers); Biomni runs without its data lake under a never-stop prompt it is designed to leave at <solution>, and the autoresearch-style arm is a harness pattern. The Discussion concedes this, so the title and abstract promise a comparison the design does not make; the harness, prompt, keep rule and evaluator are all the lab's.
findings.evidence: docs/FEATURE_COMPARISON_PROTOCOL.md:55-56 'Biomni is a general coding agent with tool retrieval ... It is not a model to compare as such'; :74-75 'Biomni stops at <solution>, not by a timer'; tools/baselines/run_biomni.py:8-9 use_tool_retriever=True, expected_data_lake_files=[]; tools/task_package/program.md:123-126 'NEVER STOP'.
findings.fix: Retitle and reword the abstract as a comparison of agents on a fixed feature-discovery harness; keep 'autonomous research system' for the lab only; or add a Biomni-native arm (protocol 'B-native') as a separate row.

verdict.evidence_checked: docs/PAPER_COMPARISON.md:8-9 'Working title: Agent-written features for a fixed linear model: comparing autonomous research systems on unseen genetic perturbations.' PAPER:15-16 'can autonomous agents find features that make it predict perturbations it has never seen, and which system finds the better ones' (the abstract says agents, not systems). PAPER:18-21 'this lab with four workers and with one, run in the lab on one clean data bundle; Biomni's general biomedical agent and an autoresearch-style coding-agent loop, each given the task exported from that bundle as a package in karpathy/autoresearch's style; a scripted no-LLM control; and four features translated by hand from CellForge's design' (each arm named as what it is). PAPER:128-130 'A4, Biomni: its A1 agent (source="OpenAI", llm="deepseek-v4-pro", no data lake) given program.md ... A session can end on <solution> before the clock, so the equal wall clock holds only approximately; ended_by is logged'. PAPER:351-353 'No claim about Biomni's or CellForge's performance on their own tasks: here each is one more agent writing feature files on our package'. PAPER:356-357 'the lab's own package and keep rule shape every foreign arm'. docs/FEATURE_COMPARISON_PROTOCOL.md:55-56 'Biomni is a general coding agent with tool retrieval. It has no Perturb-seq prediction tool. Here it is one more agent that writes feature files on the package. It is not a model to compare as such.' Protocol:61-62 'A run with the data lake is a separate arm ("B-native"), optional.' Protocol:74-75 'Biomni stops at <solution>, not by a timer.' tools/baselines/run_biomni.py:10-11 (docstring; the finding cites 8-9) 'A1(path=<package>/scratch/biomni_home, llm=<model>, source="OpenAI", use_tool_retriever=True, expected_data_lake_files=[] ...' and :81-82 the same in code; :17 'ended_by: solution when the agent returned a <solution>'. tools/task_package/program.md:123-126 '**NEVER STOP**: once the loop has begun, do not pause to ask whether to continue.' git diff cfa8034..origin/claude/block-h-script-gaps: PAPER_COMPARISON.md not touched.
verdict.note: The facts hold: only the lab runs as a planner-hypotheses-workers system; Biomni runs with no data lake under the lab's never-stop program.md and leaves at <solution> (run_biomni.py:11, 17, 81-82; protocol 74-75); the autoresearch arm is a harness pattern; the harness, prompt, keep rule and evaluator are the lab's. What the finding misreads: the abstract does not promise what the title does. It asks whether 'autonomous agents' find features for one fixed ridge and names each arm precisely (18-21: 'Biomni's general biomedical agent', 'an autoresearch-style coding-agent loop, each given the task exported ... as a package'), and the Discussion (351-353) and Limitations (356-357) carry the exact disclaimer the finding asks for. The one overclaim is the working title's 'comparing autonomous research systems' (8-9). That is wording, so minor; the B-native arm the finding offers is already in the protocol (61-62) as optional and is not needed to fix the title.
verdict.corrected_fix: Change the working title (PAPER 8-9) to a comparison of agents on one fixed harness, for example 'Agent-written features for a fixed linear model: LLM agents on one feature-discovery harness for unseen genetic perturbations', and use 'autonomous research system' only for Gene-Mila. Leave the abstract (15-21) as it is: it already names each arm as what it is. Optionally add one clause at 128 that Biomni runs with its tool retriever but without its data lake (run_biomni.py:11), so the Methods say in one place what the Discussion says at 351-353. No new arm is needed; B-native stays the protocol's optional extra (61-62).
verdict.reviewer_sentence: The working title promises a comparison of 'autonomous research systems', but only Gene-Mila runs as one: Biomni runs without its data lake under the lab's never-stop prompt and exits at <solution>, and the autoresearch arm is a harness pattern, as the Discussion (lines 351-353) itself concedes. Retitle it as a comparison of agents on one fixed feature-discovery harness; the abstract already describes the arms accurately.

findings.title: No non-agentic deep baseline on the split, though the collaborating lab asked for one
findings.claim: PAPER 13-14: 'Deep models ... do not yet beat simple linear baselines'; PAPER 264: '| CellForge-Models, as reported, other split | not comparable |'; PAPER 361-362: 'CellForge's own model on a GPU are dropped for this window'.
findings.problem: The only deep row is CellForge's published numbers marked not comparable, and STATE is excluded; GEARS, scGPT, CPA-style models and Ahlmann-Eltze's linear baselines are not run on the 88-knockdown split. The 17 October lab meeting asked for a benchmark against non-agentic deep models and traditional baselines. The Limitations do not list the absence.
findings.evidence: docs/GOAL_CRITERIA.md:42 'CellForge's own model run through our evaluator on our split (needs a GPU), or stated as not comparable'; docs/ROADMAP.md:258-259 'CellForge's own pipeline and STATE: no weights or GPU hours'; HANDOFF.md:10-12 'a benchmark paper against CellForge, non-agentic deep-learning models and traditional baselines on the test set'. Not checkable in the repository: whether GEARS or CPA can be trained on CPU within the window.
findings.fix: Add a pre-registered deep-model row on the same split and in the fresh-test batch (a CPU-trainable CPA/scGen or GEARS), or state in Abstract, Discussion and Limitations that no deep model was run and restrict the claim to agent-written features against a fixed linear model.

We ask a narrower question: with the model fixed to one ridge regression'. PAPER:36-39 'is the task of GEARS (Roohani, Huang and Leskovec, 2024), of foundation models and of CellForge's agent-built models ... none of the deep models tested outperformed simple linear baselines'. PAPER:140-146 'Not comparable, and why. CellForge produces a deep model and a training script, not features; it ships no weights, one run takes 4 to 8 GPU-hours ... STATE (Adduri et al., 2025) is out: its public weights were trained on the Replogle K562 screen that the fresh test uses (D9).' PAPER:263-264 '| P0, the built-in start ... | CellForge-Models, as reported, other split | not comparable |'. PAPER:361-362 'Norman package arms and CellForge's own model on a GPU are dropped for this window (docs/ROADMAP.md, section 9).' PAPER:199-202, 211: the frozen batch is 'per arm, its three system models and at most three single features ... plus P0 ... and C0; only clean-bundle arms enter' and 'Then nobody refits, re-exports, adds a model or deposits again'. docs/GOAL_CRITERIA.md:42 (B.5) 'CellForge's own model run through our evaluator on our split (needs a GPU), or stated as not comparable.' docs/ROADMAP.md:256-257 (section 9) 'CellForge's own pipeline and STATE: no weights or GPU hours, an unreproducible table, and a model trained on the fresh-test cohort.' HANDOFF.md:7-12 (21:45 UTC 17 Oct) '21:24 the lab meeting's notes (two branches: a genuinely novel feature means a biology paper ..., else a benchmark paper against CellForge, non-agentic deep-learning models and traditional baselines on the test set; the collaborating lab asks for ...'. git log: PAPER last changed in be3e3dc at 2026-10-17 19:34 UTC; the HANDOFF note landed in cfa8034 at 21:36 UTC, so the paper predates the ask. Protocol:39 'A0 classic | Unperturbed, mean response, additive rule (Norman), ridge on P0, linear regression and random forest reruns (genemila/benchmark/table.py:132-165) | free | partly run'. grep for GEARS/scGPT/CPA/scGen across docs/*.md: no plan, protocol or roadmap line proposes running one. PR #70 branch: PAPER untouched.
verdict.note: Confirmed: no non-agentic deep model is trained or scored on the 88-knockdown split; the only deep rows are CellForge's published numbers marked not comparable (264) and STATE is excluded (145-146); GEARS, which the paper itself cites as the task's reference method (36), is neither run nor declined; and the collaborating lab's ask of 21:24 UTC (HANDOFF 7-12) post-dates the paper's last commit (19:34 UTC) and is not reflected in it. Also unaddressed: the protocol's A0 classic row (plain linear regression, random forest; protocol 39) does not appear in Table 1, so 'traditional baselines' reduce to P0 and C0. What the finding gets wrong: 'The Limitations do not list the absence' is too strong, since 361-362 lists CellForge's own model as dropped and 140-148 gives the reasons for CellForge and STATE; GOAL_CRITERIA B.5 (42) explicitly accepts 'stated as not comparable', which the paper does; and the claims at 336-342 are already restricted to agent-written features for a fixed linear model, so half of the finding's fix (b) is in place. Severity major rather than reject: the paper's narrow question stands without a deep row, but a methods-venue reviewer will ask why the cited reference method is not on the split, and if a deep row is to carry a fresh-test number it must enter the frozen batch before the deposit's sha256 is posted (199-202, 211), which gives the decision a deadline.
verdict.corrected_fix: Record a dated decision (ROADMAP or PLAN_R) before the frozen batch is listed: either one pre-registered non-agentic deep row on the same split (GEARS is the paper's own reference method; CPU feasibility is not checkable in the repository and must be tested free on the Mac first) that enters the PLAN_R deposit beside P0 and C0, or none. If none: add one sentence to the Abstract after 'We ask a narrower question' and one to Limitations (355-362) saying that no deep model was trained on this split (GEARS, scGPT, CPA-style models absent; CellForge and STATE for the reasons in Methods) and that the claims concern agent-written features against a fixed linear model only. In either case add the protocol's A0 classic rows (plain linear regression, random forest; genemila/benchmark/table.py) to Table 1 as the traditional baselines the lab meeting asked for, and note in 'what changed when' that the lab's ask of 17 October 21:24 UTC arrived after the skeleton.
verdict.reviewer_sentence: The paper cites GEARS as the task's reference method and leans on Ahlmann-Eltze's linear-baseline result, yet no deep model is trained on the 88-knockdown split: CellForge's rows are 'not comparable' and STATE is excluded with reasons, but GEARS, scGPT or a CPA-style model are neither run nor declined, and the Limitations do not say so. Either add one pre-registered deep row to the frozen batch before the deposit is hashed, or state in the Abstract and Limitations that no deep model was run and confine the claim to agent-written features for a fixed linear model.

findings.title: Lab arms run an undisclosed exploit engine and model-family search; the paper says the model is fixed
findings.claim: PAPER 14-15: 'with the model fixed to one ridge regression'; PAPER 89-90: 'The controller schedules, fits, scores and stops everything at the wall clock, keeps every completed experiment and calls the highest selection score the best'.
findings.problem: A no-LLM exploit engine runs every 15 seconds whenever fewer experiments are queued than workers, proposing lasso and elastic-net refits, alpha refinements, ablations and exhaustive feature-subset enumerations (29 percent of a DeepSeek-planned run's experiments); the planner may also choose lasso, elastic net or OLS. The package agent has ridge with one fixed alpha grid and one file change per run. The paper never mentions the exploit engine; 'fixed to one ridge' is true of the final scoring only, and block_h_a2.sh does not turn the engine off.
findings.evidence: configs/default.toml:42-44 exploit_depth = 3, python_exploit = true; genemila/exploit.py:1-9, :112-117 for m in ("ridge", "lasso", "elasticnet"): ... spec(f"Fit the best feature set ({pid}) with {m} instead of {model}."); :167-171 'Tier 3 ... enumerate subsets'; genemila/controller.py:191-212 _maybe_exploit (self._next_exploit = time.time() + 15); genemila/prompts.py:37 "model_type": "ridge | lasso | elasticnet | ols"; docs/results/scaling.md:16 exploit share 0.290 ± 0.008; docs/mac/block_h/block_h_a2.sh:50-53 (no schedule.python_exploit=false); tools/task_package/evaluate.py:472 cross_validate(ctx, feats, {}, "ridge", alphas, ...).
findings.fix: Add to Methods (The lab) that the controller queues deterministic follow-ups without an LLM and the planner may pick lasso or OLS; say only tools/feature_compare.py fixes ridge; report per lab run the share of experiments proposed by python:exploit and the selected model's family; or run the matched lab arm with --set schedule.python_exploit=false.

verdict.note: Confirmed in the files. Every cited line reads as the finding says: the engine is on by default (default.toml:43) and at baa7dfd, runs at most every 15 s whenever queued < workers (controller.py:194-199), proposes add/drop/alpha/model-swap/subset candidates (exploit.py:90-117, 167-171), the planner's JSON may name lasso, elastic net or OLS (prompts.py:37), `best()` ranks across all model types (db.py:203-206), and `--source-run` hands the comparison the top-scored experiment's feature set whatever model chose it (feature_audit.py:1030-1033, feature_compare.py:1136). Neither document mentions the engine or the model search, including the PLAN's dated notes; the A2 script passes no override. Two things strengthen it beyond the finding: (1) the paper's description of C0 as "fixed hypothesis templates" (:133-135) is also incomplete, since 61-95% of a scripted control's experiments are the engine's follow-ups (scaling.md:16, columns 2-4; :40-44); (2) in g1_r3, one of the three A1 runs already in block H's table, the selected model EXP_0796 is itself an engine proposal (hypothesis_group exploit_alpha_EXP_0795), so the engine is not only a share of the search but the author of a reported winner. Two caveats on the finding's own details: the 0.290 ± 0.008 share is from the DeepSeek-planned runs on code 537344f (n=2), not from block G's baa7dfd, whose share no reading records; and the engine's swap loop covers ridge/lasso/elasticnet only (exploit.py:112), OLS comes from the planner, which the finding states correctly. The one part of the proposed fix to reject: running A2 with `--set schedule.python_exploit=false` would be wrong, because A1 is block G's runs, not re-run, with the engine on, and block_h_a2.sh:4 fixes A2 as differing from A1 in the worker count only; switching the engine off would confound the A1/A2 comparison and make A2 unlike C0 too. Severity major, not reject: the fair test does fix ridge (feature_compare.py:1085, evaluate.py:472), the engine is part of the lab system under comparison and C0 shares it, so no reading becomes invalid; but the abstract's framing and the Methods' description of two arms are false as written and must change before submission, and the PLAN should pre-register the engine's setting and the per-run readings before A2 runs.

State explicitly that only `tools/feature_compare.py` and the package's `evaluate.py` fix ridge. 3. PAPER :133-135, C0: say the control is the scripted templates plus the same deterministic engine, which proposed 61-95% of the scripted controls' experiments on record (`docs/results/scaling.md:16`). 4. PLAN Arms (:24-26) and a dated note: pre-register that `schedule.python_exploit` and `exploit_depth` stay at their defaults in A2 and C0, as in A1 (block_h_a2.sh:50-53 passes no override), so A2 differs from A1 in the worker count only; do not run A2 with `python_exploit=false`. 5. verdict.reviewer_sentence: The abstract states the model is "fixed to one ridge regression", but the lab arms search over ridge, lasso, elastic net and OLS (the planner's JSON, `genemila/prompts.py:37`) and run an undisclosed no-LLM exploit engine (`genemila/exploit.py`, on by default) that proposed 29% of a DeepSeek-planned run's experiments (`docs/results/scaling.md:16`), 61-95% of the scripted control's, and the selected model of one of the three A1 runs already in Table 1 (g1_r3, group `exploit_alpha_EXP_0795`). The Methods must describe this engine and the model search, state that ridge is fixed only in `tools/feature_compare.py` and the package's `evaluate.py`, correct the control's description, and report the engine's share and the selected model's family per lab run; the A2 arm should keep the engine on, as A1 had it, and the plan should say so.

findings.title: Lab arms write code with deepseek-flash; the paper says every LLM arm ran on one LLM
findings.claim: PAPER 21: 'The four LLM arms ran three 20-minute sessions each on one LLM'; PAPER 356: 'one LLM, deepseek-v4-pro, unless the probe forces the disclosed deepseek-flash fallback for A3'; protocol 113: 'The same LLM (deepseek-v4-pro) wherever the system allows it.'
findings.problem: A1, A1-ablation and A2 write every feature with deepseek-flash workers and plan with deepseek-v4-pro; A3 and A4 write every feature with deepseek-v4-pro. The abstract and Limitations say one LLM, the Methods say otherwise, so the code-writing model is confounded with 'the system' and the reader cannot tell. 'Wherever the system allows it' does not hold: run_research.py takes --worker-model, so the lab could run v4-pro workers; the choice is cost and B2 compatibility. The plan discloses a flash switch for A3 but gives the lab's flash workers no such note.

verdict.note: Confirmed in every particular. The lab arms (A1 and A1-ablation from block G, A2 in block H) plan with deepseek-v4-pro and have every feature written by deepseek-flash workers (block_g_run.sh:78-79, block_h_a2.sh:50-51); the package arms have their code written by deepseek-v4-pro (block_h_a3.sh:13, block_h_a4.sh:14). The PAPER's Methods (92-93, 316) say so, but its abstract (21) and Limitations (356) say every LLM arm ran on one LLM, and Table 1's arm labels carry no model, so the paper contradicts itself and the lab-vs-package comparison confounds the system with the code-writing model. The protocol's fairness control 3 ("the same LLM wherever the system allows it", :113) is not met by the lab: run_research.py takes --worker-model and the pricing table holds deepseek-v4-pro, so the lab allows it; the flash workers are an inheritance from B2's settings and a cost choice. The PLAN discloses the fact in its Arms table (24, 26) but gives it no note as a difference, while the far smaller A3 alias fallback gets one (162-164). The direction of the confound is not obvious (a weaker, cheaper code writer, but four of them, more attempts per dollar under the $1.00 worker cap, and a stronger planner), which is exactly why it has to be named. Not touched by PR #70. One correction to the finding's proposed fix (a): running A2 with v4-pro workers would break A2's one stated purpose, to differ from A1 in the worker count only (block_h_a2.sh:4), since A1 is block G's flash-worker runs and is not re-run; fix (b) is the right one, with an optional extra disclosed arm if Andres funds it.
verdict.corrected_fix: Keep A2 as planned (flash workers, matching A1) and fix the words, before the chain for the plan and before submission for the paper. (1) PAPER 21-22: "The four LLM arms ran three 20-minute sessions each on DeepSeek models: the lab arms plan with deepseek-v4-pro and write every feature with deepseek-flash workers, the package arms plan and write with deepseek-v4-pro". (2) PAPER 356: replace "one LLM, `deepseek-v4-pro`, unless ..." with "one model family; the code-writing model differs between the lab arms (deepseek-flash workers, inherited from B2's settings and kept so A2 matches block G's A1, at about a quarter of v4-pro's price) and the package arms (deepseek-v4-pro), so the system and the code-writing model are confounded in the lab-versus-package reading; the client and isolation differences are likewise disclosed, not removed". (3) PAPER Table 1 (254-258): label the lab rows with their models the way `tools/results_table.py`'s `run_arm` already does ("deepseek-v4-pro planner, deepseek-flash workers") and the package rows "deepseek-v4-pro". (4) PLAN: a dated note before the chain under the Arms table stating that the lab arms' workers are deepseek-flash, why A2 keeps them (it must differ from A1 in the worker count only), and that the reading in section Readings item 2 reports the served model per arm, so the lab rows show two models. (5) Protocol control 3 (:113): "The same LLM (deepseek-v4-pro) for every package arm and for the lab's planner; the lab's workers are deepseek-flash (B2's settings, kept so A1 and A2 match), a disclosed difference." (6) Optional, only on Andres's written approval and as its own arm, never in place of A2: A2-pro, the one-worker lab with --worker-model deepseek-v4-pro under the same $1.00/$1.50 caps, which would separate the code-writing model from the system; note that v4-pro workers get fewer attempts under the same worker cap, so even that arm is matched on money, not on attempts.
verdict.reviewer_sentence: The abstract and the Limitations state that every LLM arm ran on one LLM (deepseek-v4-pro), but the Methods and the run scripts show that the lab arms' features were all written by deepseek-flash workers while the Biomni and Codex arms wrote theirs with deepseek-v4-pro; the code-writing model is therefore confounded with the system under comparison and must be named as such in the abstract, Table 1 and the limitations, with the reason the lab keeps the cheaper workers.

findings.title: Abstract, Table 1 and Discussion present the seen out-of-fold tier as if it were held out

findings.problem: New fold seeds do not make the labels unseen: every arm selected hundreds of attempts on the same 50 training perturbations (the lab on val1 plus 5-fold OOF of the same labels), which Methods and the tool state, and the tool stamps every such verdict 'OOF only, not held out'. The abstract reports a per-arm number from that tier, 'fold seeds no system used' reads as independence, Table 1's header carries no 'seen' label, Discussion claim (1) lists 'out of fold' beside the fresh cohort as supporting a gain claim, and 'two matched permutation nulls' is wrong for non-proportional rows, which get one. A reviewer reading the abstract alone takes the development table for a fair test.

verdict.reviewer_sentence: The abstract and Discussion claim (1) present the out-of-fold tier as evidence of a gain ('out of fold and on a fresh cohort'), while Methods state that every system selected on those labels and that a development verdict 'proves nothing'; the abstract, the Table 1 caption and claim (1) should say the tier is a seen screen, and the abstract's 'two matched nulls' should be stated as a gene null plus a perturbation null for parent-proportional candidates only.

findings.title: Block F's withdrawn biology reading dominates the abstract and a third of Results
findings.claim: PAPER 27-32: 'In an earlier block on Norman the agents built, unprompted, a feature whose formula matches a published CRISPRa dependence ... under the corrected test it fails the minimum effect and the perturbation null'; PAPER 339: claim (3) 'That the agents built, unprompted, a feature that restates known biology'.
findings.problem: Six of twenty abstract lines go to a Norman result from a non-clean bundle under a withdrawn test that fails the corrected test, and the Discussion lists it among supported claims while also saying 'No biology discovery claim'. The six corrected passes read a tier-3 screen. 'Unprompted' is inexact: the planner's knowledge section shows the annotation table's description and column names (including cpg_oe_promoter). For a methods venue the usable content is one paragraph on the degenerate null and its replacement.
findings.evidence: docs/GOAL_CRITERIA.md:86-96 (the 22:05 UTC reading withdrawn), :137-147 (six passes all read the Replogle screen; CpG fails gain and perturbation null); tools/build_gene_annotation.py:27 'description ... every column with its unit (shown to the planner)'; genemila/research_state.py:173-178 (knowledge section rendered to the planner); tools/export_task_package.py:117-129 knowledge_lines.
findings.fix: Drop block F from the Abstract; reduce lines 283-312 to a short methods-lesson paragraph citing the corrected files, with the narrative in a supplement; replace 'unprompted' with 'with no hypothesis given, from a table whose columns were named in the prompt'; move claim (3) to 'claims it cannot support'.

verdict.note: The weight and the word stand: six of the abstract's twenty lines and thirty of the Results' ninety-one go to a Norman result from the non-clean `norman_ga` bundle that fails the corrected test, and 'unprompted' compresses 'no human hypothesis' while the knowledge line every planner and worker read named `cpg_oe_promoter` among the columns (build_gene_annotation.py:262, 895 characters, under lab.py's 900-character cut). Two parts of the finding misread the paper. First, there is no contradiction between claim (3) and 'No biology discovery claim': claim (3) is that the agents wrote a formula matching a published dependence (a methods-level recovery), the other sentence denies new biology; the paper is consistent. Second, everything the finding wants disclosed is already on the page: the non-clean bundle (287), the six corrected passes reading a tier-3 screen (305-307), the CpG row failing the perturbation null (309-310), the withdrawn first reading (232-236). What is at issue is placement and emphasis, not accuracy. On claim (3) itself: after the corrected test the CpG scalar is indistinguishable from a random per-perturbation scalar (pooled perturbation p 0.363), so 'restates known biology' is a statement about the formula's text, not a measured effect; it is a weak claim, hedged by its own clause, and belongs with the methods lesson of claim (4) rather than in the 'cannot support' list. Not touched by PR #70.
verdict.corrected_fix: Before submission: cut the block F sentence from the Abstract (keep one clause at most, e.g. 'an earlier Norman block showed the first null degenerate for proportional features, which fixed the test used here'); fold 283-312 into one paragraph on the degenerate null, its replacement and the corrected re-read, citing `norman_f_corrected_stage2/feature_compare.json` and `norman_f_corrected_pooled_holm/pooled_holm.json`, with the narrative (reading 2, sealed scores, coefficients) in a supplement. Replace 'unprompted' in the Abstract and in claim (3) with 'with no human hypothesis given, from a table whose columns were named in the prompt' (PLAN_F:24, GOAL_CRITERIA A.1's own words). Merge claim (3) into claim (4) as a methods lesson ('the agents wrote a formula matching a published CRISPRa dependence; under the corrected test it is indistinguishable from a random per-perturbation scalar'), rather than listing it as a supported claim or moving it to the 'cannot support' list. No change to GOAL_CRITERIA is needed.
verdict.reviewer_sentence: The abstract's final third and a third of the Results report a Norman feature from a bundle that still held a perturbation screen, under a test the authors themselves withdrew, which under the corrected test fails both the minimum effect and the perturbation null; this belongs in the Methods as the lesson that fixed the null, not in the abstract. 'Unprompted' overstates the case: no hypothesis was given, but the knowledge line shown to every agent named the promoter CpG column.

findings.title: 'Which system finds the better features' is not identifiable from these arms
findings.claim: PAPER 42-44: 'whether this lab's planner-and-workers design finds better ones than a single coding agent in a loop, a general biomedical agent, or a scripted control, on the same task'; PAPER 337-338: claim (2) 'Which system ... supplies the better features under the arm rule'.
findings.problem: Between the lab arms and the package arms at least seven things change at once: the code-writing LLM, evaluations per minute, the idea bank, the exploit engine's search, the selection rule, the prompt and the client's sandbox and shell timeout. With three sessions per arm none can be separated, so a difference says which configured pipeline did better here, not that the planner-and-workers design did. Only A1 against A2 changes one thing (the worker count).
findings.evidence: docs/mac/block_h/block_h_a2.sh:50-53 (flash workers, lab caps); genemila/controller.py:88-89 (every core); genemila/research_state.py:20-32 (idea bank); genemila/exploit.py:112-117 (model swaps); genemila/db.py:203-206 against tools/task_package/evaluate.py:251 (selection rules); genemila/prompts.py:188-204 against tools/task_package/program.md; tools/baselines/run_codex.sh:127-151 and docs/PLAN_H_COMPARISON.md:257-267 (client differences).
findings.fix: Reword the question and claim (2) to 'which pipeline, as configured here, hands back the better features at this clock and cap'; add a Methods table of what differs per arm; reserve the 'planner-and-workers design' wording for the A1 against A2 contrast.

verdict.note: Every one of the seven differences is in the files, and the first is worse than the finding says: the lab arms' code-writing LLM is deepseek-flash (block_h_a2.sh:51; block_g_run.sh:79; PAPER 93, 316) while A3 and A4 write code with deepseek-v4-pro (PAPER 124, 128), so the Abstract's 'on one LLM' (21) and the Limitations' 'one LLM, deepseek-v4-pro' (355-356) are false for the lab arms, and protocol control 3 ('the same LLM wherever the system allows it', 113) is not met as configured, since the lab allows a v4-pro worker. The paper discloses the client differences (125-127, 358) and the two selection rules (161-162), but its claim that the selection difference 'does not reach the table' is overstated: feature_compare.py:1136-1149 builds a lab arm's system row and candidates from db.best()'s selected model, so the lab's highest-combined-score rule and the package's noise keep rule decide which features each hand-back contains, and the tool only rescores them. Claim (2) at 337-338 is already worded at the pipeline level, so the defect sits in the Introduction's 'planner-and-workers design' attribution (42-44), in the one-LLM statements, and in the absence of a Methods table of what differs per arm. Only A1 against A2 varies one factor, as block_h_a2.sh:4 says. Major, not reject: the data will still answer which configured pipeline hands back better features at this clock and cap; the text must change before submission, and the LLM statement before the A2 sessions are written up.
verdict.corrected_fix: (1) Reword PAPER 42-44 to 'whether this lab, as configured here, hands back better features than a coding agent in a loop, Biomni or a scripted control on the same data, clock and cap', and reserve 'planner-and-workers design' for the A1 against A2 contrast, the only one-factor pair (block_h_a2.sh:4). (2) Correct PAPER 21 and 355-356: the lab arms write code with deepseek-flash workers under a deepseek-v4-pro planner, the package arms with deepseek-v4-pro; name this as the first confound, and note that protocol control 3 is met for the planner only. (3) Add a Methods table 'what differs per arm' with one row each for: code-writing LLM and planner; parallel evaluations (controller.py:87-89 cpu slots, 4 workers against one sequential evaluate.py); the idea bank (research_state.py:18-30); the exploit engine (exploit.py); the selection rule (db.py:201-204 against evaluate.py:251) and its effect on hand-back membership (feature_compare.py:1136-1149); the prompt (prompts.py:186-202 against program.md); the client sandbox and shell timeout (run_codex.sh:127-151; PLAN_H 258-267); the caps ($1.00 workers + $1.50 planner against a $2.50 session). (4) Soften PAPER 162 to 'the tool rescores every hand-back from its parent, but each arm's selection rule decides which features the hand-back holds'. No script change: A2 should keep flash workers so that A1 against A2 stays a one-factor contrast.
verdict.reviewer_sentence: The Introduction asks whether 'this lab's planner-and-workers design' finds better features than a coding-agent loop or Biomni, but between the lab arms and the package arms the code-writing LLM (deepseek-flash workers against deepseek-v4-pro), evaluation throughput, the idea bank, the exploit engine, the selection rule, the prompt and the client sandbox all change at once, so the contrast identifies a configured pipeline, not a design; only A1 against A2 varies one factor. The Abstract's 'on one LLM' and the Limitations' 'one LLM, deepseek-v4-pro' are moreover inaccurate for the lab arms, whose workers are deepseek-flash by the paper's own Methods.

Since 537344f scripted runs also take exploit-engine follow-ups (94 percent of experiments), so C0 is neither fixed templates nor deterministic. The Introduction cites the 0.554 control and omits the repository's own 0.593; C0 reads as a neutral control when it is a human-written positive control.

verdict.note: The central objection is confirmed from the files. (1) C0's hypotheses and the mock worker's templates are feature recipes the project wrote on this benchmark (mock.py SCRIPTED_HYPOTHESES and TEMPLATES); two of the eight are response-transfer features that read train_delta (similar_pert_knn via the 'similar' template, response_components via 'components'). (2) response_components is the hand-written transfer feature the README says was designed after 26 sealed results had been read, and the control carrying it scored 0.593 (control_components_w4_r0 @74e07ca, same data/adamson_cf). (3) The code pinned for the block-H C0 runs, baa7dfd, carries response_components, so the C0 the PLAN pre-registers is the 0.593-class control, yet PLAN:29 names only the @2492e11 runs (0.554) as the existing reference and the PAPER's Introduction cites 0.554 and never mentions 0.593, while the project's own README (lines 16, 75, 106, 487-490) reports both and says the agents' lead disappears against the stronger control. The PAPER calls only C2 hand-written (line 23). (4) The exploit engine is gated by schedule.python_exploit (default true), not by the planner, and the PLAN's C0 command leaves it on; in scripted runs it proposed 94-95 percent of experiments at 537344f and 74e07ca (61 percent at 72a53c5). Details the finding misreads: (a) response_components entered the scripted list at 74e07ca on 5 October, not 'since baa7dfd'; baa7dfd is only the pinned checkout and inherits it. (b) 'neither fixed templates nor deterministic' is overstated: the hypothesis list is fixed and the exploit engine is itself a deterministic rule set; what varies is scheduling order and the follow-ups it produces, and the repeats are near-identical (sealed gain sd 0.0002 over six runs @72a53c5), which the PAPER already half-concedes ('three near-identical runs', 'bound timing noise only'); 'deterministic' in lines 134 and 261 is a wording slip, not a hidden source of noise. (c) The 'ends when its templates run out' clause is right: even with the exploit engine the @74e07ca run ended after 3.0 minutes. The readings themselves stay valid (C0 is re-run fresh on the clean bundle and scored by the same out-of-fold tool), so this is a disclosure and labelling problem, not an invalid design; it must be fixed before the first paid session because the pre-registered C0 (PLAN:225) is being described against the wrong existing number, and before submission because the Introduction's 0.554 without 0.593 is selective reporting the README itself contradicts. Not addressed by PR #70, whose only PLAN change is the probe-reset and rate-card note.
verdict.corrected_fix: PAPER lines 133-135 and 261: describe C0 as 'the scripted planner's eight fixed hypotheses (genemila/providers/mock.py, SCRIPTED_HYPOTHESES), implemented by the mock worker's template code, both written by the project on this benchmark; two are response-transfer features that read the training responses (similar_pert_knn; response_components, added at 74e07ca on 5 October after 26 sealed results had been read, README Limitations), followed by the deterministic exploit engine's follow-ups (schedule.python_exploit, on by default; 94-95 percent of the experiments in the 537344f and 74e07ca control runs, docs/results/scaling.md), so its three runs are near-identical rather than identical and bound timing noise only'. Replace 'deterministic' in the Table 1 row with 'fixed recipe, near-identical runs'. PAPER lines 47-48: cite both numbers from docs/results/scaling.md, '0.554 for the no-LLM control on the code of 4 October (scale_control_r0-r5 @2492e11) and 0.593 once its list included one hand-written transfer feature written after the sealed readings (control_components_w4_r0 @74e07ca), level with the agent arms on pearson_delta (README, Results on Adamson and Limitations)'. PLAN line 29: add control_components_w4_r0 (@74e07ca, data/adamson_cf, sealed 0.593) beside the @2492e11 runs, and state that the C0 run from gene-mila-baa7dfd carries response_components, so block H's C0 is the 0.593-class control; say whether python_exploit stays on for C0 (it does under the command as written) or is turned off with --set schedule.python_exploit=false, and why. Discussion and Table 1 reading: read C0 as the project's own hand-written reference recipe (a human positive control with one post-hoc feature), so that an arm's lead over C0 is a lead over the project's own features, and a tie with it means the agents re-derived them; align this with README lines 487-490, which already say so.
verdict.reviewer_sentence: The 'scripted no-LLM control' (C0) is presented as fixed templates and deterministic, and the Introduction cites its 0.554 while omitting the repository's own 0.593 for the same control once one hand-written transfer feature, written after 26 sealed readings, joined its list (README, Results and Limitations), which is the list the pinned code baa7dfd runs in this block. The control's hypotheses and template code are the project's own feature recipes, two of them response-transfer features and one post hoc, and 94-95 percent of its experiments come from the exploit engine; it should be described and read as a human-written reference recipe, not a neutral no-LLM floor.

findings.title: No P1 parent and no positive control on the clean Adamson bundle, where every reading so far is null
findings.claim: PAPER 79-80: 'The protocol allows a second parent P1, a strong known set (--parent-run); block H does not score one'.
findings.problem: Every arm starts from the three built-ins, and the transfer family that explains the earlier Adamson gains is in the lab's idea bank, in C0's templates and in C2, so against P0 alone the winner is whoever re-implements that recipe best. On adamson_cf_clean_tables every pre-registered reading is negative (block G's 221 rows, family 8), so an all-null Table 2 cannot be told from a test that resolves nothing at 50 perturbations under a family-wise correction. findings.title: A session with no kept feature: collect_handback scores working files, feature_compare errors, and the arm rule cannot be won
findings.claim: PLAN 215-218: 'The package arms' candidate set is runs/kept/features/ at the kill, never the working features/ ... A session that handed back no kept feature is a row with the parent's score, reported, not dropped.'
findings.problem: collect_handback.py falls back to features/ filtered by results.tsv and, without results.tsv, to every features/*.py, while evaluate.py writes runs/kept/features only on a baseline or a keep; so a session that wrote files but never evaluated them hands back unevaluated working files the protocol calls an artefact never scored. For a --source directory with no passing file, feature_compare writes the set row with status 'error', not a parent-score row, so the arm's mean over three sessions would be assembled by hand. On the fresh test such a session deposits P0 itself, its paired gain is identically zero, and arm_rule requires every g_r to carry G's sign, so one empty session makes its arm unable to beat any baseline. None of this is stated.
findings.evidence: tools/baselines/collect_handback.py:58-72 kept_files: if kept.is_dir(): return ... / tsv = pkg / "results.tsv" ... return sorted((pkg / "features").glob("*.py")), "features/ (no results.tsv)"; tools/task_package/evaluate.py:386-393 (kept state written only inside finish() when not discard); tests/test_baselines.py:81 assert s["origin"] == "features/ (no results.tsv)"; docs/FEATURE_COMPARISON_PROTOCOL.md:50-52; tools/feature_compare.py:1227-1228 set_row.update(status="error", reason="no feature of this source passed the checks"); tools/arm_reading.py:9-10, :155 if G > k * se and bool((g_ > 0).all()) and wa > total / 2.
findings.fix: Make collect_handback.py copy nothing (origin 'none') when runs/kept/features is absent and keep working files under artefacts/ for reading 4; say in PLAN reading 1 that an empty hand-back is entered by hand as the parent's set row (gain 0); say in PAPER 'The fresh test' that a zero-gain session fails the same-sign condition, so an arm with an empty session is read descriptively only.

:1166-1169 rows built from `sorted(src_dir.glob("*.py"))`; :1178 `live = [f for f, r in rows.items() if r["status"] == "ok"]`; :1227-1228 `elif not live and not from_run: set_row.update(status="error", reason="no feature of this source passed the checks")`. tools/arm_reading.py:9-10 "a run that selected its reference enters with g_r = 0 and s_r = 0"; PR #70 (git diff cfa8034...origin/claude/block-h-script-gaps): touches docs/PLAN_H_COMPARISON.md (one dated note: probe reset, miss rate), block_h_common.sh (miss_rate), block_h_probe.sh, block_h_a4.sh, block_h_reset_probe.sh, run_biomni.py, tests/test_block_h_scripts.py; nothing on collect_handback, reading 1 or the paper.
verdict.note: Confirmed: (a) the plan's "never the working features/" is contradicted by collect_handback.py's last fallback, which copies every features/*.py when results.tsv is absent, i.e. when the agent wrote files but evaluate.py never ran (a Biomni session that returns <solution> without evaluating, or a timeout before its first evaluation; nothing in the session scripts runs the baseline for the agent). Those are exactly the unevaluated files protocol section 2 says are never scored; the manifest records the origin, so it is detectable, but no rule says what to do with it. (b) For an empty hand-back directory feature_compare.py emits a set row with status "error", not a parent-score row, so the "row with the parent's score" of PLAN 217-218 and PAPER 251-252 must be entered by hand from the parent tiers of the same feature_compare.json; the plan does not say so. (c) An empty session's system model is P0 itself, so on the fresh test its paired gain against P0 is exactly 0 and arm_reading's one-sign condition fails for the arm against P0. What the finding gets wrong: "unable to beat any baseline" is overstated, the zero gain is only against P0; against C0 (or any other reference) the session's gain is P0 minus C0, not zero. The middle fallback (results.tsv status keep without a kept directory) is not an exposure: every keep or baseline writes runs/kept/features, so that branch copies only stems already kept and is reachable only if the agent deleted runs/. The same-sign rule itself is stated (PAPER 209, PLAN_R 153-155); what is unstated is its consequence for an arm with an empty session. Severity major, not reject: nothing becomes irreproducible (origin and hashes are in the manifest), but which files enter the candidate set and how an empty session is entered must be fixed before the first paid session, since the candidate hashes are posted before the tool runs.
verdict.corrected_fix: (1) tools/baselines/collect_handback.py: when runs/kept/features is absent, copy nothing to <dest>/<arm>_r<seed>/ (origin e.g. "none: evaluate.py never ran"), list the working features/*.py in the manifest with sha256 as artefacts only (or copy them under <dest>/artefacts/), and drop or keep the results.tsv branch (it is harmless); update tests/test_baselines.py:81 accordingly. (2) PLAN reading 1: add that an empty hand-back gives feature_compare.json a set row with status "error" (reason "no feature of this source passed the checks"), that the arm table enters that session as the parent row's OOF numbers (ΔM1 = 0, wins 0 of n, 0 features) by hand, citing the parent tiers of the same feature_compare.json, and that the manifest's origin tells an empty hand-back from one whose files all failed the checks. (3) PAPER, The fresh test, and PLAN_R section 7: state that a session whose system model equals P0 has a paired gain of exactly 0 against P0, so under the one-sign condition an arm with such a session cannot be called better than P0 (it is still read against C0 and the other references), and is reported descriptively against P0.
verdict.reviewer_sentence: The plan says the package arms' candidate set is runs/kept/features/, "never the working features/", yet collect_handback.py falls back to every features/*.py when evaluate.py never ran, so a session that wrote files without evaluating hands back the very files the protocol says are never scored; and the "row with the parent's score" promised for an empty hand-back is not what feature_compare.py produces (a set row with status "error"), so the plan must say how that row is entered. On the fresh test an empty session's model is P0 itself, its gain against P0 is identically zero, and the one-sign condition then bars the arm from beating P0 (not every baseline); the paper should state that consequence of its own rule.

findings.title: Equal wall time is not equal compute: the lab scores tens of parallel experiments, the package one at a time
findings.claim: PAPER 111: 'Two kinds of arm share one bundle, one split, one clock and one final scoring.'; PLAN 221-223: 'per arm ... each arm's median evaluate.py runs per session from results.tsv.'
findings.problem: The lab scores experiments concurrently on every core (cpu_slots = os.cpu_count()) with four workers, a feature cache and one fold seed per experiment; the package evaluator holds a lock so one evaluation runs at a time, each on three fold seeds plus a full fit, and under Codex a shell call dies at 10 s unless the model asks for more. Block G's G1 runs produced about 70 scored experiments each in 20 minutes; a serial agent manages a small fraction. Table 1 has no evaluations column for the lab arms, so the reader cannot see that the clock buys the lab an order of magnitude more scored candidates.

The per-evaluation cost is asymmetric as claimed: a lab experiment is five folds of one fold seed plus one full fit per alpha (default.toml:24, lab.py:105, pipeline.py:257-266); a package evaluation is three seeds times five folds plus one full fit per alpha (evaluate.py:470-473, export default "0,1,2"), run serially under a lock (evaluate.py:45, 180-185), after a smoke test, with Codex's 10 s shell cut on top (PLAN:258-263). Two details are misread. (1) "Concurrently on every core": the semaphore allows a core's worth of slots, but each Worker runs one experiment end to end (worker.py:65-71, 269) and the controller starts n_workers workers (controller.py:277-278), so the lab's concurrency is min(workers, cores): four for A1 and one for A2, not every core. A2 is therefore the lab's own serial arm, which the finding does not say; its remaining advantages over A3/A4 are the cheaper one-seed evaluation and the exploit engine queueing deterministic follow-ups without LLM time (controller.py:191-212; 29 to 54 % of completed experiments on 537344f, scaling.md:16). (2) The feature cache is on both sides (default.toml:21; evaluate.py:23, 465), so it is not a lab-only advantage. The "about 70 scored experiments" for G1 is 221/3 add-one rows that read a table (PAPER:319), not a recorded completed count; the repository holds no per-run count for G1, but scaling.md:14 shows 20-minute four-worker lab runs completing 136 to 616 experiments, so the order-of-magnitude claim is well founded even though the package side is a projection (no session has run, PLAN:6). The lab-side source for the fix exists: summary.json["experiments_completed"] and ["completed_by_proposer"] (report.py:255-256). Severity major, not reject: the data to add the column exist in every run directory, so the reading is recoverable, but the plan's reading 2 as written cannot produce the count for A1, A2 and C0, and a venue reviewer would not accept "one clock" as compute parity without the count and a Methods sentence.

A Methods sentence at PAPER:111-116: "The lab runs one experiment per worker at a time (four in A1, one in A2), each scored on five folds of one fold seed plus one full fit, and its exploit engine queues deterministic follow-ups without LLM time; a package agent runs one `evaluate.py` at a time under a lock, each after a smoke test and on three fold seeds plus one full fit; both cache feature blocks. The shared clock therefore buys the arms different numbers of scored candidates, reported in Table 1." verdict.reviewer_sentence: The arms share a 20-minute clock but not the compute it buys: a four-worker lab run scores up to four experiments at once, each on one fold seed, and completes hundreds per session (136 to 616 in the authors' own scaling table), while a package agent runs one evaluate.py at a time under a lock on three fold seeds; Table 1 has no evaluations column for the lab arms and the Methods never state the asymmetry, so the reader cannot tell what the equal clock gave each system.

findings.title: Goal B.1 'identical task package' is reinterpreted in the paper, not amended in GOAL_CRITERIA
findings.claim: PAPER 117-118: 'Goal B.1's "identical task package" is read for the lab arms as the same public data, knowledge files and two feedback tiers, which the package ships from the bundle.'; GOAL_CRITERIA 35: 'At least three systems ran on the identical task package (ours; a single-agent autoresearch-style loop; Biomni)'.
findings.problem: GOAL_CRITERIA is the pre-registered rule and changes only by dated notes, yet carries no note of this reading, which appears first in the paper's parenthesis. The lab arms never run on the package: A1 is block G's runs, not re-run; A2 is a run_research.py run on the bundle; they get the worker prompt and planner state instead of program.md, the idea bank, the exploit engine, model-family choices, parallel scoring, one fold seed (cv_seed 0 against package seeds 0, 1, 2) and argmax selection. Redefining the criterion in the paper that reports it is the drift a pre-registration referee returns.

verdict.note: Confirmed on the substance: the registered criterion says 'identical task package (ours; ...)', the lab arms do not and will not run on the package (A1 is block G's runs, A2 a run_research.py run on the bundle), and neither GOAL_CRITERIA nor PLAN_H carries a dated note saying how B.1 is read; PLAN_H even restates the loose wording as its Question (13-14) and then answers it with lab runs (24-26). ROADMAP section 5's 'same cap and harness' (181) is not literally true of the lab arms either. The differences the finding lists are real and only partly disclosed in the paper: four workers and the keep rule are stated (18-22, 161-162), the exploit engine's deterministic follow-ups, its lasso/elasticnet swaps and the idea bank are not mentioned anywhere in the paper or the protocol's fairness controls. Two misreadings. (1) The reading did not originate in the paper: the protocol (15 Oct, before GOAL_CRITERIA) defines A1 as run_research.py and A3/A4 'on the task package', fairness control 1 says the package 'carries the same public data the lab's experiments receive', and ROADMAP D1 fixed 'A1 = block G's runs' before block G ran; the paper's parenthesis makes that pre-registered reading explicit. The drift is that GOAL_CRITERIA B.1 was written loosely against a protocol that never had the lab on the package, and was never reconciled. (2) 'cv_seed 0': the lab's fold seed is the run seed (lab.py:105 with run.seed=$S), so r0, r2 and r3 use fold seeds 0, 2 and 3, one per run; the package uses 0, 1, 2 in every session with a 3/3 seeds-positive gate. The asymmetry (one fold seed per lab experiment, three per package evaluation) stands. Major because the note must predate the first paid block H session for the reading to count as registered; the fix is cheap.

In the paper (117-118) replace 'is read for the lab arms as' with 'B.1 under the reading registered on <date>: ...', drop the word 'identical' from the paper's own description, and add the exploit engine and the fold-seed difference to Methods at 80-81 and 161-162. ROADMAP section 5 B.1's 'same cap and harness' should read 'same cap; the harness for the package arms'. Otherwise report B.1 as met under the protocol's definition and not under GOAL_CRITERIA's wording.
verdict.reviewer_sentence: The pre-registered criterion B.1 requires three systems on 'the identical task package', yet the authors' own system is run inside its lab (with its planner state, idea bank, exploit engine, four parallel workers and one fold seed per experiment) and only the foreign systems receive the package; the reading that reconciles this appears in the paper, not as a dated amendment of the registered criterion. findings.title: Codex's 10-second shell cut can void arm A3; the probe never exercises it
findings.claim: PLAN 258-261: 'Codex's shell tool cuts a command at 10 s unless the model itself passes timeout_ms ... no configuration key sets it'; PLAN 284-285: the probe prompt is 'Run the shell command ls and then reply with the single word ok.'; PAPER 125: 'Codex's 10-second shell timeout is disclosed per session'.
findings.problem: One python evaluate.py runs a smoke subprocess, recomputes every feature in every fold view for three fold seeds and fits the full model, budgeted up to eval_timeout_s = 600 s; program.md tells the agent only to run it. If the plan's reading of Codex is right, every evaluation longer than 10 s is cut unless the model passes a timeout, so A3 may hand back nothing and its three rows read as the parent's score while the paper reports 'three sessions'. The probe runs ls and cannot detect this; disclosing a defect per session is not a fix.

Not checkable in the repository: evaluate.py's wall time on the real bundle and the bundled Codex binary's behaviour.
findings.fix: Extend the probe to one python evaluate.py baseline run under the selected client and require its status: line in run.log before the arm is cleared; add a client-level fix for A3 (a timeout_ms instruction in the Codex config or a wrapper, not in program.md), or report A3 as 'could not run under Codex' and use the disclosed Claude Code fallback.

verdict.note: The objection stands: the arm's only priced pre-check is an `ls` round trip (run_codex.sh:87, block_h_probe.sh:41-42), which returns in milliseconds, while the arm's one action is `python evaluate.py` (program.md:116) budgeted to 600 s with two extra interpreter starts and three fold seeds (evaluate.py:50, 430-442, 461-472; export defaults 0,1,2 and k=5); nothing before the first $2.50 session shows that an evaluation's result ever reaches the model through Codex, and PLAN 217-218 / PAPER 251-252 mean three sessions that never complete an evaluation would still be reported as A3 with the parent's score, with the defect only disclosed (PLAN 258-264, PAPER 125-126). The finding misreads one detail, and so does the PLAN: the 10 s is not a cut on every build. On rust-v0.94.0 (the older bundled build the PLAN allows) the default `shell` tool kills at `timeout_ms` defaulting to 10 s and the model is told the parameter exists, so the PLAN's reading is right there. On current builds, which is what the Dockerfile installs (`@openai/codex`, 0.163.0 on 2026-10-17) and what the ChatGPT app most likely bundles, unified exec is the only shell backend, `exec_command` has no kill in its interactive lifetime (`completion_timeout = None`), the command backgrounds after a 10 s yield (max 30 s) and the model must poll it with `write_stdin` to ever see the exit code. There, nothing is 'cut short': reading 1 would count zero timed-out `command_execution` items, `run.json["shell_timeout"]` would record a wrong description, and the arm can still be voided by a model that never polls. Either way the probe exercises neither path. evaluate.py's wall time on the real bundle is not in the repository; the lab's own evaluation runs at about 5 worker-seconds on the mock control (scaling.md:14,22) and evaluate.py does strictly more, so exceeding 10 s is plausible, not shown. PR #70 changes none of this.
verdict.corrected_fix: Before any A3 session: (1) extend the Codex probe to one `python evaluate.py > run.log 2>&1` baseline in the probe's fresh package copy under the selected client, which means the probe's sandbox must be workspace-write (run_codex.sh:103 forces read-only, and evaluate.py writes runs/ and results.tsv) and the $0.05 cap may need a disclosed raise; clear the arm only when run.log holds a `status:` line and results.tsv the baseline row, and record the evaluation's wall time (results.tsv `time`, run.json) in the dated note. (2) Replace the PLAN's and run_codex.sh's single '10 s cut' description with the behaviour of the build `codex --version` reports: up to 0.94.0 a 10 s kill unless the model passes `timeout_ms`; from 0.95 on (Docker mode by construction) no kill, a 10 s yield then a background process the model must poll with `write_stdin`; make reading 1 count, per build, either timed-out `command_execution` items or `exec_command` calls on evaluate.py never followed by a poll that reached the exit code. (3) Decide a client-level lever or the fallback before the arm runs: a client-side note on the exec tool's mechanics outside program.md (whose sha256 is fixed), for example Codex's instructions file or an AGENTS.md in the package copy, disclosed as a client difference like the sandbox; or Claude Code (`A3_CLIENT=claude`), whose Bash waits eval_timeout_s + 30 s (run_autoresearch.sh:61-65, 80); or report A3 as 'could not run under Codex'.
verdict.reviewer_sentence: The only priced pre-check of arm A3 is a shell `ls` (run_codex.sh:87), while the arm's sole action is `python evaluate.py`, budgeted to 600 s (program.md:116, export_task_package.py:177); nothing before the first paid session shows that an evaluation's result ever reaches the model through Codex's exec tool, whose default is a 10 s kill on builds up to 0.94.0 and, on the current build the Dockerfile installs, a 10 s yield to a background process the model must poll. Disclosing the behaviour per session (PLAN 258-264) does not make three parent-score rows an A3 result; run one baseline evaluation under the selected client in the probe, gate the arm on its status line, and describe the client's behaviour by build.

findings.title: The foreign arms' software is unpinned and unrecorded, so no arm can be rerun
findings.claim: PAPER 124-125: 'It runs through the Codex CLI ... run.json["client"] records which ran'; PLAN 249-251: 'codex found at /Applications/ChatGPT.app/.../codex ... version unknown'; PLAN 333: 'the image installs the current npm Codex build (@openai/codex 0.163.0 on 2026-10-17)'.
findings.problem: The Dockerfile installs @anthropic-ai/claude-code, @openai/codex and biomni without versions, so the image depends on its build day; account mode uses a different Codex (the ChatGPT app's bundle, 0.160.0) in a hand-built venv; run.json records the client name but no version, no Biomni version is recorded anywhere, and check_tools.sh prints codex --version for the Mac's binary, not the image's. The image also copies tools/baselines at build time while collect_handback runs from $C on the host, and h_checks only tests that the image exists, so after a later merge the agent runs old runners while the host runs new ones. The two isolation modes would run different software under one arm label.
findings.evidence: docs/mac/block_h/Dockerfile:12-14 npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code @openai/codex / pip install --no-cache-dir $PKG_REQS biomni langchain langgraph==0.3.18 openai; tools/baselines/run_codex.sh:32 'version unknown', :42; HANDOFF.md:83 'codex 0.160.0 present'; grep -i version tools/baselines/run_biomni.py finds no version record; docs/mac/block_h/check_tools.sh:10, :28; block_h_common.sh:34.
findings.fix: Pin the three packages to exact versions in the Dockerfile and the account venv; have the runners write codex --version, biomni.__version__ and the proxy's commit into run.json; have check_tools.sh print the image's versions and sha256sum of /lab/tools/baselines/* beside the host's, posted on #41; put the versions in the arms table; forbid mixing isolation modes within an arm.

verdict.note: Confirmed in every mechanical particular: the Dockerfile pins none of the three agent packages (nor langchain or openai), so the image's contents depend on its build day and PLAN:333's `0.163.0` is a snapshot the file does not enforce; block_h_a3.sh:23 and block_h_common.sh:13 make Docker mode run the image's npm codex and account mode the ChatGPT-bundled binary; run_codex.sh writes `client` and `codex_bin` but no version, run_biomni.py writes `python` but no biomni version, and collect_handback.py's manifest summary (lines 118-119) drops even `client`; check_tools.sh:10 prints the host binary's version and :28 plus block_h_common.sh:34 only test that the image exists; the image bakes `/lab/tools/baselines` at build time (Dockerfile:15, TOOLS at common.sh:128) while ledger_proxy.py and collect_handback.py run from `$C` on the host (common.sh:104, :192), and nothing compares the two, so a later merge (PR #70 itself changes run_biomni.py's run.json) can leave the container on older runners than the host. The arms table pins the lab arms to commit `baa7dfd` but gives A3/A4 no client or Biomni version, and the paper's Data and code paragraph lists no versions or image digest. Two details the finding gets wrong: the `codex 0.160.0 present` line is HANDOFF.md:47 (and 161), not :83; and the plan already says the isolation answer `is written once into block_h/isolation.txt` (PLAN:105) and states the persisting-venv weakness (PLAN:103-104), so 'forbid mixing isolation modes within an arm' is an enforcement gap in h_checks, not a missing rule. The plan's own `version unknown` (PLAN:252, run_codex.sh:32) is also stale: Astra's 17:53 UTC check reported 0.160.0 and no dated note has taken it up. Severity major rather than reject: the block has not run, the LLM is the same across arms, the client is disclosed, and in Docker mode the installed versions remain readable from the built-once image after the fact; but without recorded versions an A3/A4 session cannot be attributed to a specific Codex or Biomni build (the ChatGPT app auto-updates its bundle), which fails AGENTS.md's 'reproducible from a run directory' standard and would draw a mandatory revision request from any venue.
verdict.corrected_fix: Before the probe: (1) pin `@openai/codex`, `@anthropic-ai/claude-code`, `biomni`, `langchain` and `openai` to exact versions in the Dockerfile (langgraph already is), build with `--label genemila.commit=$(git -C $C rev-parse HEAD)`, and require the same pins in the account venv line of check_tools.sh:40; (2) have run_codex.sh write `codex_version` (`"$CODEX_BIN" --version`) and run_biomni.py write `biomni_version`, `langchain_version`, `langgraph_version`, `openai_version` (`importlib.metadata.version`) into run.json, and extend collect_handback.py:118-119's field list with `client`, `codex_bin` and the version fields so the hand-back manifest carries them; (3) in check_tools.sh, when the daemon runs, print the image's versions (`docker run --rm genemila-h sh -c 'codex --version; claude --version; python -c "import importlib.metadata as m; print(m.version(\"biomni\"))"'`), its `genemila.commit` label, and `sha256sum /lab/tools/baselines/*` beside `shasum -a 256 $C/tools/baselines/*`, all posted on #41; in h_checks (block_h_common.sh:34) refuse Docker mode when the image's baselines hashes differ from `$C`'s, or replace the baked copy with a read-only mount of `$C/tools/baselines` so both sides always run the same files (the Dockerfile's reason for copying, never copying genemila/ or configs/, is kept by mounting only that directory); (4) record 0.160.0 (HANDOFF.md:47) in a dated PLAN note replacing `version unknown` at PLAN:252 and run_codex.sh:32, and give rows A3 and A4 of both arms tables (PLAN:27-28, PAPER:259-260) the client and Biomni versions as A1/A2 carry `baa7dfd`; (5) rather than a new rule, enforce the plan's existing 'written once': have the probe's `.passed` record the mode and h_checks refuse an arm session whose `isolation.txt` differs from it.
verdict.reviewer_sentence: The foreign arms' software is neither pinned nor recorded: the Dockerfile installs @openai/codex, @anthropic-ai/claude-code and biomni at whatever version npm and pip serve on the build day, account mode runs a different Codex (the ChatGPT app's bundle, reported as 0.160.0 in HANDOFF.md but still 'version unknown' in the plan), run.json names the client but no version for either A3 or A4, and the arms tables give A3 and A4 no version where A1 and A2 carry commit baa7dfd. Add exact pins and per-session version records (and a check that the image's baked tools/baselines match the host clone's, since collect_handback.py and the proxy run from the host) before the first paid session; as written, an A3 or A4 session cannot be attributed to a specific agent build or rerun on the same software.

findings.title: The probe's two-200-rows-and-no-400 rule is not enforced; .passed needs one call
findings.claim: codex is cleared for A3 only when h_probe_codex.jsonl holds at least two status-200 rows and no 400; otherwise the chat route is unfit for the arm and one of item 2's two paths is taken.
findings.problem: No script applies the rule. session_after writes h_probe.passed whenever one status-200 row exists with the wanted model and the runner exited 0; a 400 from upstream is logged as a priced=false row and relayed, never a stop; block_h_probe.sh only prints a reminder; block_h_a3.sh checks nothing but the marker's existence. A probe with one 200 row and a 400 on the tool round trip passes, and A3 can run on a route the plan calls unfit.
findings.evidence: docs/mac/block_h/block_h_probe.sh:52-53 session_after "$name" probe deepseek-v4-pro 0.10 || exit 3 then an echo reminder; block_h_common.sh:216 ("no call reached the proxy", not calls) is the only count check; :224 touch "$H/$name.passed"; block_h_a3.sh:15 [ -e "$H/h_probe.passed" ] || no ...; tools/baselines/ledger_proxy.py:369-372 if resp.status != 200 or kind == "free": p.log(..., priced=False); return self._relay(...).
findings.fix: In session_after for the probe require at least two status-200 rows in h_probe_codex.jsonl and no 400 row before touching the marker (or a separate h_probe_codex.passed that block_h_a3.sh requires); until then say in PLAN and PAPER that the rule is read by hand.

[ -e "$H/$n.passed" ] && { ...; continue; }; bash "$H/block_h_$arm.sh" "$s" || ...` with no pause for a reading. tools/baselines/ledger_proxy.py:369-372 `if resp.status != 200 or kind == "free": p.log(route=path, model_requested=requested, status=resp.status, latency_s=latency, stream=False, priced=False); return self._relay(resp.status, ctype, data)` (a 400 is logged and relayed, the proxy keeps serving). tools/baselines/run_codex.sh:231 `if [ "$CODE" = 124 ]; then ENDED_BY="timeout"; elif [ "$CODE" = 0 ]; then ENDED_BY="solution"; fi`; :255 `[ "$ENDED_BY" = "timeout" ] || [ "$ENDED_BY" = "solution" ]` (the runner exits 0 when the watchdog ends the retries, so the exit code does not catch item 7 either). verdict.note: Confirmed in the files. The rule at PLAN 328-330 and PAPER 125 lives in a comment (probe.sh:22-34) and a printed reminder (probe.sh:53); session_after pools both probe logs and passes on any one status-200 row with model_served deepseek-v4-pro (Biomni's row suffices even when Codex made no priced call), counts other statuses without acting on them, and touches h_probe.passed; a 400 is an unpriced relayed row in the proxy; and in the plan's own item-7 scenario (retries until the clock) run_codex.sh exits 0 on the watchdog's timeout, so the runner exit code does not stop the probe either. block_h_a3.sh needs only h_probe.passed and block_h_chain.sh runs the probe, A4 and A3 back to back with no human gate, so the dated-note reading PLAN 160-164 and 301 ask for never has to happen before A3 r0 spends its $2.50 on a route the plan calls unfit.
