verdict.corrected_fix: Enforce the rule where the marker is written: in session_after when arm is probe and A3_CLIENT is codex (or in block_h_probe.sh between the check and the marker), read $H/proxy/h_probe_codex.jsonl alone and require at least two rows with status 200 and model_served deepseek-v4-pro and no row with status 400 (count 404 and 502 there too, since both mean a route failure); on failure append the cause to block_h_stopped.txt and return 3 so h_probe.passed is never touched. Keep block_h_a3.sh:15 as the only gate once the marker carries the rule, or write a separate h_probe_codex.passed and require it there. Add one test beside tests/test_block_h_scripts.py with a fixture log of one 200 and one 400. Until that lands, amend PLAN step 6 and PAPER 125 in a dated note to say the two-200-no-400 rule is read by hand from h_probe_codex.jsonl and that the chain must not be started past the probe (or must be stopped after it) until that reading is in the plan.
verdict.reviewer_sentence: The protocol says Codex is cleared for A3 only when the probe's log holds two status-200 rows and no 400 (PLAN 328-330, PAPER 125), but no script applies it: session_after passes the probe on any single priced call with the wanted served model (block_h_common.sh:216), the proxy logs and relays a 400 without halting (ledger_proxy.py:369-372), the runner exits 0 when the watchdog ends the retries (run_codex.sh:255), block_h_a3.sh:15 needs only h_probe.passed, and the detached chain runs A3 after A4 with no reading in between, so the first A3 session can spend its cap on a route the plan itself calls unfit.

findings.title: C2 was translated after the lab's Adamson results; two plugins are response-transfer features
findings.claim: PAPER 136-138: 'C2, CellForge's ideas translated by us: four plugins written by hand from CellForge's public code and model cards ... Nothing in them is CellForge's output'.
findings.problem: The four plugins were committed on 16 October, after the Adamson scaling results (the transfer family carrying nearly all the gain) and B2 were known to the author. Which of CellForge's ideas to translate, and how, was a free choice made with that knowledge, and two of the four (cf_pathway_transfer, cf_latent_offset) are leave-one-out transfers of training responses between related perturbations, the known-good family. Neither the C2 README nor the paper states when the set was written or what its author had seen.

Nearly all of it is transfer of the measured responses of training knockdowns whose targets share gene sets or protein-interaction neighbours with the new target." README.md:477-478 "the hand-written transfer feature was designed after 26 sealed results had been read" and :488-490 "a control given one hand-written transfer feature, written after the agent runs had shown what works". docs/FEATURE_COMPARISON_PROTOCOL.md:86-88 (15 Oct) "We write 3–4 plugins from CellForge's design ideas: gene-network propagation, pathway membership, perturbation-embedding similarity, and a pair-interaction term". verdict.note: Every factual element checks out and the record is stronger than the finding states. The C2 set was committed at 01:51 UTC on 16 October by the #41 session, 24 minutes after that same session committed README.md:104-105 saying the agents' whole gain was "transfer of the measured responses of training knockdowns whose targets share gene sets or protein-interaction neighbours"; cf_pathway_transfer (leave-one-out mean of training changes of perturbations sharing gene sets) and cf_latent_offset (leave-one-out transfer of training codes through PPI neighbours) are those two mechanisms, one each. The scaling report (4-5 Oct), the hand-written transfer control (5 Oct), the transfer ceilings (11 Oct) and B1/B2 (11-12 Oct) all predate it. The protocol's own 15 October wording was "pathway membership" and "perturbation-embedding similarity"; the implementation turned both into train_delta-reading transfers, which is the free translation choice the finding describes. Neither the C2 README's Provenance section (CellForge file:line citations only), PAPER 136-138, Table 1 (262) nor the paper's own "three changes belong in the paper" disclosure paragraph (228-241) says when C2 was written or what its author had seen, and the PLAN's dated notes never mention C2. The repository already applies the disclosure the finding asks for to the analogous object (README 477-478, 488-490: the hand-written transfer feature "written after the agent runs had shown what works"), so the omission for C2 is an inconsistency with the project's own standard, not a new demand. Mitigations that keep this from "reject": the paper does say C2 is hand-written with no session, no arm claim is made from the development tier, and the fix is an additive disclosure that invalidates no number. Small precision points the finding gets slightly off: three of the four plugins read train_delta (cf_pair_interaction too), so the accurate phrasing is "two of the three Adamson-scoreable rows are related-perturbation transfers"; and the PAPER already states the transfer-family result at 47-49, so the paper's gap is specifically the failure to connect C2 to it. PR #70 does not touch this.

findings.title: No pre-registered consequence for a detected network call in account mode
findings.claim: PLAN 101-103: 'The filesystem isolation holds ...; the network one does not, so the proxy log and the transcript scan are the check, and the paper says so.'; PLAN 266: 'reading 4 reads both transcripts for network attempts'.
findings.problem: In account mode Biomni runs agent code with exec() and the account's full network; the scan flags transcript lines naming http, requests, curl or socket but rejects nothing, and the stop rules list credentials, out-of-package writes and the cap, not a network call. The protocol says a system that brings its own knowledge is a separate arm, so a Biomni session that queried UniProt or PubMed cannot stay in the A4 mean; the plan must say what happens before it can happen.
findings.evidence: tools/baselines/collect_handback.py:15-16 'A flagged transcript is not rejected here; the operator reads the lines.', :43 NETWORK = re.compile(r"https?://|\brequests\b|..."); tools/baselines/run_biomni.py:26-28 'Biomni executes the agent's code with exec() ... with the user's rights and whatever network the process has.'; tools/baselines/run_codex.sh:140-141 [sandbox_workspace_write] network_access = false; docs/PLAN_H_COMPARISON.md:192-198 (stop rules); docs/FEATURE_COMPARISON_PROTOCOL.md:106-108.
findings.fix: Add to the stop rules and reading 4 before any session: a session whose transcript, scratch files or proxy log show a request to any host other than the proxy is its own arm ('brought outside knowledge'), is excluded from its arm's mean and stops the chain for a dated note; in Docker mode state that the control holds by construction.

verdict.evidence_checked: docs/PLAN_H_COMPARISON.md:101-103 "The filesystem isolation holds (the account cannot read Andres's home); the network one does not, so the proxy log and the transcript scan are the check, and the paper says so."; :192-198 "**Stop rules** (the session becomes its own arm, the chain stops, the cause goes in a dated note): a session's ledger delta over $2.50 or the cap reached; a runner error; a transcript, output, work copy, session log or proxy file containing a credential pattern ...; an agent that touched anything outside its package copy (Docker: impossible by construction; account mode: `find -ls` of the account's home compared before and after ...); `planner.mixed` or a non-empty `run.external_knowledge` in an A2 run." (no network item); :227-233 reading 4 lists sources read, attempts, keeps, rejections and val1 reads only, no network flags; :264-267 "in account mode Codex's Seatbelt sandbox (`network_access = false`) blocks the agent's shell commands from the network, which `program.md` forbids anyway and Claude Code's Bash is only told ... reading 4 reads both transcripts for network attempts; in Docker mode both arms are equal (the internal network is the isolation)."; :318-323 item 6 covers Codex's own start-up requests and asks for a decision on the runner's 404 rule only. Every dated note through 2026-10-17 22:00 UTC (PR #70's note included, read from origin/claude/block-h-script-gaps) adds no consequence for a detected network call. docs/PAPER_COMPARISON.md:146-148 "Isolation of the foreign arms: only the package folder is mounted and only the proxy is reachable, in Docker or in a second macOS account checked by the proxy log and the transcript scan; without either, the foreign arms wait". docs/FEATURE_COMPARISON_PROTOCOL.md:106-108 "A system that brings its own knowledge (for example Biomni's data lake) is a separate arm."; :122-124 "Network only to the LLM endpoint. Without a container this control does not hold, and the arm must wait." tools/baselines/collect_handback.py:15-16 "A flagged transcript is not rejected here; the operator reads the lines."; :43 `NETWORK = re.compile(r"https?://|\brequests\b|\burllib\b|\bsocket\b|\bcurl\b|\bwget\b")`; :124 flags stored in manifest.json only. tools/baselines/run_biomni.py:26-31 "Biomni executes the agent's code with exec() inside its own process ..., with the user's rights and whatever network the process has. So the package must be the only writable place the child can reach and the proxy its only network route: the Mac script runs it in Docker or under a second user account (ROADMAP D6). This tool only refuses what it can see itself". tools/baselines/run_codex.sh:140-141 `[sandbox_workspace_write]` / `network_access = false`; :47-48 comment that only Codex's shell commands are blocked in account mode. docs/mac/block_h/block_h_common.sh:168-224 session_after(): stops on runner rc (171), ledger delta (173-175), credential scan (176-181), home diff in account mode (187-190); the val1 scan (184-186) is recorded only; grep finds no read of transcript_flags or any network scan in any block_h script, on cfa8034 or on PR #70's branch. docs/mac/block_h/check_tools.sh:29-35 the Docker egress test ("api.deepseek.com ... unreachable: good"), so Docker mode holds by construction; account mode has no counterpart.
verdict.note: Confirmed on every point. In account mode nothing restricts the agent's network (PLAN 101-103 says so), the A4 agent runs code with exec() in-process with the account's full network (run_biomni.py:26-28), and the only check is collect_handback's six-token regex over stdout/stderr, which flags and never rejects; the session script never even reads those flags, and the pre-registered stop rules (PLAN 192-198, block_h_common.sh session_after) name the cap, runner errors, credentials, out-of-package writes and A2's planner, not a network call. Protocol control 1 makes a system that brings its own knowledge a separate arm and control 7 says the arm must wait without a container; the plan relaxes control 7 for account mode without saying what a detected call does, so a Biomni session that queried an external database could stay in the A4 mean on a post-hoc judgement, which the project's own rules forbid. Two further points the finding does not make: the proxy log cannot show a request that never went to the proxy, so "the proxy log and the transcript scan are the check" (PLAN 102) is half wrong for this control; and the paper's sentence at 146-148 ("only the proxy is reachable ... in a second macOS account") overstates account mode. The exposure is mostly A4 (and a Claude Code fallback's Bash), since Codex's Seatbelt sandbox blocks its shell commands' network in account mode. Severity major rather than reject: the gap is a missing pre-registered consequence; no reading is invalid until a flagged session is kept in a mean, and the fix is a few lines before the first paid session.
verdict.corrected_fix: Before any session, in PLAN (stop rules and reading 4) and in session_after: after collect_handback, read transcript_flags from the hand-back manifest; because the regex also matches benign text (a URL in a comment, an import that never ran, Biomni's tool descriptions), a flag is not itself the verdict: the operator reads the flagged lines before the next session starts and records the decision in a dated note under a rule fixed now: evidence that a request to any host other than the proxy was executed (a fetched URL, a requests/urllib/socket/curl/wget call that ran, a scratch file holding downloaded content) makes the session its own arm ("brought outside knowledge", protocol control 1), excluded from its arm's mean and from the frozen batch, and stops the chain until the note is written; a mention that did not run is recorded and changes nothing. State that in Docker mode the control holds by construction (check_tools.sh's egress test), so a flagged attempt there is a failed attempt, recorded only. Fix PLAN 102 to say the transcript scan (not the proxy log) is the check for this, make reading 4's text match line 266 (it does not mention network now), and correct PAPER 146-148 to say that in account mode only the filesystem isolation holds and the network is checked, not blocked.
verdict.reviewer_sentence: In the second-account isolation mode the plan concedes that nothing blocks the agent's network and relies on a transcript scan that flags but rejects nothing, yet its pre-registered stop rules name the cap, credentials and out-of-package writes and never a network call, so a Biomni session that fetched outside data could remain in the A4 mean against the protocol's own control 1; the paper's "only the proxy is reachable ... in a second macOS account" overstates what that mode guarantees. State, before the first session, what a detected request to any host other than the proxy does to the session, and that the proxy log cannot show such a request at all.

findings.title: Lab arms may drop or retune parent columns; the lab system row is built by a different recipe than the package's
findings.claim: PAPER 152-153: 'tools/feature_compare.py scores every arm alike: one system row (parent plus all the arm's kept features) and one add-one row per feature ... with the same ridge, alpha grid, fold seeds and metrics'; protocol 109: 'Same parent. P0 for every arm ... The parent cannot be removed.'
findings.problem: Nothing in the lab stops a run from removing a built-in: the exploit engine's ablation list includes the built-ins, the planner's ablate action removes any feature from the base set, and validate_spec has no built-in rule. For a --source-run the set row rebuilds the run's selected model: parent features the run dropped are absent, retuned ones are recomputed with the run's params, and only the selected model's own features enter; for a --source it is parent plus every passing file with class-default params. The package evaluator always includes every parent feature. So a lab run that gained from dropping is_target or control_mean gets a system row no package arm could produce, and the fair-test paragraph does not disclose the two recipes.
findings.evidence: genemila/exploit.py:107-111 spec(f"Drop {f} from the best model" over built-ins too; genemila/planner.py:254-255 remove = set(h.get("remove_features") or []) / fs = [f for f in base_set if f not in remove] + add; genemila/spec.py:114-160 (validate_spec, no built-in protection); tools/feature_compare.py:1148-1152 retuned, kept, "dropped_parent": [f for f in p_feats if f not in params]; :1230-1231 own = live + retuned / set_row["model"] = kept + own; :962-964 'set row: the run's selected model with its recorded params'; tools/task_package/evaluate.py:466 feats = list(manifest["parent_features"]) + sorted(current).
findings.fix: Pre-register before the chain: a lab run's system row is scored as P0 plus the run's own features (a flag for --source-run that restores dropped parent columns), with the run's own model reported beside it; or keep the tool and print dropped_parent in Table 1 with the sentence 'for a package arm, the parent plus every kept feature with class-default params; for a lab arm, the run's selected model, which may drop or retune parent features'.

verdict.reviewer_sentence: The 'same parent' control does not hold for the lab arms: all six block G runs that form A1 and A1-ablation selected models without control_mean, the comparison tool rebuilds a lab system row from the run's selected model while a package arm's row always carries every parent column, and the paper's fair-test paragraph describes only the package recipe; the authors should pre-register one system-row recipe for every arm, or print the dropped parent columns in Table 1 and disclose the two recipes.

findings.title: 'The difference does not reach the table' is false: selection rules decide each hand-back and the correction ignores search size
findings.claim: PAPER 161-162: 'Two selection rules, one scoring. The lab keeps every completed experiment and picks the highest combined score; the package keeps a change only under the noise keep rule ... The tool rescores every hand-back from its parent, so the difference does not reach the table.'
findings.problem: Rescoring on new fold seeds removes the selection scores, not the selection. For a lab run the tool's candidates are the features of the single argmax experiment over tens of experiments on seen labels; for a package arm they are the files that passed gain > max(2 SE, 0.002), wins on more than half and positive under every seed, a bar a serial agent with a dozen evaluations in 20 minutes rarely clears, so its row is likely the parent's score. Which features sit in each system row and how many add-one rows form each family follow from the rule, and the step-down family is per hand-back while the gain of each row was already maximised by a search whose size differs by arm (four parallel workers against a Codex loop with a 10-second cut), so the winner's-curse inflation and the chance of a floor p differ by arm in a way p_fwer does not touch. The plan records attempt counts but never uses them; protocol item 7 (strict rule as an ablation) was never decided.

LIMIT 1; tools/task_package/evaluate.py:23-26 'hundreds of attempts are chosen on the same folds of the same labels, so the kept state's score is optimistic', :251 keep = gain > max(2 * se_adj, MIN_GAIN) and wins > len(d) / 2 and all(g > 0 for g in seed_gains); tools/task_package/program.md:97-101; tools/baselines/collect_handback.py:58-61; docs/FEATURE_COMPARISON_PROTOCOL.md:386; PLAN 222.
findings.fix: Replace the last clause with 'the tool rescores every hand-back on new fold seeds, so no selection score reaches the table; the selection rules still decide which features each hand-back holds, and the development p-values are conditional on each system's search and not comparable across arms with different attempt counts'; report each hand-back's size and attempts beside the verdict count in Table 1; pre-register one of: a second candidate list from each package session's best attempt set, the noise rule applied to the lab's in-run gains, or the strict keep rule as the A3 ablation.

(grep 'strict' in PLAN_H: no hit except 'stricter' about the sandbox at :266, so undecided); :402-404 'today best() is the plain highest selection score ... "More than fold noise" is a proposal, not the current rule'. docs/results/adamson_cf_g_stage1/feature_compare.json: f_r0_selected EXP_0777 selected 23 features, 20 ok add-one rows; f_r2_selected EXP_0730 22 / 20; f_r3_selected EXP_0796 22 / 20.
verdict.note: The objection stands: rescoring removes the selection scores, not the selection, so 'the difference does not reach the table' overstates. The code confirms the asymmetry and it is larger than the finding says: the lab's parent for every new experiment is the current best and max_new_features is 1, so the selected model is a lineage that added a feature whenever an experiment beat the best on the seen tiers by any amount (block G's selected Adamson models hold 22 to 23 features, 20 add-one rows per session), while a package arm keeps a file only under the noise rule. The lab therefore runs under a rule as loose as the 'strict' rule it does not give the foreign arms, and the system rows and families differ in size by rule. What the finding misreads: the paper already says every development verdict screens and proves nothing (156-157) and that the lab's keep rule shapes the foreign arms (357); Table 1 already has a 'features kept' column, and PLAN readings 2 and 4 already report attempts (median evaluate.py runs, attempts/keeps/rejections), so 'records attempt counts but never uses them' is true only of a correction, which the design never claimed; 'its row is likely the parent's score' is speculation the plan already handles (217-218). Protocol 7.7 (strict-rule ablation) is indeed undecided and absent from PLAN_H. Not fixed in PR #70 (its diff adds only the 22:00 note on the probe reset and the rate flag).
verdict.corrected_fix: PAPER 161-162: replace the last clause with 'the tool rescores every hand-back on new fold seeds, so no selection score reaches the table; the selection rules still decide what each hand-back holds: the lab's lineage adds a feature whenever an experiment beats the current best on the seen tiers (any positive combined gain; block G's selected Adamson models hold 22 to 23 features), the package keeps one only under the noise rule, so the system rows and the add-one families differ in size by rule and the development verdicts screen searches of different size.' Add the per-session attempt count (reading 2's median evaluate.py runs; summary.json experiment counts for the lab) to Table 1's template beside 'with a verdict'. Decide protocol 7.7 before the chain and record it in a dated PLAN_H note: either the strict keep rule as an A3 ablation (paid, so before the first session), or, free and pre-registered now, a second candidate list per lab session made by applying the package's noise rule to the run's own in-run gains (read_run already returns delta_from_parent per feature), scored as a further --source in reading 1. No tool change needed.
verdict.reviewer_sentence: 'The difference does not reach the table' is not right: rescoring removes the selection scores, not the selection. The lab's hand-back is an argmax lineage that adds a feature on any gain over the current best on the seen tiers (22 to 23 features per block G session), while the package arms keep a file only when its gain clears max(2 SE, 0.002) on every seed; the system rows and add-one families therefore differ in size and composition by rule, and the paper should state this and pre-register either the strict-rule ablation left open in the protocol or a noise-rule candidate list for the lab sessions.

findings.title: Proportionality check covers one parent column; sums of parent columns evade both nulls
findings.claim: A candidate that is, within every perturbation's row, a per-perturbation scalar times one parent column cannot fail that null ...; such a row is marked proportional ... It must pass both.
findings.problem: The degeneracy the block F withdrawal describes holds for any candidate whose row is a per-perturbation reweighting of the span of the parent columns (c_i·mean_response + d_i·control_mean, or a parent column plus a per-perturbation constant): permuting it across genes scrambles factors the model already holds, so the gene null is again a spike at zero, yet proportional_to_parent tests one column q at a time and such a row is marked not proportional and gets no perturbation null. On Adamson the parent has three columns, so an agent feature of that shape would pass at the floor as block F's CpG row did.
findings.evidence: tools/feature_compare.py:579-589 for q in range(parent_full.shape[2]): Q = parent_full[:, :, q] ... if np.all(np.linalg.norm(x - cj[:, None] * Q, axis=1) <= rtol * nx): ... break / else: return None; :34-42 docstring limits the second null to 'a per-perturbation scalar times one parent column'; tests/test_feature_compare.py:158-189 single-column proportionality only.
findings.fix: Generalise the detector to a per-row least-squares fit on all parent columns plus a per-row constant, route every such row to the perturbation null, add a guard flagging any add-one row whose gene-null sd is below a stated fraction of the typical null sd as 'null degenerate', and document the rule in PAPER 163-166.

verdict.evidence_checked: tools/feature_compare.py:565-590 proportional_to_parent: 'for j in range(k): x = cand[:, :, j] ... for q in range(parent_full.shape[2]): Q = parent_full[:, :, q] ... cj[qq > 0] = einsum(x, Q)/qq ... if np.all(np.linalg.norm(x - cj[:, None] * Q, axis=1) <= rtol * nx): idx.append(q); break / else: return None' (one parent column per candidate column, no constant, no combination). :34-42 docstring 'A candidate that is, within every perturbation's row, a per-perturbation scalar times one parent column ... gets a second null'. :876-885 null_row: null_pert only 'if prop and row["kind"] == "add_one"'. :818-836 pert_null 'rebuilds the candidate as the permuted scalar times the parent column'. :1192-1198 the check and proportional_in_folds. tests/test_feature_compare.py:158-189: single column only; :181 'cand * rng.normal(size=(1, 20, 1))' asserted not proportional; :187-189 'several columns: every one must fit, each with its own parent column'. docs/PAPER_COMPARISON.md:163-166 'a per-perturbation scalar times one parent column ... It must pass both'. docs/FEATURE_COMPARISON_PROTOCOL.md:319-330 same rule. docs/ROADMAP.md:48-51 D2(a) 'proportional to a parent column'. genemila/features/registry.py:12 'BUILTIN_FEATURES = ["control_mean", "mean_response", "is_target"]'; docs/results/adamson_cf_g_stage2/feature_compare.json parent n_columns 3. Same report, computed by me: 221 ok add-one rows, 18 proportional, none passing; gene-null sd over all rows median 2.4e-5, max 3.4e-4; the 18 proportional rows' gene-null sd 1.2e-5 to 1.7e-4; 37 non-proportional rows with gene-null sd 0.0 and observed gain about 1e-7 (p = 1: features constant across genes within a perturbation, which the gene permutation leaves unchanged).
verdict.note: Confirmed in the code: the detector fits one parent column at a time with no constant, so a candidate that is, per perturbation row, a combination of parent columns (c_i*mean_response + d_i*control_mean), a parent column plus a per-perturbation constant, or, the commonest agent pattern, a proportional feature re-centred or z-scored within each row (x_i = (c_i Q_i - m_i)/s_i = c_i' Q_i + d_i' 1) returns None, is marked proportional=false and gets the gene null only. For that class the gene permutation scrambles the parent part and keeps the constant, so the null replicates are as uninformative as in block F's case and the right question (do the per-perturbation coefficients carry information) is never asked. Adamson's parent has three columns, so the class is easy to produce. Two details the finding gets wrong: (1) the proposed 'null degenerate' guard on the gene-null sd would not work: in the block G Adamson report the proportional rows' gene-null sd (1.2e-5 to 1.7e-4) overlaps the non-proportional rows' (median 2.4e-5), and the rows with sd near 0 are harmless per-perturbation constants with p = 1; (2) 'would pass at the floor as block F's CpG row did' overstates: a floor p on the gene null is not a pass, the row must also clear max(2 SE_adj, 0.002), wins, M2, mse_top and every report, and the CpG row itself now fails the minimum effect. No false pass has occurred yet (block G: none of 221 passes). Not fixed in PR #70.
verdict.corrected_fix: Generalise proportional_to_parent to a per-row least-squares fit of each candidate column on all parent columns plus a per-row constant (residual at most PROP_RTOL times the row norm, in the full view and in every fold view as now), store the per-row coefficient vector, extend pert_parts and NullEngine.score_pert so the perturbation null rebuilds the candidate as the permuted coefficient vectors times the parent columns plus the constant, route every such row to the perturbation null, and add tests for a two-column combination and for a per-row z-scored proportional feature. Rewrite the docstring (lines 34-42), PAPER 163-166 and protocol 319-330 to 'within the per-perturbation span of the parent columns and a constant'. Do not add the sd-ratio guard: the Adamson block G report shows it would flag per-perturbation constants (sd 0, p = 1) and miss the proportional rows. Re-read block G's stage 2 (free) with the new detector before block H's reading 1 so both readings use one rule, and record the change as a dated note.
verdict.reviewer_sentence: The perturbation null is applied only to a candidate that is a per-perturbation scalar times a single parent column (proportional_to_parent tests one column at a time with no constant). A candidate in the per-perturbation span of the parent columns, or a per-row re-centred or z-scored proportional feature, is marked not proportional and faces the gene null alone, which for that class asks a question the model has already answered; with three parent columns on Adamson this class is easy for an agent to produce, so the detector must cover the span plus a constant before block H is read.

findings.title: Lab-arm families in reading 1 differ from the block G reading the paper cites
findings.claim: A max-gain step-down permutation test (Westfall and Young) over one source's add-one rows ... --source-run A1_r0=<MAIN>/runs/adamson_cf_g1_ds_w4_r0 --source-run A1_r2=... --source-run A1_r3=...
findings.problem: A 'source' is one command-line entry, so reading 1 makes three families per arm, one per session, and for a --source-run the add-one rows are only the selected model's features. The block G reading of the same runs, which the paper reports as 'none passes (Adamson 210 unique predictions)', used every plugin in each run's feature_store as --source directories and pooled the three runs into one family of 210 with block_f_readings.py pool. The same feature can carry two verdicts (a family of 5 against 210), the paper never says which family Table 2 uses, and the top-3 selection across an arm's three families for the frozen batch is a further uncorrected maximum.
findings.evidence: tools/feature_compare.py:1059-1061 for name, _ in sources: for kind in ("add_one", "set"): fam = [r for r in rows if r["source"] == name ...]; :1146; :962-964; docs/results/adamson_cf_g_stage1.command.txt --source f_r0=.../adamson_cf_g_plugins/r0 --source f_r2=... --source f_r3=... --source-run f_r0_selected=...; docs/results/adamson_cf_g_pooled_holm/pooled_holm.json family 210, stage1_rows 221, tested 221, duplicates 11; docs/PLAN_G_CLEAN_ARM.md:185-199.
findings.fix: State in PLAN reading 1 and PAPER 'The fair test' that the family is per session (or add the pool step over an arm's three sessions as block G did) and which rows enter it (selected-model features or every kept plugin); use the same definition for A1 as the cited block G reading, or report both.

verdict.note: The core stands and is verified: reading 1 makes one family per session (three per arm) whose members are the selected model's features at the run's recorded params, whereas the block G reading the paper cites pooled every table-reading plugin of the same three runs, at class defaults, into one family of 210, and the _selected rows scored in stage 1 were not part of that pooled family. A feature in a selected model is then judged in a family of about 20 in Table 2 and was judged in a family of 210 in the block G text; the smaller family gives the smaller step-down p, so the two verdicts can disagree, and neither PAPER nor PLAN says the family differs. Details the finding misreads: the G1 selected models hold 20 add-one features per session, not 5; Table 2 does name its source file (reading 1's), what is missing is the family rule in words; and the top-3-per-arm frozen batch is the pre-registered screening step whose multiplicity the fresh test's Holm over every batch comparison is designed to absorb (PAPER 210-211, protocol 6.2-6.4), not an uncorrected claim. Not fixed in PR #70.
verdict.corrected_fix: In PLAN reading 1 and PAPER 'The fair test' and Table 2, state the family rule: one family per --source or --source-run entry, i.e. per session; for a lab session the members are the selected model's features the parent lacks at the run's recorded params, for a package session the kept files; so the A1 verdicts of Table 2 come from three families of about 20, while the block G statement pools 210 table-reading plugins at class defaults. Then either add a pre-registered pool step per arm (block_f_readings.py pool over an arm's three sessions, or a --family option in the tool) as a second reading, or write a reconciliation rule now: a feature with a verdict in reading 1 that failed in the pooled 210-family is reported with both p's and the family sizes. Change the docstring's 'one family per system' to 'one family per source entry (a session)'. Leave the frozen-batch top-3 as it is and say in the paper that the fresh test's Holm covers that selection.
verdict.reviewer_sentence: Table 2's A1 verdicts come from reading 1, where each session is its own family of the selected model's about 20 features at the runs' tuned parameters, whereas the 'none of 210 passes' statement pools every table-reading plugin of the same three runs at class defaults; the paper does not say the two readings define different families, and a feature could pass in one and fail in the other. State the family rule for Table 2 and reconcile it with the block G reading before any block H score is read.

findings.title: The 'under 30 targets, not powered' floor has no stated detectable effect
findings.claim: under 30 such targets in R2, re-checked after the R1 exclusion, the arm criteria are reported as not powered.
findings.problem: Thirty is given as the powered threshold without the quantity power is about. From the development set rows the paired SE of a system over P0 is 0.003 to 0.014 on 50 perturbations, so about 0.004 to 0.018 on 30; with the Holm family the bar is three or more such SEs (0.01 to 0.05), while the arms' development gains over P0 are 0.007 (G1) to 0.042 (G0). A referee needs the minimal detectable gain at the floor and its basis before accepting 30 as 'powered' rather than 'unpowered for every realistic gain'.
findings.evidence: docs/results/adamson_cf_g_arm_summary.md:11-16 SE_adj 0.012857, 0.007593, 0.013529, 0.004816, 0.002817, 0.004619 on 50 perturbations; docs/PLAN_R_FRESH_TEST.md:89 'Minimum n: at least 30 in-distribution eligible targets in R2, else B.3 and B.4 are reported as not powered'. Not checkable beyond that: no fresh-cohort SE exists.
findings.fix: Add to PLAN_R section 3 and PAPER the calculation: the minimal detectable paired gain at n = 30 for a single model (2·SE scaled by sqrt(50/30) from the development rows) and for an arm under the arm rule; define 'not powered' by that number rather than the count alone.

verdict.note: The objection stands: the 30-target floor is stated in PAPER 192-195, PLAN_R 89-91 and ROADMAP 241-243 with the word 'powered' and no detectable effect, no per-condition spread and no computation; the only MDE formula in the docs (WETLAB_CANDIDATES 47-50) is for the wet-lab readout and says it is not the power of the paired reading; PLAN_R's 'to be filled in' list has no power item. The finding misreads four details. (1) It misquotes the sentence: the text says 'the arm criteria are reported as not powered' (B.3 and B.4) on 'in-distribution' targets, not 'the fresh test' on 'eligible targets'; the A.4 feature reading on R2 is in fact under no stated floor at all, a gap the finding does not see. (2) The fresh test does not use the '±2 SE_adj rule': PLAN_R 149-150 and PAPER 205-206 use the plain paired SE for a feature, and PAPER 207-211 k·SE with k = max(2, Welch t) plus one Holm correction over the batch for an arm; SE_adj is the development tier's overlap widening (PAPER 170), and on the fresh test the gene-clustering ratio is about 1 (distinct target genes in a 2,055-gene panel, as in the G readings). (3) 'With the fresh-cohort SE unknown, the rule may be impossible to meet at any plausible gain' is speculation; the repository holds the per-perturbation paired spreads to estimate it: the six block G sealed readings (n = 21) give paired SEs of 0.011 to 0.063, so 2·SE at n = 30 is roughly 0.02 to 0.05 (median about 0.036, worst run 0.106) for a selected model against its start, and the OOF readings (n = 50) give 0.007 to 0.035 against a parent; gains of the size the development arms make over their start (0.03 to 0.08 sealed in scaling.md, +0.06 and +0.07 in two G runs) are therefore at the edge of detectability, while arm-versus-arm and arm-versus-control differences (0.01 to 0.03) are inside the noise, and the Welch-t and Holm steps raise the bar further for the arm criteria. (4) scaling.md:10 is the between-repeat sd of the sealed score, which enters sd_g in the arm rule, not the per-condition spread that sets S; and the Norman B1 export's report holds no per-condition deltas in the repository, so the finding's suggested data source is wrong on both counts (the Adamson G readings are the right source, and the modality the test scores). The floor is also not in PLAN_H at all, so 'doc: both' should read PAPER and PLAN_R (with ROADMAP section 8). Severity major, not reject: the reading rule reports every gain with its realised paired SE and Holm p (PAPER 250, PLAN_R 161), so a null result stays interpretable after the fact and the design is neither unfair nor irreproducible; but a pre-registered floor labelled 'powered' without a stated minimum detectable gain is an unsupported claim in a methods paper and must be fixed before the manifest is built and before submission. It does not need to change before block H's first paid session, which is the development comparison. PR #70 does not touch it.
verdict.corrected_fix: By a dated note at the end of docs/PLAN_R_FRESH_TEST.md (the plan changes only that way) and in PAPER_COMPARISON.md's 'Eligibility and the deposit' paragraph: state the minimum detectable paired gain at the floor, computed from the development data's per-perturbation spread, which is already in the repository: the six block G sealed readings (docs/results/adamson_cf_g_sealed_summary.md, n = 21, paired SE 0.011 to 0.063, per-perturbation sd 0.05 to 0.29) and the OOF readings (docs/results/adamson_cf_g_arm_summary.md, n = 50, SE_adj 0.003 to 0.014). At n = 30 that gives 2·SE of about 0.02 to 0.05 for a selected model against its start (median about 0.036) and 0.01 to 0.04 against a parent, before the arm rule's k·SE (k = max(2, Welch t on R = 3 runs), sd_g from scaling.md's between-repeat spread of 0.002 to 0.044) and the Holm step over the whole batch. Say what the test can show (an arm's gain over P0 or C0 of the size seen in development, 0.03 to 0.08) and cannot (arm-versus-arm differences of 0.01 to 0.03, which B.4 will then report as 'what wins' without a verdict). Then either keep 30 as the floor with that MDE named beside it, or derive the floor from a target gain: n >= (2·sd/Δ)², so sd 0.08 and Δ 0.03 give n about 28, Δ 0.02 about 64. Name A.4 on R2 under the floor explicitly (PLAN_R 89-91 names only B.3, B.4 and A.3). Label the MDE as indicative, since the fresh cohort's per-perturbation spread may differ (same-target agreement with Replogle has median 0.52, docs/results/external_loo_replogle2022_k562_v2.md:86), and require the holder's report to print the realised paired SE beside it. Do not cite the Norman B1 export for per-condition deltas: its report.md in the repository holds none, and Norman is not the modality this test scores.
verdict.reviewer_sentence: The fresh test pre-registers a floor of 30 in-distribution targets below which the arm criteria are 'not powered', but neither the plan nor the paper states the paired gain that 30 targets can detect; from the project's own development readings (per-perturbation paired SD 0.05 to 0.29 on the Adamson sealed set), twice the paired SE at n = 30 is roughly 0.02 to 0.05 before the Welch-t and Holm steps, so the test can show a gain of the size the arms make over their start but not the 0.01 to 0.03 differences between arms. State the minimum detectable gain beside the floor, say which comparisons it covers (the feature rule A.4 on R2 is under no stated floor at all), and either justify 30 from it or set the floor from a target gain.

findings.title: The 1e-6 reproduction cited covers Norman B1 on its own conditions, not Adamson or new targets
findings.claim: Every model predicts every eligible target through tools/frozen_model.py predict-targets without refitting, after the adapter reproduced each arm's saved predictions to 1e-6 (docs/results/norman_frozen_export_20261013/report.md: three B1 members exact).
findings.problem: The sentence reads as if the gate were passed for this paper's arms. The cited report is a Norman B1 export reproducing the original anchor conditions only, says the anchor-plus-new-condition recipe 'still needs prospective acceptance' and did not infer on any external cohort. No Adamson arm has been exported or reproduced; the new-target path is covered only by a synthetic fixture. The tolerance is stated three ways: 'bit for bit' (ROADMAP D7), rtol = atol = 1e-6 (PLAN_R), 'to 1e-6' (PAPER), while the report says the ensemble is 'not bit identical' (5.96e-08).

verdict.note: The objection stands in substance: the only real-data reproduction is the Norman B1 export replaying the 119 conditions it was trained and scored on, no Adamson export exists yet, and the anchors-plus-one-new-condition path that every fresh-test prediction will take has been exercised only on a four-gene synthetic fixture, whose test checks that the `predict_targets` wrapper equals `predict_ensemble` on the same query rather than any independently known value. ROADMAP D7 itself asks for a reproduction "on a new cohort path" before any deposit date, and PLAN_R section 6 narrowed that to "on its own conditions" plus the synthetic test, so the plan's gate is weaker than the ROADMAP's wording. Three things the finding gets wrong. (1) The quoted claim is not in the paper: line 197-198 says "saved predictions to 1e-6", not "every sealed score", and it names the B1 report; no score is reproduced and the report says so. (2) PLAN_R:130-132 already says which export the figure comes from and on which conditions (B1, 13 October, "on its own conditions"), already makes the per-Adamson-arm own-conditions reproduction a gate before the deposit (:134-136), and lists the summaries as to be filled (:179); so the first half of the fix is done in the plan, though not in the paper, where "each arm's saved predictions" with B1 as the only evidence reads as if the Adamson arms' checks were done. (3) The proposed gate, "an Adamson export, scored on held-out conditions through the new-target path, bit-exact against the lab's own scorer", cannot be run as stated: a held-out condition is an anchor and takes the saved full-batch row (frozen.py:424-426), the manifest pins the anchor set so it cannot be removed (:340-343), and for a batch-dependent feature a different batch is not expected to be bit-exact (FROZEN_EXPORT.md:52-55, test fixture `batch_switch`). The lab never predicted a target it did not see, so there is no lab reference for a genuinely new target. What is possible, and what the plan lacks, is a real-data exercise of the new-condition path with a known reference: re-submit each held-out condition under a fresh id with its own targets through `predict` (the `_queries` check allows it), which must reproduce the saved prediction bit for bit for every batch-independent feature, with batch-dependent features declared beforehand and their differences reported. Not fixed in PR #70, which changes only a PLAN_H dated note and the Mac scripts. Severity: the paper wording is minor, but a one-shot, irrevocable deposit through a path never run on real data is a plan gap to close before the deposit, at no cost.

verdict.reviewer_sentence: The 1e-6 reproduction the paper cites (line 198) is the Norman B1 export replaying its own 119 saved conditions; no Adamson export exists yet, and the anchors-plus-one-new-condition path that every fresh-test prediction will take has been run only on a four-gene synthetic fixture (tests/test_frozen_model.py:287), which the B1 report and FROZEN_EXPORT.md themselves flag as unverified on real data. findings.title: No exporter or fitting rule exists for package-arm, C2 or single-feature models in the fresh-test batch
findings.claim: Every model predicts every eligible target through tools/frozen_model.py predict-targets without refitting ... The batch is, per arm, its three system models and at most three single features with a development verdict and the largest out-of-fold gain, plus P0 ... and C0.
findings.problem: The only exporter, genemila/frozen.py export_ensemble, takes a receipt of frozen members each naming a lab run directory, an EXP_ id and that experiment's models.pkl and run_spec.json; tools/frozen_model.py export wraps it and nothing else builds a frozen package. A3 and A4 hand back plugin files and results.tsv (evaluate.py saves scores and alphas, no fitted model), C2 is a directory of files, and a 'single feature added to the parent' exists only as a feature_compare refit in memory; no tool writes a receipt for any of them. So only the lab arms' selected experiments can reach the headline tier, what a package arm's 'system model' is (which fit, which alpha, chosen how) is nowhere defined, and the documents do not say on which rows (training only or plus val1), at which alpha, or by one rule for both sides of a pair the deposited models are fitted. The lab would deposit its own fits (possibly lasso, alpha chosen on the seen tier) while every other model would be a refit: B.3 cannot be executed as written and would not be 'one procedure'.

findings.fix: Pre-register now, before any session, one fitting rule for every deposited model: ridge on P0 plus the files, fitted on all 50 training perturbations (no val1), alpha chosen by the fair test's honest OOF rule on seeds 101-103, parent and candidate fitted identically; build and test an exporter from a feature_compare system or add-one row (plugin directory, standardisation arrays, receipt, reproduction check) to the frozen package format; deposit every arm, lab arms included, from that one refit, or state that the lab models are the runs' own fits and why; say so in PAPER 'The fresh test' and PLAN_R section 4.

verdict.note: Confirmed in the files. The only export path is genemila/frozen.py export_ensemble (wrapped by tools/frozen_model.py export): it takes a hand-written receipt whose every member names a lab run directory, an id matching EXP_[0-9]+, that experiment's artifacts/<EXP>/models.pkl and run_spec.json, the run's complete feature_store/*.py snapshot and public_data/ hashes, and it deserialises the lab's pickled estimator grid. The three kinds of batch member the finding names have none of that: (a) a package session's hand-back is plugin files plus runs/kept/scores.json (scores and alphas; evaluate.py persists no estimator) and collect_handback.py only copies and hashes the files; (b) C2 is four .py files and a README with no run; (c) a single feature over the parent exists only as feature_compare.py's closed-form OOF refit in memory, with a different alpha per fold-seed pair and nothing saved; and even for a lab arm an EXP with exactly P0 + x exists only by chance. No document gives the fitting rule (rows: training only or plus val1; alpha: the lab's val1+OOF choice or the fair test's OOF rule; model family) for any refit member, and the reproduction gate at PAPER 197-198 and PLAN_R 130-136 presupposes 'each arm's saved predictions', which A3, A4 and C2 do not have. PLAN_R section 4 nonetheless commits every member 'as a frozen export' and section 6 says genemila/frozen.py stays byte-identical, so the gap cannot be closed by editing the exporter's core; it needs a wrapper that produces a lab-layout run plus a receipt, or a declared lab-only fresh test. No dated note in PLAN_H (247-384), PLAN_R (none exist) or ROADMAP amends this. What the finding gets wrong, none of it material: the hand-back collector is tools/baselines/collect_handback.py, not tools/task_package/ (which holds evaluate.py, literal.py and program.md); frozen_model.py export's parser takes --receipt, --receipt-sha256 and --member EXP=ALPHA, not 'a run directory' (the receipt's members name the run directories, so the substance holds); and the quoted claim is a paraphrase of PAPER 199-200, which reads 'its three system models and at most three single features with a development verdict and the largest out-of-fold gain'. The finding also understates it: no tool in the repository writes a receipt even for lab runs (the B1 receipt was assembled by hand for PR #13), and the adapter check HANDOFF reports (17 October) covered the Norman B1 export only. Severity major, not reject: the fresh test is undated and costs nothing, the gap is detectable before any deposit, and the fix is a tool plus a pre-registered rule; but as written the batch cannot be built for two of its arms or for any single-feature member, which would silently make the fresh tier lab-only or invite a fitting rule chosen after the development scores are known, so it must be fixed before the first paid block H session (so the rule is not chosen with the hand-backs in view) and certainly before the batch is listed on #41.
verdict.corrected_fix: (1) Pre-register, as a dated note at the end of PLAN_H and a line in PLAN_R section 8 (not an edit of the earlier text), one fitting rule for every refit member of the batch: ridge on the lab's standardised design (genemila/pipeline.py run) with the parent P0 (control_mean, mean_response, is_target) plus the package session's kept files, or the three scoreable C2 plugins, or the one single feature, at each plugin's own class params (--source rule) or the run's recorded params (--source-run rule), fitted on the 50 training perturbations only (no val1, consistent with D5's 'the fresh test is the one unseen tier'), alpha chosen by the fair test's honest OOF rule on seeds 101-103 with the tie rule stated (for example the alpha with the best mean OOF pearson_delta over the three seeds, as feature_compare.score()'s full-training fit does), parent and candidate fitted identically; and say whether the lab arms' system models are the runs' own selected EXPs (their alpha chosen on val1 + OOF, possibly another model family) or the same refit, and why, so B.3 is one procedure or its asymmetry is disclosed. (2) Build and test the exporter before the batch is listed: a tool (for example tools/freeze_feature_set.py) that assembles a lab-layout run directory (public_data/public.npz and knowledge/*.json copied from the clean bundle, feature_store/ holding exactly the plugin files, artifacts/EXP_nnnn/run_spec.json and models.pkl produced by `python -m genemila.pipeline run --spec ... --public ... --plugins ... --out ...` under PYTHONHASHSEED=0) and writes the receipt JSON (frozen_members with run_directory, experiment_id, selected_alpha, weight 1, features, files_sha256), so tools/frozen_model.py export and genemila/frozen.py run unchanged (PLAN_R section 6's byte pin); tests in tests/test_frozen_model.py export a synthetic hand-back and a single feature and reproduce them through predict-targets. (3) Restate the gate: PAPER 197-198 and PLAN_R 130-136 presuppose 'each arm's saved predictions'; for a refit member the gate is the refit's own predictions.npz from pipeline.run reproduced through the export's anchor path at rtol = atol = 1e-6, said as such. (4) Alternatively, if no exporter is written: state in PAPER 'The fresh test', PLAN_R section 4 and ROADMAP D8 that only lab-run experiments can be frozen, so the deposit holds the lab arms' selected EXPs, P0 and C0 only, B.3/B.4 are read lab-only on the fresh tier, and claim (2) is read on the development tier alone.
verdict.reviewer_sentence: The fresh-test batch (PAPER 199-200; PLAN_H 224-226; PLAN_R 104-105, 'each as a frozen export') includes the package arms' and C2's system models and up to three single-feature models per arm, yet the only exporter (genemila/frozen.py export_ensemble, wrapped by tools/frozen_model.py export) accepts a receipt whose members each name a lab run directory, an EXP_[0-9]+ id and that experiment's artifacts/<EXP>/models.pkl and run_spec.json; the package evaluator persists no estimator (runs/kept/scores.json holds scores and alphas), C2 is a directory of four files with no run, and the fair test refits in closed form and saves nothing, so no document or tool says on which rows, at which alpha or by which rule those models are fitted, and the batch cannot be built as described. Pre-register one fitting rule for every refit member and build and test the exporter, or declare the fresh test lab-only, before the first paid session and before the batch is listed on #41.

findings.title: Fresh-test Holm family is not enumerated and the arm rule yields no p-value
findings.claim: Every paired comparison in the batch enters one Holm correction at 0.05.
findings.problem: The batch holds, per arm, three system models and up to three single features, plus P0 and C0, over two slices (R1, R2) and two subsets (in- and out-of-distribution). 'Every paired comparison' could mean each model against P0 (about 36), each against P0 and C0, or all pairs among roughly 38 models (about 700), with or without the out-of-distribution rows; the family size moves the bar from z about 3 to z about 4, so the correction cannot be pre-registered as written. Separately, the arm rule returns a verdict from k·SE (two-sided t) and no p-value, while the protocol's Holm uses a one-sided normal p per model; the text never says which decides an arm or how a Holm-adjusted per-model p feeds a per-arm k·SE verdict.
findings.evidence: tools/arm_reading.py:161-163 returns {"R": R, "G": G, ..., "verdict": verdict} with no p; docs/FEATURE_COMPARISON_PROTOCOL.md:357-361 'every candidate sent there ... gets a one-sided p from its paired M1 gain, p = 1 − Φ(Δ / SE_adj) ...; Holm runs over all of them at 0.05'; docs/PLAN_R_FRESH_TEST.md:156-157, :162 'one Holm correction over the whole batch, R1 and R2 together'.
findings.fix: Enumerate the Holm family in PAPER and PLAN_R before any deposit: list each (model, reference, slice, subset) pair, give m and the sidedness, and state that the arm rule is applied to Holm-uncorrected per-run gains as a separate pre-registered verdict (or define the arm p as the t tail at nu degrees of freedom and put it in the family).

verdict.note: The objection stands in substance: PLAN_R section 7 and PAPER 204-211 call for 'one Holm correction at 0.05' over 'every paired comparison in the batch' and ask the holder to report 'Holm-adjusted p-values', yet neither document defines the p-value (statistic, reference distribution, one- or two-sided, plain paired SE or the overlap-widened SE_adj), neither names the baselines an arm is compared with (P0 only? C0? every other arm?), so the family size m is unknown, and neither says whether the stated thresholds (2 SE for a feature; k·SE with k = max(2, t_0.975) for an arm) or the Holm-adjusted p decides. These are not equivalent: with m >= 3 Holm at 0.05 needs a raw one-sided p <= 0.0167 (z >= 2.13), stricter than 2 SE, and at a plausible m of 20 to 40 it needs z of about 3; the headline verdict therefore depends on a choice the plan leaves open, and the holder scores once with no second look. The tools confirm the gap: arm_reading.py and evaluator._paired emit no p-value. The finding misreads three details. (1) 'Never enumerated' is wrong for the models: PLAN_R 4 and 8 and PLAN_H 224-226 require the batch, every model with its export-manifest sha256, on #41 before any contact with the holder; what is missing is the list of comparisons (pairs), not of models. (2) 'The arm rule yields no p-value, so Holm cannot be applied to it' is overstated: the arm statistic G/SE on Welch-Satterthwaite nu is a t-statistic and the tool already computes nu and t.ppf(0.975, nu) (arm_reading.py:151-153), so a two-sided p is derivable; the correct statement is that no document or tool defines or emits it, and the same-sign and wins conditions are gates, not part of any p. (3) 'Two tests with incompatible decision rules are called one procedure' is not itself a flaw: Holm is valid over heterogeneous tests as long as each contributes a valid p. The real defect is the one the finding half-states: three documents give three rules for the same tier (GOAL_CRITERIA A.4/B.4: 2 SE and wins, no Holm; PROTOCOL 6.3-6.4: one-sided Φ(Δ/SE_adj), Holm over all candidates, Holm p <= 0.05 plus wins, with the arm rule as an extra gate, marked 'proposal, to be fixed before anything is scored'; PLAN_R 7 / PAPER: 2 SE or k·SE thresholds plus an undefined Holm). PLAN_R, the fixed plan, silently diverged from the protocol's proposal and never resolved it. Severity major rather than reject: nothing has run, no holder is named, no deposit exists, and the plan's own mechanism (a dated note) can fix it before the batch is posted; left unfixed through the deposit it would become reject-level, since the headline rule would then be chosen after the scores exist. Not fixed by PR #70 (its only document change is the script-gaps note in PLAN_H) nor by PR #75.
verdict.corrected_fix: A dated note at the end of docs/PLAN_R_FRESH_TEST.md (its own amendment mechanism), before the batch list goes on #41, that: (1) defines the p-value of every paired comparison, adopting or amending the protocol's section 6.3 proposal: for a feature row, one-sided p = 1 − Φ(Δ/SE) (or Student t on n−1) on the in-distribution R2 perturbations, the direction being the pre-registered sign, and say whether SE is the plain paired SE or the overlap-widened SE_adj (on a single-gene CRISPRi slice they coincide; say so); for an arm, choose one of two and name it: (a) one p per system model against each baseline, three per (arm, baseline) pair, with the arm rule's same-sign and wins conditions kept as gates outside Holm, as protocol 6.4 does, or (b) one p per (arm, baseline) pair from the arm statistic G/SE on Welch-Satterthwaite nu, two-sided, and add `p` to arm_rule's output in tools/arm_reading.py (nu and k are already computed at lines 151-153) so the holder's number is reproducible from the tool; (2) enumerates the comparisons, not only the models: each feature-vs-parent pair, each (arm, baseline) pair with the baselines named (P0, C0, and whether other arms count as baselines for B.4's 'each baseline'), and how many of them are R1 rows, so m is a number posted on #41 beside the batch hashes; (3) states which rule decides: Holm-adjusted p <= 0.05 plus the wins gate (plus same sign for arms), and demotes 'more than twice the paired standard error' and 'G exceeds k·SE' to descriptive thresholds or drops them, since for m >= 3 they are weaker than Holm and cannot be the decider; (4) propagates the same rule to docs/GOAL_CRITERIA.md A.4 and B.4 (which carry no Holm) and to docs/PAPER_COMPARISON.md 204-211, and marks the protocol's section 6.3-6.4 proposal as superseded or adopted. Apply Holm to the p-values only; the sign and wins conditions stay gates.
verdict.reviewer_sentence: The fresh test, which supplies the paper's headline numbers, is read under three different rules in three documents (GOAL_CRITERIA A.4/B.4: twice the paired SE, no correction; the protocol's section 6.3-6.4 'proposal': one-sided p = 1 − Φ(Δ/SE_adj) with Holm over all candidates; PLAN_R section 7 and the paper's Methods: a 2-SE feature threshold and a k·SE arm rule plus 'one Holm correction at 0.05' over 'every paired comparison'), and the governing plan neither defines the p-value Holm would adjust (no tool emits one), nor names the baselines and hence the family size, nor says whether the threshold or the adjusted p decides, although for any family of three or more the two give different verdicts. Fix it by dated note before the batch is posted: enumerate the comparisons, define the p-value for feature rows and for the arm statistic, and make the Holm-adjusted p, with the sign and wins conditions as gates, the single decision rule in all three documents.

findings.title: Fresh-test feature rule contradicts protocol section 6.4 on what decides
findings.claim: A feature is useful when its model beats its parent in pearson_delta by more than twice the paired standard error with wins on more than half the in-distribution perturbations of R2, with the pre-registered sign.
findings.problem: The sentence gives a fixed 2·SE bar (one-sided p about 0.023) as the decision, while four lines later every comparison enters a Holm correction at 0.05 and the protocol says a feature is useful when its Holm-adjusted p is at most 0.05. With 36 or more comparisons the Holm bar is z about 3 or higher, so the 2·SE sentence is either moot or a second, looser rule; a referee cannot tell which verdict the paper prints when 2 < z < 3.

findings.fix: Replace 'more than twice the paired standard error' with 'Holm-adjusted one-sided p at most 0.05 over the batch of section [x]' in PAPER and PLAN_R section 7, and say that 2·SE is reported descriptively.

verdict.note: The finding inverts both documents. Protocol section 6.4 is the Holm-adjusted (family-wise) rule, not a plain paired-gain-with-sign rule, and it names no sign; the paper's rule at 205-211 is a paired gain of twice the paired SE with majority wins and the pre-registered sign, with one Holm correction over the batch, citing PLAN_R section 7, and it matches PLAN_R 149-157 and GOAL_CRITERIA A.4 (plus A.2/A.3's sign) word for word. Nothing in the paper carries the development verdict (the Westfall-Young p_fwer) over to the fresh test: the development verdict appears at 199-200 only as the screen that picks which features enter the batch, exactly as protocol 6.2, PLAN_H reading 3 and ROADMAP D8 say, and Table 2 (271) keeps the development p_fwer columns separate from the fresh-test "R2 gain ± SE, wins, Holm p" column. So the paper and the plan already state one rule and cite the section that fixes it. PLAN_H states no fresh-test rule at all, so "doc: both" is wrong for it. What remains is wording drift, not a contradiction: protocol 6.3 is explicitly "(proposal, to be fixed before anything is scored)", written 15-16 October, and PLAN_R, written 16-17 October, is where it was fixed ("Reading, paired per perturbation, fixed here"), adding the 2×SE floor, the sign and the in-distribution subset to the protocol's Holm-p-plus-majority wording. The fixed rule is a superset of the protocol's conditions (with Holm at 0.05 over the batch's many comparisons the first step already needs z above 2.13; the 2×SE floor binds only on later Holm steps), and the SE_adj versus paired SE difference is nil on single-gene Replogle CRISPRi (sealed_reading.py: ratio exactly 1). The only gap is that the protocol carries no note pointing section 6 items 3-4 at PLAN_R section 7.
verdict.corrected_fix: No change to the paper's or PLAN_R's rule. Add one dated line to docs/FEATURE_COMPARISON_PROTOCOL.md (at the end, as its convention requires) saying that the tier-F proposal of section 6, items 3 and 4, was fixed by docs/PLAN_R_FRESH_TEST.md section 7 on 2026-10-16/17: gain above twice the paired SE, wins on more than half the in-distribution R2 perturbations, the pre-registered sign (GOAL_CRITERIA A.2 to A.4), one Holm correction over the whole batch at 0.05, the arm rule of tools/arm_reading.py; and note that SE_adj equals the paired SE on a single-gene cohort. Optionally the paper's reading-rule paragraph (205) can add "(docs/FEATURE_COMPARISON_PROTOCOL.md section 6, items 3-4, as fixed by PLAN_R section 7)" beside its existing PLAN_R citation.
verdict.reviewer_sentence: The paper's fresh-test feature rule (gain above twice the paired SE, majority wins, pre-registered sign, one Holm correction over the batch) is the rule PLAN_R section 7 fixes and GOAL_CRITERIA A.4 states, and the development verdict enters only as the screen that selects the batch, so there is no second rule; the protocol's section 6 items 3-4 remain labelled a proposal and should carry a one-line note that PLAN_R section 7 fixed them.

verdict.note: Confirmed on both counts. (1) No holder-side scoring tool exists or is named: PLAN_R section 7 points the holder at `genemila/benchmark/`, a package with no command-line entry point whose `evaluate()` takes arrays and whose CellForge DE metrics need `reference.build` over cells (today called only by the oracle and the results table from a bundle's private directory); the ingest normalisation lives in `genemila/data/external_screen.py:stream_sums`, written for knowledge-file building, not scoring. The deposit (section 5) and the to-fill list (section 8) carry no script, commit or hash for what the holder runs, so the holder would have to write glue code of their own, unpinned. (2) `tools/arm_reading.py rule` reads only sealed_reading JSON twins and refuses any entry without `planner`, `bundle`, `has_summary`, `stored_sealed` and a `cluster_ratio.estimator` (lines 113-136, 220-228); `combine` opens run directories and a QueryOracle over a bundle (429-434). A package arm's hand-back has none of these, and the holder's scores are not in that format, so the tool as it stands cannot produce the fresh-test arm reading for any arm, lab or package. One detail in the finding is wrong: arm_reading.py never reads `feature_compare.json` (no such string in the file); `rule` reads sealed_reading JSON twins and `combine` reads run directories through `open_run`. That does not weaken the objection. Two things the finding did not say that strengthen it: `arm_rule(g, s, wins, n)` is a pure function, so the rule itself is computable from the holder's per-perturbation scores — the gap is the absence of a fixed, hashed pipeline from deposit plus cohort to those inputs, not an undefined rule; and "`tools/arm_reading.py`'s rule" is itself ambiguous for the fresh test, because the tool's RULE (lines 61-65) inflates each run's SE by a gene-clustering ratio that comes from sealed_reading's jackknife on visible labels, which the holder cannot compute, while the paper's and PLAN_R's spelled-out versions omit it; a holder reader must say which SE enters. Not 'reject': nothing has run, the rule is stated mathematically, and the metrics are defined in protected code; but the deposit is one irreversible step away (manifest built, adapter gate passed, only the holder's name missing per HANDOFF), and after it 'nobody ... changes a rule' (PLAN_R:163), so the script and its hash must exist and be pinned before then. The PLAN's amendment rule (a dated note at the end) has not been used for this; PLAN_R has no dated notes.
verdict.corrected_fix: Before the deposit, and recorded as a dated note at the end of PLAN_R and in section 8's list: (a) add one holder scoring tool (for example `tools/fresh_test_score.py`) whose inputs are the deposit archive, the slice manifest and either the cohort cells or the per-perturbation means Andres chooses; it computes the per-label means and control mean with `genemila/data/external_screen.py`'s normalisation, aligns columns from `genes.txt`, builds the DE reference with `genemila/benchmark/reference.build` when cells are given (and, when only means are given, states that the DE set is the top-20 |true delta| of `evaluate()` and that the Wilcoxon `cellforge_*_de` and `*_deset` metrics are not computable), scores every deposited `predictions.npz` with `evaluate()` and `comparable.cellforge()` unchanged, writes `paired_summary` for every pre-registered pair, applies `arm_reading.arm_rule` to each arm's three system models against each baseline with the SE it uses stated (plain paired SE; no clustering inflation exists off the lab), runs one Holm correction over the posted batch, and emits one JSON of fixed schema plus a markdown report; (b) give `tools/arm_reading.py` a `fresh` subcommand (or a separate reader) that takes that JSON instead of sealed_reading twins and skips the planner/summary.json checks for package-arm members, with a synthetic-fixture test; (c) pin the scoring tool's commit and sha256 in the manifest and on #41 before the holder is told the archive exists, and have the holder run that pinned version; (d) reword PAPER:204-211 and PLAN_R:140-146, 153 to name the script, its hash, and the SE definition the arm rule uses on the fresh test, instead of 'the evaluator's metrics' and '`tools/arm_reading.py`'s rule'.

findings.title: Arm rule at R = 3 cannot detect any gain the arms have shown; no power statement
findings.claim: An arm beats a baseline under tools/arm_reading.py's rule: the mean gain G over the R runs exceeds k·SE with SE = sqrt(S² + sd_g²/R) ... k = max(2, Student t at 0.975 on Welch-Satterthwaite degrees of freedom) ... PAPER 349-351: 'No claim of a difference inside run-to-run noise: three sessions per LLM arm'.
findings.problem: With three sessions the sd_g²/R term has two degrees of freedom and the Welch k rises toward 3. Applying the coded formula to block G's recorded per-run gains over P0 gives, for G0, G = 0.0417 but k·SE = 0.0693 (S = 0.0113, sd_g = 0.0353, nu = 3.4, k = 2.97): a 0.04 pearson_delta arm gain, larger than any feature gain in this project, reads 'no difference established'; for G1 the bar is 0.010 against G = 0.0067. On a fresh subset of about 30 targets S is larger still, and the roadmap's own odds for B.4 are 20 percent. The arm comparison the Discussion lists as supportable cannot, at the spreads observed, find a difference between any two arms, and neither document states the minimal detectable arm difference, so a reviewer cannot tell a null table from an underpowered one.
findings.evidence: tools/arm_reading.py:143-153 sd = float(g_.std(ddof=1)) if R > 1 else 0.0; se = float(np.sqrt(S ** 2 + sd ** 2 / R)); Welch den; k = max(2.0, float(stats.t.ppf(0.975, nu))); docs/results/adamson_cf_g1_vs_g0/feature_compare.json rows g0_r0/r2/r3: mean_diff 0.0563, 0.0015, 0.0674 with se_adj 0.0129, 0.0076, 0.0135; docs/results/adamson_cf_g_arm_summary.md:7-8 |g0|3|0.525950139 ± 0.035263074|, |g1|3|0.490964428 ± 0.004435578|; formula applied: g0 k·SE = 0.0693 > G = 0.0417; g1 k·SE = 0.0101 > G = 0.0067; docs/GOAL_CRITERIA.md:108-109; docs/ROADMAP.md:33-34 'B.4 ... about 20 percent'.
findings.fix: Add a pre-registered power paragraph to the fresh-test Methods: the minimal detectable arm gain under the rule at R = 3 from block G's spreads (about 0.07 for a G0-like arm, 0.01 for a G1-like arm) and at the measured S and sd_g on n = 30; state that with three sessions the arm rule is reported descriptively and an arm claim needs more sessions; move Discussion claim (2) to 'claims it cannot support' unless sessions are added, or raise R for the matched arms.

If it does not, the paper reports what wins." it bounds the perturbation term S, not sd_g²/R); :153-154: "B.3 and B.4 (arms): each arm's three system models against each baseline under `tools/arm_reading.py`'s rule (G above k·SE, SE = sqrt(S² + sd_g²/R), one sign, most wins)". tools/arm_reading.py:146-150: `se = float(np.sqrt(S ** 2 + sd ** 2 / R))`, `den = (S ** 4 / (n - 1) ...) + ((sd ** 2 / R) ** 2 / (R - 1) ...)`, `nu = se ** 4 / den`, `k = max(2.0, float(stats.t.ppf(0.975, nu)))` — when sd_g dominates, nu falls toward R−1 = 2 and k toward 4.30. docs/results/adamson_cf_g_arm_summary.md:7-8: "g0 | 3 | 0.525950139 ± 0.035263074 | 0.041719869 ± 0.035263074", "g1 | 3 | 0.490964428 ± 0.004435578 | 0.006734158 ± 0.004435578"; Applying the tool's own formula (scipy, n = 50): G0 vs P0 gives SE 0.0233, nu 3.4, k 2.97, bar 0.069 > G 0.042; G1 gives bar 0.010 > G 0.0067; neither passes at R = 3. On a 30-target fresh slice with S = 0.01 the bar is 0.024 (sd_g 0.01), 0.038 (0.02), 0.071 (0.035); at R = 5 the 0.035 case falls to 0.043, at R = 8 to 0.034. docs/results/scaling.md:10: sealed pearson_delta sd across repeats "0.566 ± 0.032 | 0.602 ± 0.002 | 0.584 ± 0.001 | 0.577 ± 0.022 | 0.594 ± 0.009 | 0.570 ± 0.044"; :13 gain over start sealed: control 0.034, agent arms 0.047-0.083 (arm-minus-control 0.013-0.050). docs/results/norman_b2_arm_vs_additive.md:17: "sealed, pooled | +0.0113 | 0.0042 | 0.0054 | 0.0053 | 2.14 | 0.0113 | yes | 117/51 of 168 | arm better" — the rule did return a verdict at R = 3 when sd_g was 0.005. docs/results/norman_b2_arm_vs_control.md: "sealed, pooled | +0.0051 | 0.0090 | 0.0054 | 0.0095 | 2.01 | 0.0191 | ... no difference established" (arm vs the no-LLM control, the block H analogue, null at R = 3). git diff cfa8034 origin/claude/block-h-script-gaps -- docs/PLAN_H_COMPARISON.md: 22 added lines, the 2026-10-17 22:00 UTC note on the probe reset and run_biomni's rate only; docs/PAPER_COMPARISON.md and docs/PLAN_R_FRESH_TEST.md unchanged.
verdict.note: The substance holds: neither document states a minimum detectable arm difference or a power statement for R = 3, and PLAN_R's only power floor (30 in-distribution targets) bounds the perturbation-sampling term S, not the run-to-run term sd_g²/R that dominates at three sessions. Computed with the rule's own code on the lab's Adamson arms, the bar is 0.069 for the G0-like spread (sd_g 0.035; k rises to 2.97 because the Welch-Satterthwaite df falls to 3.4) against a gain of 0.042, and on a 30-target fresh slice about 0.07 at that spread, above every arm-versus-control gain seen on Adamson (0.013-0.05, scaling.md). The paper's headline claim (2) rests on this rule and the Results template has no place for the rule's G, sd_g, k·SE or verdict, so what is reported when every arm reads 'no difference established' is unspecified. The finding misreads three details. (a) It quotes GOAL_CRITERIA B.4's 'twice the paired standard error' and 'reports what wins' as PAPER 207-211; the paper's and PLAN_R's rule is the stricter k·SE with the between-session term, so the finding understates the bar (and the inconsistency between B.4 and the paper's rule is itself a gap it did not name). (b) 'Cannot detect any gain the arms have shown' is too strong: power depends on sd_g, which spans 0.004 to 0.035 across arms; at the G1-like spread the bar is 0.010, and B2 on Norman returned 'arm better' at R = 3 (G 0.0113 at bar 0.0113). (c) On block H's OOF tier the arm rule is explicitly descriptive (PLAN_H 16-18, 223); the verdict is taken on the fresh test under PLAN_R B.3/B.4, so the finding's objection lands there. The paper already disclaims differences inside run-to-run noise (349-351) and names more sessions per arm as the strengthening (359), but a disclaimer is not an MDE. PR #70 touches none of this.
verdict.corrected_fix: Before the chain (a dated note in docs/PLAN_H_COMPARISON.md, and the paper's Methods after line 211): state the minimum detectable arm difference at R = 3 from tools/arm_reading.py's own formula using the development spread: about 0.010 at the G1-like spread (sd_g 0.004, S 0.004, n 50), about 0.07 at the G0-like spread (sd_g 0.035, S 0.011; k ≈ 3.0 as the df falls to ≈ 3), and on a 30-target fresh slice with S ≈ 0.01 about 0.024, 0.038 and 0.071 for sd_g 0.01, 0.02 and 0.035, against the arm-minus-control gains of 0.013-0.05 observed on Adamson; say that the design can show only an effect above that bar and that an arm with G0-like spread is expected to read 'no difference established' at R = 3. Say in advance what the paper reports when no arm passes: Table 1 and the fresh-test table gain per-arm columns for the rule's G, S, sd_g, k·SE and verdict, and the Results sentence is 'no system's features are shown better' with means ± sd, never a ranking. Reconcile GOAL_CRITERIA B.4 ('twice the paired standard error') with the k·SE rule of the paper and PLAN_R so one rule is named in all three. Beside PLAN_R's 30-target floor, note that it bounds S only, not sd_g²/R. Put the choice of R to Andres before the first paid session, with the cost of each extra session per arm (the $2.50 session cap; R = 5 lowers the G0-like bar from ≈ 0.07 to ≈ 0.043, R = 8 to ≈ 0.034), and record his answer as a dated note; never raise R silently.
verdict.reviewer_sentence: The comparison rests on three sessions per arm, and under the pre-registered rule (G > k·SE with SE = sqrt(S² + sd_g²/R) and k rising to about 3 when the between-session spread dominates) the bar at the spread the authors' own Adamson arms showed (sd_g 0.035) is about 0.07 in pearson_delta, above every arm-versus-control gain they report (0.01 to 0.05); the paper gives no minimum detectable difference or power statement for R = 3, its only power floor (30 fresh-test targets) bounds the wrong variance term, and it does not say what it will report when every arm reads 'no difference established'.

findings.claim: Of the 38 screen-free unique rows none passes: the CpG feature gains 0.00056 ± 0.00015, below the 0.002 minimum, and fails the perturbation null the first test lacked (pooled p 0.363); ... the step-down over the 38 screen-free rows alone changes nothing.
findings.problem: The cited docs/results/norman_f_corrected_pooled_holm/pooled_holm.json gives 53 unique rows of which 13 carry reads_replogle: true, leaving 40 screen-free unique rows, not 38. The two rows that separate the counts carry screen names but by the record and their committed sources read only gene_annotation; 38 can only come from counting by name, a rule stated nowhere. The conclusion holds at 40, but a number that does not reproduce from its cited source is a must-fix, and it is repeated in two other documents.
