verdict.note: Confirmed on my own count. The record the paper cites defines screen-free as the source not reading replogle2022_k562 (pooled_holm.md:3, tools/block_f_readings.py:136), and by that flag 40 of the 53 unique rows are screen-free, not 38. The two rows that make the difference (e446, e391) are named after the screen but their committed sources read only gene_annotation and the lab's own control means, gene correlations and training deltas, so the flag is right and a name-based count is the only way to reach 38; no document states such a rule, and GOAL_CRITERIA:135 claims every number there was re-derived from the JSON. The finding is right that the conclusion is unaffected: all 40 flag-false rows have found false, and the four with pooled p 0.001 fail the 0.002 minimum gain whatever the subset. Severity: the number does not reproduce from its cited record, in a project whose stated standard is that every number does, and it is repeated in four documents (paper twice, GOAL_CRITERIA twice, ROADMAP, HANDOFF); it must be corrected before submission, but it changes no result, so not reject. The finding's doc_lines understate the spread (GOAL_CRITERIA:147, ROADMAP:355 and HANDOFF:64 also carry it); that is scope, not a misreading. Neither PR #70 nor PR #75 touches the number.
verdict.corrected_fix: In docs/PAPER_COMPARISON.md:308 and :311, docs/GOAL_CRITERIA.md:145 and :147, docs/ROADMAP.md:355 and HANDOFF.md:64, replace 38 with 40 and state the rule once: "Of the 40 screen-free unique rows (the 53 unique rows whose source does not read replogle2022_k562, the record's reads_replogle flag; two of them, screen_delta_times_cds_length_e446 and replogle_additive_x_promoter_cpg_oe_e391, carry screen names but read no screen table) none passes." If the lead's subset step-down was in fact run over 38 rows chosen by name, either rerun it over the 40 flag-false rows and record the output file, or say which 38 rows it used and why; the "changes nothing" conclusion holds either way because the four flag-false rows with pooled p 0.001 all gain below the 0.002 minimum.
verdict.reviewer_sentence: The paper says 38 screen-free unique rows (lines 308 and 311), but the record it cites, norman_f_corrected_pooled_holm/pooled_holm.json, marks 40 of the 53 unique rows reads_replogle false, and the two rows that separate the counts (e446, e391) read no screen table by their committed sources; the conclusion that none passes holds at 40, but the number must be corrected, with the counting rule stated, here and in GOAL_CRITERIA, ROADMAP and HANDOFF where it is repeated.

findings.title: The disclosed deepseek-flash fallback for A3 can never pass session_after
findings.claim: The script refuses the session as passed when no row has status 200, when the served model is not deepseek-v4-pro (or the disclosed deepseek-flash for A3)
findings.problem: The rate card and the proxy's test fixture record that DeepSeek serves deepseek-flash under the legacy name deepseek-chat, and the proxy logs model_served as upstream reports it. session_after compares the served names with the wanted name exactly, so an A3 session with H_A3_MODEL=deepseek-flash logs deepseek-chat, fails the check and stops the block: the fallback the plan and paper disclose is unrunnable as scripted. The plan also still says the fallback reaches the runner as BASELINE_ANTHROPIC_MODEL while the Codex path uses BASELINE_CODEX_MODEL.
findings.evidence: docs/mac/block_h/block_h_common.sh:216 (f"served model {models}, not {want}", bool(calls) and models != [want]); block_h_a3.sh:13 model="${H_A3_MODEL:-deepseek-v4-pro}", :24 env BASELINE_CODEX_MODEL="$model", :31 session_after "$name" a3 "$model"; configs/default.toml:83 'The API serves the legacy name "deepseek-chat" with deepseek-flash.'; tests/test_ledger_proxy.py:84, :426 assert call["model_served"] == "deepseek-chat"; tools/baselines/ledger_proxy.py:421.
findings.fix: Accept the served alias in session_after (want in {deepseek-flash, deepseek-chat} when H_A3_MODEL=deepseek-flash, or compare priced_as), and correct PLAN 162-163 to name BASELINE_CODEX_MODEL for the Codex client.

verdict.evidence_checked: docs/PAPER_COMPARISON.md:355-356 "one LLM, `deepseek-v4-pro`, unless the probe forces the disclosed `deepseek-flash` fallback for A3". docs/PLAN_H_COMPARISON.md:161-164 "if Claude Code rejects the alias, A3 runs on `deepseek-flash` (`H_A3_MODEL`, passed to the runner as `BASELINE_ANTHROPIC_MODEL`) and the difference is disclosed"; :189-190 "refuses the session as passed when no row has status 200, when the served model is not `deepseek-v4-pro` (or the disclosed `deepseek-flash` for A3)"; :155-156 still describes the second probe session as "one one-turn `claude -p` call ... (run id `h_probe_claude`)"; :247-268 (note of 03:52 UTC) makes Codex the A3 client. docs/mac/block_h/block_h_a3.sh:13 `model="${H_A3_MODEL:-deepseek-v4-pro}"`; :24 `agent_run "$name" env BASELINE_CODEX_MODEL="$model" ...`; :28 `agent_run "$name" env BASELINE_ANTHROPIC_MODEL="$model" bash "$TOOLS/run_autoresearch.sh"`; :31 `session_after "$name" a3 "$model"`. tools/baselines/run_codex.sh:89 `BASELINE_CODEX_MODEL="${BASELINE_CODEX_MODEL:-deepseek-v4-pro}"`. block_h_common.sh:211 `models = sorted({str(r.get("model_served") or "?") for r in calls})`; :216 `(f"served model {models}, not {want}", bool(calls) and models != [want])` (an exact compare). tools/baselines/ledger_proxy.py:421 `p.log(route=path, model_requested=requested, model_served=served, priced_as=key, status=200, ...)`; :102-107 price_key prefers the served name. configs/default.toml:83 `# ... The API serves the legacy name "deepseek-chat" with deepseek-flash.` (requests for the legacy name are served by flash; it says nothing about the name reported for a `deepseek-flash` request). tests/test_ledger_proxy.py:84 `served = "deepseek-chat" if model == "deepseek-flash" else model  # the legacy name, as the real API does`; :426 `assert call["model_served"] == "deepseek-chat" and call["priced_as"] == "deepseek-chat"` (a mock's assumption, written for the proxy). docs/archive/records/deepseek_test_2026-10-03.md:6-7 "The API serves `deepseek-chat` requests with `deepseek-flash` and reports that name. `deepseek-flash` was missing from the price table, so the runs priced it at the pessimistic fallback" (the repository's one record of a real response: the API reported `deepseek-flash`). genemila/providers/openai_compat.py:77 default model "deepseek-chat"; :67 `model=data.get("model", self.model)`. genemila/llm.py:114-120 price_key maps requested to served when served is in the table. No committed run record carries a served name for a `deepseek-flash` request (grep of docs/mac and docs/results finds only configured names).
verdict.note: The naming drift stands: step 6 (PLAN 162-163) says the fallback reaches the runner as BASELINE_ANTHROPIC_MODEL and names Claude Code and run id h_probe_claude, while the 03:52 note makes Codex the client and block_h_a3.sh:24 passes BASELINE_CODEX_MODEL to run_codex.sh; the note does not amend that line. The central claim, that the fallback can never pass session_after, does not hold up: the finding reads configs/default.toml:83 backwards (it says a request for the legacy name deepseek-chat is served by deepseek-flash, not that a deepseek-flash request is reported as deepseek-chat), and the only support left is the comment on the test fixture (tests/test_ledger_proxy.py:84), which the repository's one real record contradicts: docs/archive/records/deepseek_test_2026-10-03.md:6-7 says the API answered a deepseek-chat request with the reported name deepseek-flash (which is why the lab's price table gained a deepseek-flash entry). On that record the exact compare at block_h_common.sh:216 would pass with H_A3_MODEL=deepseek-flash. What is true is that the reported name for a flash request is unverified in block H's own records and the probe runs deepseek-v4-pro only, so the fixture's belief, if right, would stop the block after the first fallback session; a one-line alias acceptance removes that risk either way. findings.title: The Docker egress test does not verify that the relay reaches the Mac's loopback proxy
findings.claim: check_tools.sh verifies, with a throwaway listener on the Mac, that a container on genemila_h cannot reach https://api.deepseek.com and can reach the relay. ... if Docker Desktop's host.docker.internal does not reach a 127.0.0.1 listener on this Mac, Docker mode is out and the arms wait.
findings.problem: The script starts the listener, but the test only opens a TCP connection to the relay's port and sends nothing; socat accepts before it dials host.docker.internal, so the test prints 'relay reachable: good' even when the relay cannot reach the host's 127.0.0.1 listener, the one question that decides Docker mode. The failure then shows up in the paid probe as 'no proxy call within 180 s' or a healthz refusal, a stopped block rather than a free NOT STARTED.
findings.evidence: docs/mac/block_h/check_tools.sh:31 "$PY" -m http.server --bind 127.0.0.1 $PORT ... & LISTENER=$!; :33-35 docker run ... TCP-LISTEN:$PORT,fork,reuseaddr TCP:host.docker.internal:$PORT ... alpine/socat -T 5 - TCP:h_relay:$PORT,connect-timeout=5 < /dev/null > /dev/null 2>&1 && echo reachable: good; nothing reads the listener's output.
findings.fix: Send GET /healthz HTTP/1.0 through the relay from the test container and require an HTTP response line from the Mac listener (or run the real proxy on a scratch ledger copy and check its healthz JSON); fail 'Docker mode' otherwise.

verdict.evidence_checked: docs/PLAN_H_COMPARISON.md:92-95: "`check_tools.sh` verifies, with a throwaway listener on the Mac, that a container on `genemila_h` cannot reach `https://api.deepseek.com` and can reach the relay. The proxy listens on the loopback only (it refuses any other address), so if Docker Desktop's `host.docker.internal` does not reach a `127.0.0.1` listener on this Mac, Docker mode is out and the arms wait for the account." -> the plan assigns this check the job of deciding whether the host.docker.internal-to-127.0.0.1 path works. docs/mac/block_h/check_tools.sh:30 "# the egress test: a throwaway listener on the Mac stands in for the proxy; the relay must reach it, the internet must not"; :31 "\"$PY\" -m http.server --bind 127.0.0.1 $PORT > /dev/null 2>&1 & LISTENER=$!"; :33 "docker run -d --rm --name h_relay --network genemila_h alpine/socat TCP-LISTEN:$PORT,fork,reuseaddr TCP:host.docker.internal:$PORT"; :35 the positive test is "docker run --rm --network genemila_h alpine/socat -T 5 - TCP:h_relay:$PORT,connect-timeout=5 < /dev/null > /dev/null 2>&1 && echo reachable: good || echo UNREACHABLE: the proxy route does not work" -> stdin is /dev/null and stdout is discarded: no request is sent and no reply is read; socat's TCP-LISTEN accepts the connection before it opens its second address, so the connect (and exit 0) succeeds whether or not the relay's forward to the Mac's 127.0.0.1 listener works; the listener started on line 31 is never observed. :36 kills the listener; :5 "It does not write isolation.txt: that line is written by hand from Andres's answer". docs/PLAN_H_COMPARISON.md:320-384 (dated notes): none amends lines 92-95 or the egress test. git diff cfa8034 origin/claude/block-h-script-gaps: one commit e5a7fff; diffstat touches PLAN (22 added lines, the 22:00 UTC note on the probe reset and the first-call rate), block_h_a4.sh, block_h_common.sh, block_h_probe.sh, block_h_reset_probe.sh, tests, run_biomni.py; the diff of check_tools.sh is empty and no relay/socat/host.docker line of block_h_common.sh changes; the branch's PLAN lines 92-94 are identical. docs/mac/block_h/block_h_common.sh:99 the production relay is the same one-target socat "TCP-LISTEN:$PORT,fork,reuseaddr TCP:host.docker.internal:$PORT"; :127 "PROXY_URL=\"http://host.docker.internal:$PORT\"" in Docker mode; :148 "docker run --rm --name h_agent --network genemila_h --memory 8g --add-host \"host.docker.internal:$RELAY_IP\""; :30 "read -r MODE ACCOUNT 2> /dev/null < \"$H/isolation.txt\""; :216 "(\"no call reached the proxy\", not calls)" -> PROBLEM -> :223 block_h_stopped.txt. tools/baselines/ledger_proxy.py:57 "- GET /healthz answers {\"ok\": true, ...} with the caps and the spend, so a runner can check the proxy before starting."; :299-304 do_GET, loopback only, /healthz -> 200; :530-532 "raise SystemExit(f\"refusing: {KEY_ENV} is not set in the proxy's environment\")" -> the proxy cannot stand in for the throwaway listener in the key-less check_tools.sh. tools/baselines/run_biomni.py:107-114 session_cap() GETs <proxy>/healthz with a 10 s timeout and returns None on OSError; :146-149 "cap = session_cap(args.proxy) / if cap is None: print(f\"refusing: {args.proxy}/healthz does not answer; start the ledger proxy first\") return 2"; :143 accepts only loopback or http://host.docker.internal. tools/baselines/run_codex.sh:176 and run_autoresearch.sh:94 "HEALTH=$(curl -fsS --max-time 5 \"$PROXY/healthz\") || { echo \"refusing: $PROXY/healthz does not answer\" >&2; exit 2; }". docs/mac/block_h/block_h_probe.sh:16-18 the probe is the first paid command: proxy_up at $0.05 then run_biomni.py --probe (--minutes 2) through agent_run; block_h_chain.sh:16 the chain stops at a failed probe. docs/PLAN_H_COMPARISON.md:137-138 step 2: "bash $L/block_h/check_tools.sh; post its output on #41 ... Then write isolation.txt as above." docs/PAPER_COMPARISON.md: no mention of the relay or the egress test (grep).
verdict.note: The core objection stands and I saw it in the script: the positive half of the egress test (check_tools.sh:35) only completes a TCP connect to the relay's socat listener, which accepts before it opens its forward; nothing is sent through it and nothing is read back, so it prints 'reachable: good' whether or not host.docker.internal reaches the 127.0.0.1 listener started on line 31, which is exactly the condition PLAN 93-95 says this check settles ('Docker mode is out'). The script's own comment (line 30) and failure text ('the proxy route does not work') claim more than the test does. No dated note amends it and PR #70 does not touch check_tools.sh. The finding misreads three details. (1) The consequence is bounded: in Docker mode every runner is pointed at http://host.docker.internal:8787 through the relay (block_h_common.sh:127, :148) and refuses to start within 10 s when <proxy>/healthz does not answer (run_biomni.py:146-149, run_codex.sh:176, run_autoresearch.sh:94), so no session 'runs with no working path and fails every call': the probe, the first paid command, refuses, session_after records 'no call reached the proxy' and stops the block at $0 (and PR #70 adds the reset). The cost of the false 'good' is a misleading #41 report, a stopped block and a dated note, not money or a reading. (2) 'the relay could be misconfigured to reach more than the proxy' has no support: the relay is one socat to one host:port (common.sh:99, check_tools.sh:33), the listener is the loopback-only proxy with four POST routes and /healthz, and the runners refuse any other proxy host; no mechanism is shown and a 'nothing else' test is not specified. (3) The fix is misdirected: the proxy's /healthz exists but the proxy refuses to start without DEEPSEEK_API_KEY (ledger_proxy.py:530-532) and check_tools.sh is the free, key-less step 2, so the positive check there must go through the throwaway http.server; and 'record both results in isolation.txt' conflicts with check_tools.sh:5 and with h_checks parsing that file as 'MODE ACCOUNT' (common.sh:30). Severity 'major' rather than 'reject': no reading or fairness control is affected (the egress-blocked half, the actual control, is tested correctly), but the check that step 2 bases the isolation decision on reports a false positive in the one failure mode the plan names, and the fix is one line that must land before check_tools.sh is run.
verdict.corrected_fix: In docs/mac/block_h/check_tools.sh:35, replace the bare connect to the relay with a request through it and a check of the stand-in's reply, e.g. `printf 'GET / HTTP/1.0\r\n\r\n' | docker run -i --rm --network genemila_h alpine/socat -T 5 - TCP:h_relay:$PORT,connect-timeout=5 2>/dev/null | head -1 | grep -q ' 200 '`, printing 'relay to a 127.0.0.1 listener on the Mac: good' or 'UNREACHABLE: host.docker.internal does not reach a 127.0.0.1 listener on this Mac (plan, Isolation: Docker mode is out)'; keep the api.deepseek.com test as it is. Amend PLAN_H_COMPARISON.md:92-93 to say what is verified: 'cannot reach https://api.deepseek.com and, through the relay, gets an answer from a listener bound to 127.0.0.1 on the Mac'. Optionally, in block_h_common.sh proxy_up (Docker mode), after the proxy listens, run the same GET against /healthz through the relay from a throwaway container before agent_run, so a broken route ends in NOT STARTED rather than a stopped block at the probe. Do not write anything into isolation.txt (check_tools.sh:5; h_checks reads it as `MODE ACCOUNT`): the two results belong in the check_tools.sh output that step 2 posts on #41. Drop the 'reaches nothing else' check: the relay forwards one host:port and no path to more is shown.

The consequence is bounded, since every runner refuses to start when <proxy>/healthz does not answer through that same path (run_biomni.py:146-149, run_codex.sh:176, run_autoresearch.sh:94) and the probe then stops the block at $0, but the free check should send a request through the relay and check the reply, and the plan should state that this is what it verifies.

findings.title: The chain's resume rule fails both ways: a free refusal strands the session and a stopped session has no path past it
findings.claim: A session whose .passed marker exists is skipped, so a pre-session refusal (exit 1 or 2) is fixed and the chain restarted the same way; a stop after a session (block_h_stopped.txt, exit 3) is not resumed until the cause is written up here.
findings.problem: session_dirs creates the work copy and the out directory before proxy_up runs; proxy_up can refuse for free (relay container did not start, proxy did not listen) with nothing spent and no .log, and on the restart session_dirs finds the work copy and refuses the session under its name forever; no script or plan line sanctions deleting the copy. After a stop (exit 3) the session has no .passed marker, so a restarted chain reaches it again and its .log, work copy, out directory and hand-back make the session script refuse it; h_checks refuses everything while block_h_stopped.txt exists and nothing says who deletes it; the only reset (PR #70) covers the probe and refuses an arm's stop. So the plan's own stop rules leave no scripted way to run the sessions after the stopped one, and the improvised ways either count the session as passed or are undocumented.

findings.fix: Start the proxy and relay before session_dirs (or have proxy_up's no remove the untouched $W and $O), and state which files a free refusal may leave and who removes them; define a <session>.stopped marker written by session_after on a stop, let the chain skip such a session (reported as its own arm) once block_h_stopped.txt has been moved into a dated failed/ folder by a reset script as #70 does for the probe, and say in reading 1 that .stopped sessions are excluded from --source.

The improvised ways are a fake .passed (which the chain then counts as passed) or moving the session's files aside and re-running it under its name (which the plan forbids and which loses the 'own arm'). Reading 1 (:211-212) also lists every seed's hand-back although collect_handback runs before the stop decision (:192-193), so a stopped session's hand-back exists and nothing says it is excluded. The finding misreads nothing material. PR #70 closes the gap for the probe only (its reset moves work/out/handback h_probe* aside and refuses an arm's stop). verdict.reviewer_sentence: The chain's resume rule (PLAN 150-152) holds in neither case: a relay or proxy refusal comes after session_dirs has copied the package (block_h_a3.sh:17-19, block_h_common.sh:133-135), so the restart the plan promises is refused forever under the never-repeated rule, and after a stop (exit 3, common.sh:223) no marker lets the chain pass the session, h_checks:55 refuses everything while block_h_stopped.txt exists, nothing says who removes it, and PR #70's reset covers the probe only; the plan's own 'the session becomes its own arm' rule (PLAN 192) therefore has no scripted continuation, and reading 1 (PLAN 211-212) does not say a stopped session's hand-back is left out.

findings.title: The $0.05 probe cap: run_biomni's first-call pre-estimate is skipped in both isolation modes and no rule covers a 402
findings.claim: two proxy sessions of $0.05 each (D6's cap per round; one round of either client is estimated at $0.02 to $0.03, so one $0.05 cap for both would sit at the expected cost) ... a 402 is the proxy's cap, not a route failure, and is read before any fallback is disclosed
findings.problem: The runner's protection against a first call exceeding its cap reads input_cache_miss from configs/default.toml three directories above itself; the image copies only tools/baselines and account mode copies only tools/baselines into /Users/Shared, so the rate is None and the check is silently skipped in both modes (the lead's 19:33 UTC note names this; PR #70 closes it with miss_rate, --miss-usd-per-mtok and rate_source). The probe then relies on the proxy's 402 alone, and the 402 is likely: the Biomni probe makes three calls and the proxy admits a call only while settled spend plus the largest priced call so far stays under the cap, so with v4-pro at $1.32 per million miss tokens a first call above about $0.017 makes the third call a 402, the runner ends with 'cap', exits 1 and the block stops. The plan says how to read that row but not what follows (a larger probe cap is a D6 change, and the reset needs #70).

PR #70 (origin/claude/block-h-script-gaps, e5a7fff): block_h_common.sh adds miss_rate() reading "$C/configs/default.toml" and failing NOT STARTED without an entry; block_h_probe.sh and block_h_a4.sh add "BIOMNI_RATE=$(miss_rate deepseek-v4-pro) || exit 1" and "--miss-usd-per-mtok \"$BIOMNI_RATE\""; run_biomni.py takes the flag first, warns on stderr with no source, records run.json rate_source flag/config/none; new block_h_reset_probe.sh; PLAN note "2026-10-17 22:00 UTC" items 1 and 2; tests/test_block_h_scripts.py:127-187 cover miss_rate and the three rate sources.
verdict.note: One of the finding's three parts holds and two do not. (1) Confirmed at cfa8034: in both isolation modes the runner sits at /lab/tools/baselines (Docker) or $SHARED/tools/baselines (account) with no configs/ beside it, so miss_rate() returns None, the --miss-usd-per-mtok flag is never passed to the child, and the pre-estimate at run_biomni.py:86-94 is silently skipped. But this was already on record (ROADMAP note of 19:33 UTC) and PR #70 closes it exactly as that note asked. (2) Refuted: the proxy's reservation is $0.01 per in-flight call (MIN_RESERVATION_USD), not a sum that "meets or exceeds" $0.05, and it is multiplied by inflight, which is 0 when the first call is checked (the increment at :228-229 follows the check at :219). Biomni is a sequential client, so inflight is 0 at every admission; the reservation can only refuse concurrent calls. With session_spent 0 and h_checks guaranteeing ledger + 2.50 <= CAP, the first call is always admitted at a $0.05 cap: a 402 before any model call cannot come from the proxy's cap logic. The finding also attributes a reservation to PLAN 159-160, which mention none. (3) Mostly refuted: a 402 anywhere in the probe is not an undecided outcome. The child prints BIOMNI_ENDED_BY: cap, the parent returns 1, block_h_probe.sh folds it into AGENT_RC, session_after records 'runner exit code', writes block_h_stopped.txt and returns 3, and no .passed marker is written: the probe is failed and the chain stops; PLAN :160 says how the 402 is read (the cap, not a route failure) and :150-152 that a stop is written up before anything resumes. What cfa8034 lacked was the way to rerun a failed probe, which PR #70's block_h_reset_probe.sh adds. The proposed fix is therefore built on a misreading: 'the reservation plus one call' is $0.01 that never applies to the first call. One residual point of my own, minor: the realistic cap failure is mid-probe (Biomni's retriever call plus two main calls at $1.32/M input against $0.05; the plan's $0.02-0.03 is an estimate, nothing has run), or, now that PR #70 makes the pre-estimate run, a pre-call 'refused' if Biomni's full pre-retrieval system prompt (agent.system_prompt at construction, which the estimate uses; Biomni is not installed here to measure it) reaches about 38k tokens. Either lands as a stop with the probe cap still hardcoded at 0.05 (block_h_probe.sh:16), and neither the plan nor PR #70's note says what the cap becomes on the rerun. A one-line rule would close that.
verdict.corrected_fix: Keep the $0.05 cap and PR #70's rate plumbing. Add one line to PLAN step 6 (or PR #70's note): 'A probe that ends in the proxy's 402 or in run_biomni.py's pre-estimate refusal (ended_by refused, nothing sent) is a sizing failure of the probe cap, not of the route: the dated note records the estimate or the proxy log's settled cost, the probe cap is raised to that figure plus one call in block_h_probe.sh (never above $0.25 without Andres's line), block_h_reset_probe.sh moves the failed probe aside, and the chain reruns it.' Optionally have run_biomni.py print the estimate's source prompt length so the note can cite it. Drop the 'reservation plus one call' wording: the reservation is $0.01 per in-flight call and is zero for the first call of a sequential client.
verdict.reviewer_sentence: The proxy reserves $0.01 per call in flight and the count is zero when the first call is checked (ledger_proxy.py:91, :218-229), so a $0.05 probe cap cannot produce a 402 before any model call, and a 402 or a pre-estimate refusal during the probe already ends it as a stop (run_biomni.py:99-101, :208; block_h_common.sh:171, :223), not as an undecided outcome. The one real gap, the runner's silent skip of the first-call pre-estimate in both isolation modes because configs/default.toml is not beside it, was recorded in the ROADMAP note of 19:33 UTC and is closed by PR #70; what remains is a line saying what the probe cap becomes on a rerun after a cap stop.

findings.title: Account-mode 'home changed' stop rule fires on the venv's own bytecode cache
findings.claim: an agent that touched anything outside its package copy (Docker: impossible by construction; account mode: find -ls of the account's home compared before and after, with the tools' own state, .claude*, .cache, .npm and Library, left out)
findings.problem: In account mode the venv lives inside the account's home and the agent runs without PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE, so the first import of langchain, openai and Biomni's modules during the session writes __pycache__ files into the venv; h_checks's own import biomni warms only part of it before the before-listing is taken. The after-listing then differs, session_after records 'the account's home changed', the first A4 session stops the block and is declared its own arm for a bytecode cache. Benign first-run dotfiles (.matplotlib, .config, .ipython) have the same effect; the prune list does not cover this.

HOME=... But the finding's mechanism is conditional, not certain: pip byte-compiles every installed module at install time (the Dockerfile's own recipe and the repository's only venv recipe use pip), so a pip-built venv gets no new __pycache__ files on first import; the writes occur only for a venv built without bytecode compilation (uv pip install, pip --no-compile), which the plan and check_tools.sh neither require nor exclude because they name the packages but not the installer. Three details are misread: (1) the first account-mode session is the $0.10 probe, which runs the same agent_run and session_after home comparison, not the first A4 session; under PR #70 a probe false-stop is resettable, though a later arm session can still trip on Biomni tool modules first imported during a full session (arm stops have no reset and the name is never reused). (2) .matplotlib, .config and .ipython: nothing in the stated venv (biomni, langchain, langgraph, openai, numpy, scipy, scikit-learn; biomni's declared deps are pydantic, langchain, python-dotenv) installs matplotlib or IPython, a non-interactive python writes no history, and platformdirs on macOS writes under Library (pruned), so the dotfile claim is unsupported. (3) The proposed fix would not work as written: run_biomni.py rebuilds the child's environment from an allowlist, so PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 passed by agent_run never reaches the process that imports Biomni; and pruning $H_ACCOUNT_VENV would hide a real violation (an agent pip-installing into the venv, possible in account mode where the network is open).
verdict.corrected_fix: In home_listing add `-o -name __pycache__` to the prune group (keeps the venv in the comparison, drops bytecode noise regardless of how the venv was built); optionally run the Biomni child with `-B` (run_biomni.py's cmd) rather than relying on an environment variable the allowlist drops. In the plan's stop rule, list the paths left out (`.claude*`, `.cache`, `.npm`, `Library`, `__pycache__`) and name the venv installer (pip, as the Dockerfile) in the account-mode venv instruction. Do not prune $H_ACCOUNT_VENV itself.
verdict.reviewer_sentence: The account-mode 'home changed' stop rule compares a listing that includes the agent's own venv with no bytecode suppression, so a venv built without precompiled bytecode (uv, pip --no-compile) would trip it on first import; with the pip-built venv the plan implies this does not happen, and the $0.10 probe would absorb the first hit, but a one-line `__pycache__` prune in home_listing removes the dependence on the installer and should go in before the chain.

findings.title: The probe marker does not record the client or wire format it cleared
findings.claim: Either way the probe runs the selected client through the proxy once, at $0.05, before any arm.
findings.problem: h_probe.passed is an empty file; the chain, the probe script and block_h_a3.sh skip or require it by existence alone, while A3_CLIENT and H_CODEX_WIRE_API are read from the environment at every start. verdict.note: Confirmed on the files. The marker is literally `touch "$H/h_probe.passed"` (block_h_common.sh:224) and the three places that consult it (chain :15, a3 :15, probe :9) test `-e` only, while the client (`A3_CLIENT`), the wire format (`H_CODEX_WIRE_API`) and the isolation mode are read fresh from the environment and `isolation.txt` on every start (common.sh:11,17,30) and never compared with what the probe ran. The plan itself makes a post-probe switch likely: lines 305-307 name `A3_CLIENT=claude` and `H_CODEX_WIRE_API=responses` as paths "decided before any A3 session", line 384 says "the probe runs again" after a proxy route change, and item 7 (the 400 after the first 200) is left to the operator's reading of `h_probe_codex.jsonl` (probe.sh:53) after `session_after` has already written the marker on exit code plus served model (common.sh:216, 224), so a passed marker and a Codex route the plan calls unfit for A3 can coexist; the restarted chain with `A3_CLIENT=claude` then skips the probe and the first $2.50 A3 session is the first call on the `<proxy>/anthropic` route the plan lists as unverified (lines 155-157), against lines 339-340. Two details the finding overstates: (1) the 03:52 and 04:32 notes cannot have produced a stale marker, since nothing has run on the Mac (PLAN:289); they show how often the route moves, not an actual stale marker; (2) the client and wire format are not wholly unrecorded, the proxy log's name (`h_probe_codex.jsonl` vs `h_probe_claude.jsonl`) and the runner's `run.json` (`client`, `wire_api`, `codex_bin`, run_codex.sh:245-248) keep them; what is missing is any comparison with the current configuration, and the Codex version and image are recorded nowhere (Dockerfile:13 unpinned; check_tools.sh:10 prints the version to the console only; run.json has no version). Not "reject": the per-session guards (the first-proxy-line rule run_codex.sh:203-225, the served-model check common.sh:216, `run.json["client"]`) bound the damage to one session and keep the arm labelled, so no reading becomes invalid; but the block's own stated precondition can be bypassed silently, and PR #70's reset script refuses to clear a passed probe (reset_probe.sh:16), so the operator has no documented way to force the re-probe the plan promises.
verdict.corrected_fix: In `session_after` (block_h_common.sh:224), for the probe write one line into `h_probe.passed` instead of touching it: the runner commit (`git -C "$C" rev-parse HEAD`), `MODE`, `A3_CLIENT`, `H_CODEX_WIRE_API` (when codex), and the client build: in account mode `"$CODEX_BIN" --version` (or `claude --version`), in docker mode `docker image inspect -f '{{.Id}}' genemila-h`. Factor that line into a `probe_stamp` function in block_h_common.sh, and have both `block_h_chain.sh:15` and `block_h_a3.sh:15` compare `probe_stamp` with the marker's content: the chain reruns the probe on a mismatch (after moving the passed probe's files aside, since probe.sh:10, session_dirs and proxy_up refuse to overwrite; so let `block_h_reset_probe.sh:16` accept a passed probe whose stamp differs from the current one, naming the plan note that records the switch), and `block_h_a3.sh` refuses with `NOT STARTED` on a mismatch so an arm started by hand cannot bypass it. While there, make the probe enforce item 7 before the marker is written (codex: at least two status-200 rows and no 400 in `h_probe_codex.jsonl`, in the check heredoc at common.sh:194-219 or a probe-only check), so "passed" means what the plan says. Add one sentence at PLAN step 5 (line 150): a change of `A3_CLIENT`, `H_CODEX_WIRE_API`, the isolation mode or the client build after a passed probe makes the chain run the probe again.
verdict.reviewer_sentence: The probe's `.passed` marker is an empty file (`touch` in `session_after`, block_h_common.sh:224) and the chain and the A3 script test only that it exists (block_h_chain.sh:15, block_h_a3.sh:15), while the client, wire format and isolation mode the probe exercised are taken from the environment at probe time (block_h_probe.sh:38-47, block_h_common.sh:11,17,30) and compared with nothing afterwards; after the client or wire-format switch the plan itself foresees (lines 305-307, 384) a restarted chain skips the probe and the first $2.50 A3 session is the first call on a route the probe never touched, against the plan's own rule at lines 339-340. PR #70 does not close this: its reset script refuses to touch a passed probe (block_h_reset_probe.sh:16), so the only way to re-probe after a switch is an undocumented `rm` of the marker.

findings.title: Abstract counts four LLM arms; Table 1 has five

findings.problem: Table 1 and the Methods list five LLM-driven arms with three sessions each (A1, A1-ablation, A2, A3, A4); the abstract's enumeration omits the ablation and then says 'four LLM arms'.
findings.evidence: PAPER 111 'The lab arms (A1, A1-ablation, A2 and C0)'; PAPER 256-260 rows A1 (G1), A1-ablation (G0), A2, A3, A4 each '3'; PLAN 24-25 A1 and A1-ablation as separate rows.

DeepSeek planner `deepseek-v4-pro`, 4 `deepseek-flash` workers, 20 min' ; :25 '| A1-ablation | block G's g0 runs, `runs/adamson_cf_g0_ds_w4_r{0,2,3}`, the same bundle without the three tables | not re-run | paid in G |' ; :208 '--source-run A1abl_r0=<MAIN>/runs/adamson_cf_g0_ds_w4_r0 ...' -> the plan scores the ablation as its own arm. docs/PLAN_G_CLEAN_ARM.md:38 '12 runs: `runs/<ds>_g1_ds_w4_r<S>` and `runs/<ds>_g0_ds_w4_r<S>`.' ; :40 '`deepseek-v4-pro`, 4 `deepseek-flash` workers, 20 minutes, fresh start' -> the g0 runs are three 20-minute DeepSeek sessions, so the ablation is an LLM arm on the abstract's own definition. PLAN dated notes (lines 247-end) and the 'To be filled in' list (235-246): nothing amends the arm count. PR #70 (origin/claude/block-h-script-gaps, commit e5a7fff): git diff cfa8034..branch touches only docs/PLAN_H_COMPARISON.md (+22 lines, the 22:00 UTC note on block_h_reset_probe.sh and run_biomni.py's miss rate); docs/PAPER_COMPARISON.md is unchanged.
verdict.note: Confirmed. The abstract's enumeration omits A1-ablation and then states 'The four LLM arms ran three 20-minute sessions each', while the Methods (line 111), the block-G paragraph (line 331), Table 1 (rows 256-260) and the plan (PLAN 24-25, 208) treat A1-ablation as a fifth LLM arm with three 20-minute DeepSeek sessions (PLAN_G 38-40), which is exactly what the abstract's sentence describes. The finding's citations all hold. Two details it did not mention: (1) the abstract's total is still a placeholder '[N arms; ...]', so the author left the overall count open but wrote 'four' definitively in the next sentence; (2) the paper is itself split on the convention, since the arm bullet at line 120 folds the ablation under A1's bullet while lines 111, 331 and Table 1 give it its own place, so the fix must choose one convention and apply it at all four sites, not just the abstract. Severity minor: it is wording in a template draft with placeholders, not a flaw in the plan or the reading; but a reviewer will catch a count that disagrees with the paper's own table. PR #70 does not touch the paper.
verdict.corrected_fix: Pick one convention and apply it everywhere. Either (a) count the ablation as an arm: in the abstract write 'this lab with four workers, with and without the three per-gene tables, and with one worker' and 'The five LLM arms ran three 20-minute sessions each on one LLM', and give A1-ablation its own bullet in the Methods list (line 120) as Table 1 (line 257), line 111 and PLAN 25 already do; or (b) treat it as a lab row under A1: keep 'four LLM arms' but say so once ('A1 also has an ablation row, the same runs without the tables, G0'), and indent or rename the Table 1 row as a sub-row of A1 and amend line 111 to match. In both cases resolve the '[N arms]' placeholder at line 18 to the same count (seven scored rows under convention (a): five LLM arms, C0 and C2; plus P0 as reference and CellForge-Models as not comparable).
verdict.reviewer_sentence: The abstract enumerates four LLM arms and says 'The four LLM arms ran three 20-minute sessions each', but Table 1 and the Methods list five LLM-driven arms with three sessions each (A1, A1-ablation, A2, A3, A4); the ablation is folded under A1 in the Methods bullet yet counted separately at line 111, line 331 and in the table. State one count and use it in the abstract, the Methods and Table 1.

findings.title: The $2.50 caps are not the same cap: split and paced in the lab, one pool for a package agent
findings.claim: PAPER 21-22: 'the package arms under a $2.50 session cap and the lab arms under the lab's own per-run caps'; PAPER 92-94: 'per-run caps of $1.00 for the workers and $1.50 for the planner, enforced by the lab, and the shared ledger'.
findings.problem: A lab run cannot move money between roles and the planner's allowance is paced over the run, while a package agent may spend its whole $2.50 on one model at any time. B.1 asks for the same dollar cap; the totals match but the constraints do not, and the paper does not say so.
findings.evidence: docs/mac/block_h/block_h_a2.sh:53 --set budget.max_total_usd=1.0 --set budget.max_planner_usd=1.5; genemila/controller.py:163-166 allowed = gw.role_caps["planner"] * min(1.0, (elapsed + 900) / max(1.0, self.seconds)); docs/mac/block_h/block_h_a3.sh:19 proxy_up "$name" 2.50.
findings.fix: One sentence at PAPER 93-94: 'equal in total ($2.50) but split by role and paced for the planner in the lab; one pool for a package agent'.

verdict.evidence_checked: docs/PAPER_COMPARISON.md:21-22 "the package arms under a $2.50 session cap and the lab arms under the lab's own per-run caps". docs/PAPER_COMPARISON.md:92-94 "per-run caps of $1.00 for the workers and $1.50 for the planner, enforced by the lab, and the shared ledger" (the $2.50 total, the role split and the pacing are not contrasted with the package's single pool anywhere in the paper). docs/GOAL_CRITERIA.md:35-36 "three search seeds each, same wall time and dollar cap". docs/FEATURE_COMPARISON_PROTOCOL.md:110 "3. **Same budget.** Same wall clock (20 min, as B2 and B4) and the same dollar cap." docs/PLAN_H_COMPARISON.md:26 "caps `budget.max_total_usd=1.0`, `budget.max_planner_usd=1.5`"; :122-124 "the proxy's `--session-cap-usd 2.50` ... A2 passes `--set budget.cumulative_usd.deepseek=<cap>` with its two run caps"; :190 "when the ledger delta exceeds $2.50". docs/mac/block_h/block_h_a2.sh:53 "--set budget.max_total_usd=1.0 --set budget.max_planner_usd=1.5 --no-watchdog"; :62 '[ "$(echo "$cost <= 2.50" | bc)" = 1 ] || stop="$stop cost \$$cost over \$2.50;"' (the lab run's total is checked against $2.50 after the fact). docs/mac/block_h/block_h_a3.sh:19 'proxy_up "$name" 2.50'. genemila/llm.py:81 'self.role_caps = {"worker": float(b["max_total_usd"]), "planner": planner_cap}'; :170-173 'if self.spent[role] + wc > self.role_caps[role]: self.halted[role] = (f"{role} budget ${self.role_caps[role]:.4f} reached ... no new {role} API calls")' (each role halts on its own cap; nothing moves money between roles). configs/default.toml:68 "max_total_usd = 0.25  # hard cap on worker-LLM spend in one run". genemila/controller.py:163-166 'elapsed = time.time() - (self.started or time.time())' / 'allowed = gw.role_caps["planner"] * min(1.0, (elapsed + 900) / max(1.0, self.seconds))' / 'if gw.spent["planner"] + gw.reserved["planner"] >= allowed: return  # pace the planner budget over the run instead of spending it all early and halting' (for a 1200 s run: 0.75 × $1.50 = $1.125 allowed at t = 0, the full $1.50 from t = 300 s). docs/PAPER_COMPARISON.md:222 "B2's three Norman runs cost $1.29, $1.37 and $1.19"; docs/results/scaling.md:25-26 DeepSeek-planner four-worker runs: worker $0.520 ± 0.018, planner $0.684 ± 0.084 (neither role cap bound in the comparable runs). PR #70 diff: PAPER_COMPARISON.md untouched; PLAN_H gains only the 22:00 UTC note on the probe reset and the first-call rate.
verdict.note: The objection stands: the lab's $2.50 is two independent role caps ($1.00 workers, $1.50 planner) that halt separately (llm.py:81, 170-173) with no transfer, while a package session is one $2.50 pool at the proxy (a3.sh:19), and the paper says "the lab's own per-run caps" (21-22) and gives the split (92-94) without stating that the totals match or that the constraints differ; B.1 and protocol control 3 say "the same dollar cap". One detail is overstated: "paced over the run" echoes the code comment, but the formula is a 900-second head start, so in the block's 20-minute runs 75 % of the planner cap ($1.125) is available from the first second and all of it from minute five; it is not spread across the run. Two things bound the practical effect and belong in the sentence: the split constrains the lab, not the package, so it is a disclosure point rather than an advantage for the lab; and in the comparable runs neither role cap bound (B2 at $1.19 to $1.37 total, PAPER:222; DeepSeek-planner four-worker runs at about $0.52 worker plus $0.68 planner, scaling.md:25-26), so the caps are unlikely to shape the search. Minor: one sentence fixes it.
verdict.corrected_fix: At PAPER:93-94, after "enforced by the lab, and the shared ledger": "The two caps sum to the package arms' $2.50, but the constraint differs: a lab run cannot move money between its planner and its workers, and the planner may spend at most three quarters of its cap in the first five minutes (`genemila/controller.py`, `_maybe_plan`), while a package agent draws its whole $2.50 from one pool at any time; in the comparable runs neither lab cap bound (B2 $1.19 to $1.37 per run). Block H checks every lab run's total against the same $2.50 after it ends (`block_h_a2.sh`)." Optionally the same clause in PLAN_H Money (118-126) and in GOAL_CRITERIA B.1 ("same dollar cap in total").
verdict.reviewer_sentence: The paper calls the dollar cap the same across arms, but the lab's $2.50 is two separate caps ($1.00 workers, $1.50 planner, the planner's three-quarters available in the first five minutes) that cannot be pooled, while a package agent spends one $2.50 pool freely; the totals match, the constraints do not, and the Methods should say so in one sentence.

findings.fix: Add a ΔM6 column to Table 1 (source: feature_compare.json), or state in the caption that M6 is in the JSON and why it is left out.

findings.title: best() excludes ensembles, unlike the paper's description of selection
findings.claim: 'keeps every completed experiment and calls the highest selection score the best (genemila/db.py, best())'; 'The lab keeps every completed experiment and picks the highest combined score'
findings.problem: best() returns the highest-scoring completed experiment that is not an ensemble, while the headline finalist can be an ensemble kept on the visible set; the sentence does not match the function it cites, and the results index reports ensembles as headline finalists.
findings.evidence: genemila/db.py:203-206 "SELECT * FROM experiments WHERE status='completed' AND primary_score IS NOT NULL AND COALESCE(kind, '') != 'ensemble' ORDER BY primary_score DESC, finished_at ASC LIMIT 1"; configs/default.toml:118 ensemble = true; docs/results/scaling.md:3.
findings.fix: 'calls the highest selection score among single models the best (best(), ensembles excluded); an average of the top final.top_k finalists is tried and kept as the headline finalist only when it wins on the visible set'.

findings.title: 'program.md as the whole prompt' ignores each client's own system prompt
findings.claim: PAPER 99: 'and program.md as the whole prompt (tools/task_package/program.md)'; PLAN 255: 'the task package, program.md as the whole prompt'.
findings.problem: Biomni's A1 wraps the task in its own system prompt (the runner logs its length, typically thousands of characters), Codex adds the CLI's built-in instructions and tool definitions, and the lab's workers get WORKER_SYSTEM plus the task text. program.md is the task prompt, not the whole prompt, and the surrounding instructions differ by client.
findings.evidence: tools/baselines/run_biomni.py:83-85 n_chars = len(agent.system_prompt) / print(f"biomni A1 ready: ... system prompt {n_chars} chars"; tools/baselines/run_codex.sh:157-158 (program.md on stdin; Codex's system prompt is the CLI's); genemila/prompts.py:121-124 WORKER_SYSTEM.
findings.fix: Write 'program.md as the task prompt; each client adds its own system prompt (Biomni's length is logged; Codex's is the CLI's built-in instructions and tool schema; the lab's workers get WORKER_SYSTEM)' in PAPER 99 and PLAN 255.

findings.title: 'Wins on more than half' is a majority filter, not a test
findings.claim: wins on more than half the perturbations; a gain outside the targets; mse_top not significantly worse
findings.problem: The code counts strict wins and asks for more than n/2 with ties excluded; at n = 50 that is 26 wins, which under no effect happens about 44 percent of the time, so the condition carries almost no evidence and no error rate. 'A gain outside the targets' is a point estimate above zero. Both are listed beside the 2·SE and permutation tests as if they were tests.
findings.evidence: genemila/benchmark/evaluator.py:178-179 wins_a, wins_b = int((diff > 0).sum()), int((diff < 0).sum()) / verdict = "a" if mean > 2 * se and wins_a > n / 2; tools/feature_compare.py:941-942 if not m2.get("mean_diff", -1.0) > 0: failed.append("no M2 gain").
findings.fix: Call the wins and M2 conditions 'direction-consistency filters with no error rate' where the verdict is described, or replace wins by a sign test at a stated level.

findings.title: 'Equal feedback' overstates: package agents read the labels, lab workers see nothing
findings.claim: So every arm gets the feedback the lab's agents get, and every arm's final scoring is still out of fold on new fold seeds (B.2) and then the fresh test.
findings.problem: The lab's workers see the API, an example and summaries, never a label; only the planner sees aggregate scores. A package agent can open harness/val1.npz and read the 17 validation profiles. The direction favours the foreign arms and no reported number is contaminated, but 'the feedback the lab's agents get' and 'equal feedback' (D5) do not describe what each side could see.
findings.evidence: tools/task_package/program.md:73-77 'The file is readable from your shell'; tools/export_task_package.py:19-25 'harness/val1.npz ... the labels the lab's own controller scores every experiment on'; PAPER 86-87; genemila/lab.py:96 self._val1 = LabelSet.load(...) (controller side only).
findings.fix: Replace 'the feedback the lab's agents get' with 'at least the feedback the lab's controller uses: the same combined score, plus the labels themselves, which the lab's workers never see', and list the asymmetry under Limitations.

findings.title: A1-ablation ran on a different bundle than the package; 'share one bundle' is inexact
findings.claim: PAPER 111: 'Two kinds of arm share one bundle, one split, one clock and one final scoring.' PLAN 25: 'A1-ablation | block G's g0 runs ..., the same bundle without the three tables'.
findings.problem: The G0 runs searched on data/adamson_cf_clean (five knowledge files) while the package and every other arm come from data/adamson_cf_clean_tables (eight). Rescoring on the tables bundle is harmless for features that read no table, but the row's search saw less knowledge, so fairness control 1 does not hold for it.
findings.evidence: docs/PLAN_G_CLEAN_ARM.md:35-36 'G1 (tables): run.data_dir=data/<ds>_clean_tables. G0 (no tables): data/<ds>_clean'; docs/PLAN_H_COMPARISON.md:205-208 (G0 runs scored with --data .../adamson_cf_clean_tables).
findings.fix: Say 'the same split; A1-ablation searched on the bundle without the three tables and is rescored on the tables bundle' and mark the row as an ablation outside fairness control 1.

findings.title: Package sessions share fixed fold seeds 0,1,2; lab runs use their run seed
findings.claim: PLAN 32-33: 'Seeds 0, 2 and 3 everywhere (B2's and G's). A coding agent has no seed: for A3 and A4 the seed names the session'.
findings.problem: The package is exported once with the exporter's default fold seeds 0, 1 and 2, so all A3 and A4 sessions select on identical folds and their repeats vary only in the agent's sampling, whereas lab runs r0, r2 and r3 each select on their own fold seed (cv_seed = run.seed). 'Three seeds' means different things for the two kinds of arm.
findings.evidence: tools/export_task_package.py:173 --fold-seeds default "0,1,2"; docs/PLAN_H_COMPARISON.md:39 (export command without --fold-seeds); tools/task_package/evaluate.py:344 seeds from manifest["fold_seeds"]; genemila/lab.py:105 self.cv_seed = int(cfg["run"].get("seed", 0) or 0), :480.
findings.fix: State in PLAN (seeds paragraph) and PAPER 113-114 that package sessions share fold seeds 0, 1, 2 while each lab run selects on fold seed = its run seed, so package repeats measure agent variation only.

findings.title: Paper names two different A3 fallbacks: Claude Code (Methods) and deepseek-flash (Limitations), the latter stale
findings.claim: PAPER 124-125: 'Claude Code is the disclosed fallback and run.json["client"] records which ran.'; PAPER 356: 'one LLM, deepseek-v4-pro, unless the probe forces the disclosed deepseek-flash fallback for A3'; PLAN 305-307: the two paths for a Codex failure are the /v1/responses route or 'A3 falls back to Claude Code'.
findings.problem: Under the Codex default the plan's dated notes pre-register two fallbacks that keep the LLM (the responses route, or the Claude Code client); the deepseek-flash model fallback belonged to the Claude-client path of the original text (if Claude Code rejects the alias). The Limitations name only the model fallback and the Methods only the client fallback, so a reader cannot tell what 'one LLM' may become; the Limitations are stale relative to the plan's notes of 03:52 and 04:32 UTC and Methods 123-127.
findings.evidence: docs/mac/block_h/block_h_a3.sh:10 '# H_A3_MODEL=deepseek-flash only after the probe showed that the client rejects the alias', :13; tools/baselines/run_codex.sh:245 "client": "codex"; docs/PLAN_H_COMPARISON.md:161-163, :299-307 ('In both the LLM and the rest are unchanged'), :348.
findings.fix: PAPER 356: 'unless the probe forces a disclosed fallback for A3: Claude Code as the client on the same LLM (or the responses route); deepseek-flash as the model only on the Claude-client path (PLAN_H, step 6 and notes of 03:52 and 04:32 UTC)'; in PLAN 189-190 state which fallbacks apply to which client.

findings.title: An A3 session can end early on 'solution' and still pass as a full session
findings.claim: PAPER 130: 'A session can end on <solution> before the clock ...; ended_by is logged (tools/baselines/run_biomni.py).'; PLAN 189-190: the pass rule (status 200, served model, ledger delta, exit code).
findings.problem: The Codex and Claude Code runners also record ended_by=solution whenever the client exits 0 before the clock, and such a session passes the chain's checks, so a two-minute A3 session counts as one of the arm's three 20-minute sessions. The paper discloses early ends for Biomni only, and no rule says how a short session is read.
findings.evidence: tools/baselines/run_codex.sh:230-231 ENDED_BY="error" / if [ "$CODE" = 124 ]; then ENDED_BY="timeout"; elif [ "$CODE" = 0 ]; then ENDED_BY="solution"; fi, :255; tools/baselines/run_autoresearch.sh:149-150; docs/mac/block_h/block_h_common.sh:170-171 (stop only on a non-zero runner exit); tools/task_package/program.md:123 'NEVER STOP'.
findings.fix: Extend PAPER 130 to A3 and add to PLAN's pass rule: a session that ends on 'solution' before 20 minutes counts as one of the three, its wall minutes go in Table 1, and it is never rerun.

verdict.evidence_checked: tools/baselines/run_codex.sh:230-231 'ENDED_BY="error"' / 'if [ "$CODE" = 124 ]; then ENDED_BY="timeout"; elif [ "$CODE" = 0 ]; then ENDED_BY="solution"; fi'; :251 '"wall_s": round(time.time() - float(started), 1)'; :255 '[ "$ENDED_BY" = "timeout" ] || [ "$ENDED_BY" = "solution" ]' (the runner's exit status). tools/baselines/run_autoresearch.sh:149-150 and :168 identical. docs/mac/block_h/block_h_common.sh:170-171 'stop=""' / '[ "$AGENT_RC" = 0 ] || stop="$stop runner exit code $AGENT_RC;"'; :224 'touch "$H/$name.passed"; echo "SESSION_DONE $name rc=0"'; :133 'no "$W, $O or $H/handback/$1 exists: a session is never repeated under its name"'. docs/PLAN_H_COMPARISON.md:150-151 'A session whose `.passed` marker exists is skipped'; :169 'the agent for 20 minutes, the runner's own clock (`--minutes 20`)'; :189-190 'refuses the session as passed when no row has status 200, when the served model is not `deepseek-v4-pro` ..., when the ledger delta exceeds $2.50, or when the runner's exit code is not 0' (no wall-time term); :221 'per arm also the sessions' minutes, calls, tokens, served model and spend from the proxy logs'; :217-218 a session with no kept feature is a parent-score row; the dated notes at 247-384 say nothing on session length. docs/PAPER_COMPARISON.md:123-124 'editing one feature file and running `python evaluate.py` until the clock kills it'; :130 'A session can end on `<solution>` before the clock, so the equal wall clock holds only approximately; `ended_by` is logged (`tools/baselines/run_biomni.py`)'; :254 Table 1 column 'minutes, calls, tokens, $'; :259 'A3 autoresearch-style (Codex) | 3 | ... | [proxy log]'. docs/FEATURE_COMPARISON_PROTOCOL.md:50 '`results.tsv`, "never stop" until the wall clock kills it'; :74-75 'Wall clock: Biomni stops at `<solution>`, not by a timer ... the "same wall clock" control holds only approximately.' tools/task_package/program.md:123 '**NEVER STOP**: once the loop has begun, do not pause to ask whether to continue.' tools/baselines/collect_handback.py:118 copies ended_by and minutes into the hand-back manifest. PR #70 (e5a7fff): no change to run_codex.sh, run_autoresearch.sh, block_h_common.sh's session_after, the PLAN's pass rule or the PAPER.
verdict.note: Confirmed. `codex exec` and `claude -p` are single non-interactive turns that end whenever the model stops calling tools, so for A3 an end before 20 minutes is the ordinary way a session ends, not a rare case; both runners then record ended_by=solution and exit 0, the chain writes `.passed` and refuses to repeat the session, and no sentence in the PLAN or PAPER says how such a session is counted. PAPER 123-124 asserts the opposite ('until the clock kills it'), the early-end caveat at 130 names Biomni only, and program.md:123's NEVER STOP is prompt text the client does not enforce. One nuance the finding's fix overlooks: the wall minutes are already reported, in reading 2 (PLAN 221) and in Table 1's last column (PAPER 254, 259, from the proxy log), and run.json carries wall_s and ended_by for A3 too (run_codex.sh:251-252; collect_handback.py:118), so that item is in place; what is missing is the A3 disclosure in the PAPER and the explicit counting/no-rerun rule in the PLAN. Wording and disclosure, hence minor.
verdict.corrected_fix: PAPER 123-124: replace 'until the clock kills it' with 'until the clock kills it or the client's single turn ends on a final message; `ended_by` and `wall_s` are logged (run_codex.sh, run_autoresearch.sh)', and extend the caveat at 130 to A3. PLAN, the pass rule at 189-190: add 'a session that ends on `solution` before 20 minutes passes, counts as one of the arm's three, is never rerun (`session_dirs` refuses the name), and is read with its agent minutes in Table 1 and `ended_by` in the hand-back manifest.' The minutes column already exists (PLAN 221, PAPER 254); no new column is needed.
verdict.reviewer_sentence: A3's sessions are described as running 'until the clock kills it' (PAPER 123-124), yet both A3 runners record ended_by=solution and exit 0 whenever the client's single non-interactive turn ends before 20 minutes (run_codex.sh:231,255; run_autoresearch.sh:150,168), the chain passes such a session and never repeats it (block_h_common.sh:171,224,133), and the early-end caveat at PAPER 130 names Biomni only. State for A3 that a session ending on the client's final message counts as one of the three, is never rerun, and is read with its minutes from Table 1.

findings.title: A keep written by an evaluation that outlives the clock can enter the hand-back
findings.claim: PLAN 169-170: 'the agent for 20 minutes, the runner's own clock (--minutes 20), with a hard stop at 30 minutes from the script'; PLAN 215-216: 'The package arms' candidate set is runs/kept/features/ at the kill'.
findings.problem: The runners kill the agent's process group at 20 minutes, but evaluate.py runs its scoring in a child started with start_new_session=True under a kernel CPU limit of eval_timeout_s (600 s), so an evaluation in flight at the kill survives it and writes the kept state when it finishes. collect_handback.py reads runs/kept/features after the runner returns, so a keep completed after the clock counts, and the pre-session checks look for no orphan evaluate.py. The lab terminates its experiments 30 s after the deadline.
findings.evidence: tools/task_package/evaluate.py:52-53 'The evaluation also gets eval_timeout_s CPU seconds as a kernel limit, so it ends even when this process is killed', :190-192 run_limited(...), :388-396 finish(); genemila/sandbox.py:129 preexec_fn=_limits(ram_mb, cpu_s), start_new_session=True; tools/baselines/run_codex.sh:187-193 os.killpg(p.pid, sig); run_biomni.py:181-184; docs/mac/block_h/block_h_common.sh:191-193, :56-60; genemila/controller.py:339-357.
findings.fix: In session_after or collect_handback.py, record the mtime of runs/kept/scores.json and the last results.tsv row against run.json["ended"]; exclude and list a keep written after it; add evaluate.py to the pre-session pgrep and, in account mode, kill the session's orphan evaluations before collection.

findings.title: The Biomni merge fallback has no knob in the scripts
findings.claim: If deepseek-v4-pro rejects Biomni's consecutive assistant messages, one disclosed rerun with the proxy merging them follows
findings.problem: proxy_up passes a fixed flag list and no variable adds --merge-consecutive-assistant, so the disclosed rerun requires editing block_h_common.sh on the Mac between the probe and the rerun, which the plan's 'a change is a dated note, never an edit' rule does not cover for scripts, and nothing in the session record says whether merging was on except the proxy's start row.
findings.evidence: docs/mac/block_h/block_h_common.sh:104-105 ledger_proxy.py --listen ... --log "$PROXY_LOG_FILE" (no merge flag); tools/baselines/ledger_proxy.py:554-556 ap.add_argument("--merge-consecutive-assistant", action="store_true", ...); docs/ROADMAP.md:277-279.
findings.fix: Add H_MERGE_ASSISTANT=0|1 to block_h_common.sh, forwarded to proxy_up and printed in the progress line and the check file.

verdict.evidence_checked: docs/mac/block_h/block_h_common.sh:104-106 `"$PY" "$C/tools/baselines/ledger_proxy.py" --listen 127.0.0.1:$PORT --upstream https://api.deepseek.com --ledger "$LEDGER" --run-id "$1" --session-cap-usd "$2" --block-cap-usd "$CAP" --log "$PROXY_LOG_FILE"` (fixed flag list; `grep -n merge docs/mac/block_h/*.sh` finds only the probe's comment at block_h_probe.sh:14). tools/baselines/ledger_proxy.py:554-556 `ap.add_argument("--merge-consecutive-assistant", action="store_true", help="OpenAI route: join adjacent assistant messages into one ...")`; :326-328 `if kind == "openai" and p.merge_assistant and isinstance(req.get("messages"), list): req["messages"], merged = merge_consecutive_assistant(req["messages"])`; :419-420 `if merged: extra["merged_messages"] = merged` (per-request record); :567-568 start row `merge_consecutive_assistant=proxy.merge_assistant`. block_h_common.sh:194-218 session_after's check script prints calls, minutes, tokens, cost, served models and other statuses; nothing about merging. PLAN:7 `a change is a new dated section at the end, never an edit`; PLAN:71-72 `If that branch changes before it lands, the scripts change with it in a dated note.`; PLAN:130 `the scripts copied to $L/block_h/` (the Mac runs copies outside git); PLAN:160-161 `If Biomni's route fails with the proxy's message merging, A4 is reported as "could not run on DeepSeek v4-pro"`; PAPER:131-132 `If deepseek-v4-pro rejects Biomni's consecutive assistant messages, one disclosed rerun with the proxy merging them follows`; ROADMAP:277-279 `it runs first without the proxy's --merge-consecutive-assistant option; if the route rejects ..., one rerun with the option, disclosed in the arm's report`. PR #70 branch block_h_common.sh:120-122: proxy_up's flag list unchanged; no merge variable added.
verdict.note: The core objection stands: the paper, the plan and the roadmap all promise a disclosed rerun with the proxy merging Biomni's consecutive assistant messages, and the scripts have no switch for it; proxy_up's flag list is fixed, so the rerun means editing the Mac's copy of block_h_common.sh under $L/block_h/, which is outside git. Two details are misread. First, the session record does say whether merging was on, and better than the finding allows: the proxy's start row carries `merge_consecutive_assistant` and every forwarded request that was merged carries `merged_messages` (ledger_proxy.py:419-420), so the proxy log is a per-call record; what is missing is only that session_after's check file does not surface it. Second, the plan's 'never an edit' rule is about the plan text, and the plan already provides for script changes by commit plus dated note (line 71-72), so the gap is the absence of a pre-registered knob rather than a rule that forbids the change. Not closed by PR #70.
verdict.corrected_fix: Add `H_MERGE_ASSISTANT=${H_MERGE_ASSISTANT:-0}` to block_h_common.sh, append `--merge-consecutive-assistant` in proxy_up when it is 1, include its value in the progress.md start line and in h_checks's `ok:` line, and make session_after's check script print the start row's `merge_consecutive_assistant` and the sum of `merged_messages` over the status-200 rows so the check file records it. The probe's rerun (after block_h_reset_probe.sh) then runs with `H_MERGE_ASSISTANT=1` in the chain's environment and the dated note names it; the plan's probe paragraph should say so.
verdict.reviewer_sentence: The disclosed rerun with message merging that the paper (line 131), the plan (lines 160-161) and the roadmap (D6) promise has no switch in the block H scripts: proxy_up passes a fixed flag list, so the rerun would require editing the Mac's untracked copy of block_h_common.sh between the probe and the rerun; the proxy log does record merging per call (start row and `merged_messages`), but the session check file does not, so an `H_MERGE_ASSISTANT` variable printed in the check file would close the gap.

findings.title: STATE's exclusion rests on a training-data claim the VERIFIED mark does not cover
findings.claim: STATE (Adduri et al., 2025) is out: its public weights were trained on the Replogle K562 screen that the fresh test uses (D9).
findings.problem: The literature check's VERIFIED mark is for the bioRxiv abstract fetch; the training-data sentence is asserted without a source (model card, data manifest or paper section), and ROADMAP D9 marks STATE's licence and CPU inference unverified without marking this. A reviewer who knows STATE's corpora will ask which checkpoint and release.
findings.evidence: docs/CANDIDATE_LITERATURE_CHECK.md:118-121 'VERIFIED, https://api.biorxiv.org/details/... Trained on Replogle K562 among others, so it cannot be a fair row'; docs/FEATURE_COMPARISON_PROTOCOL.md:98 '(per the clone; CPU training unverified)'.
findings.fix: Cite the STATE release (checkpoint name and the training-data statement's location) beside the sentence, or mark the claim UNVERIFIED and say the exclusion is precautionary.

findings.title: SE_adj citation points at the wrong implementation
findings.claim: SE_adj is the paired standard error widened by the perturbations' target-gene overlap (tools/sealed_reading.py)
findings.problem: The fair test uses its own overlap_ratio, computed on the same tier's differences and floored at 1; sealed_reading.py estimates the ratio on the visible validation labels and the arm reading applies it to the sealed SE. The formulas match, the inputs do not.
findings.evidence: tools/feature_compare.py:484-493 overlap_ratio(diff, genes_of) ... 'the core of tools/sealed_reading.py _cluster_ratio'; :507-508 se_adj = s["se"] * max(1.0, ratio or 1.0); tools/sealed_reading.py:98-99 'estimated on visible labels only'.
findings.fix: Cite tools/feature_compare.py, overlap_ratio, and say the ratio is computed on the same perturbations as the gain and floored at 1.

verdict.evidence_checked: docs/PAPER_COMPARISON.md:150 '### The fair test'; :152 '`tools/feature_compare.py` scores every arm alike'; :157 '`--with-val1` stays off'; :170-171 'The minimum effect. The mean gain must exceed max(2 SE_adj, 0.002), where SE_adj is the paired standard error widened by the perturbations' target-gene overlap (`tools/sealed_reading.py`) and 0.002 is the package's noise rule'. tools/feature_compare.py:484-487 'def overlap_ratio(diff, genes_of)' docstring 'sqrt(e'Oe / e'e) ... the core of tools/sealed_reading.py _cluster_ratio. 1 when no two perturbations share a gene.'; :507 'ratio = overlap_ratio(np.array([a[p] - b[p] for p in perts]), [data.genes_of[p] for p in perts])' (the deciding tier's own differences); :508 'se_adj = s["se"] * max(1.0, ratio or 1.0)'; :918 the verdict reads m1["se_adj"]. tools/sealed_reading.py:97-99 'def _cluster_ratio ... How much sharing genes widens the paired standard error, estimated on visible labels only: on the visible validation perturbations'; :107-110 scores visible_predictions and takes perts from lab_a._val1.perts; :102-103 'exactly 1 when no two perturbations share a gene (always on a bundle of single-gene perturbations), and 0 when the overlap terms sum below zero (the arm reading inflates only above 1)'. tools/arm_reading.py:7-9 'paired standard error s_r, the latter multiplied by the run's gene-clustering ratio when it exceeds 1 (the leave-one-gene-out jackknife SE over the plain SE on visible labels, which tools/sealed_reading.py records)' (the ratio is applied to the sealed SE). docs/FEATURE_COMPARISON_PROTOCOL.md:239-240 'SE inflated by the gene-overlap ratio (`tools/sealed_reading.py:97-130`)' and :360-361 'SE_adj widened by the gene-overlap ratio as in `tools/sealed_reading.py`' (the paper inherited the protocol's citation convention). git diff cfa8034..origin/claude/block-h-script-gaps -- docs/PLAN_H_COMPARISON.md: only a new dated note (22:00 UTC, probe reset and run_biomni.py's rate); PR #70 touches neither the paper nor this sentence.
verdict.note: Confirmed as the finding states it. The sentence sits inside the section that describes tools/feature_compare.py, and the SE_adj that the verdict uses there is feature_compare.py's own (overlap_ratio on the same tier's per-perturbation differences, max(1, ratio)); sealed_reading.py's _cluster_ratio has the same formula but is estimated on the visible validation labels and is applied by arm_reading.py to a sealed SE. A reader following the citation would conclude that the fair test reads val1, which the paper itself denies three lines earlier (--with-val1 stays off). The protocol (lines 239-240, 360-361) uses the same citation convention, which is where the paper got it, so this is inherited imprecision, not a wrong formula. It changes no number: on Adamson's single-gene perturbations no two share a target gene, so the ratio is 1 and SE_adj = SE whichever implementation is cited. Side drift seen while checking, not part of the finding: arm_reading.py:8-9 still describes the ratio as the leave-one-gene-out jackknife, which sealed_reading.py:104-106 now only reports beside the overlap-robust ratio.
verdict.corrected_fix: In PAPER lines 170-171 replace '(`tools/sealed_reading.py`)' with '(`tools/feature_compare.py`, `overlap_ratio` and `paired`: the ratio sqrt(e'Oe/e'e) of `tools/sealed_reading.py`'s `_cluster_ratio`, computed on the deciding tier's own per-perturbation differences, the same perturbations as the gain, and floored at 1; it is 1 when no two perturbations share a target gene, as on Adamson's singles)'. The same wording can replace the protocol's citations at lines 239-240 and 360-361, and the arm_reading.py docstring (lines 8-9) should say 'overlap-robust ratio' rather than 'jackknife'.
verdict.reviewer_sentence: Section 'The fair test' attributes SE_adj to tools/sealed_reading.py, but the fair test's SE_adj is computed by tools/feature_compare.py (overlap_ratio and paired, lines 484-514) on the deciding tier's own per-perturbation differences and floored at 1, whereas sealed_reading.py's _cluster_ratio estimates the ratio on the visible validation labels for the arm reading to apply to a sealed SE. Cite the code that runs, and note that on Adamson's single-gene perturbations the ratio is 1.

findings.title: Fresh test drops the 0.002 minimum effect the development verdict requires
findings.claim: The mean gain must exceed max(2 SE_adj, 0.002), where ... 0.002 is the package's noise rule
findings.problem: The confirmatory reading keeps only the 2·SE and wins conditions; a fresh-test gain of 0.001 at 3 SE would be 'useful' although the same gain fails the development screen. If 0.002 is a floor of practical interest it should hold at the tier that makes the claim; if only a screening device the paper should say so.
findings.evidence: PAPER 205-206; docs/PLAN_R_FRESH_TEST.md:149-150 (no minimum effect); tools/feature_compare.py:920-921 if "mean_diff" in m1 and not m1["mean_diff"] > MIN_GAIN: failed.append(...).
findings.fix: Either add 'and above 0.002' to the fresh-test feature rule in PAPER and PLAN_R section 7, or state that the minimum effect is a screening threshold only.
