PR #70's only document change is the PLAN_H note on scripts.
verdict.note: Confirmed. The development verdict (feature_compare.py:920-921) and ROADMAP A.1 require the gain to clear 0.002, which D3 and the tool call 'the minimum effect of practical interest', while every statement of the fresh-test rule (PAPER 205-207, PLAN_R 149-151, GOAL_CRITERIA A.4, protocol tier F item 4) asks only for 2 SE, wins and the sign. So a feature that reaches the batch (it needs a development verdict, hence an OOF gain above 0.002) could be called 'useful' on R2 at a confirmed gain of, say, 0.001 at 3 SE, below the effect the same paper says is the smallest of practical interest. The documents carry both framings of 0.002 ('noise rule' of the package's keep loop, which is a screening device; 'minimum effect of practical interest', which is a claim-level floor) without choosing, which is exactly the ambiguity the finding names. Nothing in the dated notes resolves it. The rule as written is a valid rule, and candidates are pre-screened, so this is a wording and consistency matter; but because the fresh-test reading is pre-registered and fixed when the batch is posted on #41 (PLAN_R section 4), the choice must be written before then, not after the holder's report. The protocol's tier F item 4 (Holm-adjusted p at 0.05 rather than 2 SE) is a further, older formulation that should be aligned with whichever is chosen.
verdict.corrected_fix: Before the batch is posted on #41, decide once and write it in PAPER lines 205-207, PLAN_R section 7 (the A.4 bullet, lines 149-151) and GOAL_CRITERIA A.4 (lines 21-22): either 'gain above max(2 SE, 0.002)' at the fresh test, or one sentence in the PAPER's fair-test paragraph and in PLAN_R section 7 such as '0.002 is the package's keep rule and the development screen's minimum; the fresh test reads the gain's size and paired SE and claims no minimum effect, and a replicated gain below 0.002 is reported as replicated but below the development minimum'. Align the protocol's tier F item 4 (lines 362-364) with the same rule. As PLAN_R is a dated document, add it in section 8 or a dated note rather than an edit.
verdict.reviewer_sentence: The development verdict requires a gain above max(2 SE_adj, 0.002), with 0.002 called the minimum effect of practical interest (ROADMAP D3, feature_compare.py MIN_GAIN), but the fresh-test rule (paper lines 205-207, PLAN_R section 7, GOAL_CRITERIA A.4) asks only for 2 SE, wins and the sign, so a feature could be declared useful at a confirmed gain below the stated minimum. State, before the batch is posted, whether 0.002 is a screening threshold or a floor that the confirmatory reading also applies.

findings.title: 'With the pre-registered sign' is undefined for features outside the prereg families
findings.claim: A feature is useful when ... with the pre-registered sign.
findings.problem: Signs were pre-registered only for the families the three per-gene tables allow. A Biomni or Codex feature built from Reactome, CORUM or STRING, or any lab feature outside those families, has no pre-registered sign, so the rule cannot be applied to most block H features and the paper does not say whether such a feature can be 'useful' at all.
findings.evidence: docs/ROADMAP.md:59-62 D3 pre-registers 'for each family the agents can build from the tables'; docs/PREREG_G_KNOWN_BIOLOGY.md:25-27; PAPER 173.
findings.fix: Add: 'for a feature with no pre-registered family the sign condition is void; its sign is recorded and no mechanism claim is made'.

findings.title: The Mac's file hash is an md5; the holder's check is a sha256; the manifest may record none
findings.claim: Replogle et al. 2022 K562 CRISPRi screens (ReplogleWeissman2022_K562_gwps.h5ad, Zenodo 13350497, md5 13db594f8f1d2ccb88fec44a13e414dc ...) ... The holder ... posts its sha256 on #41
findings.problem: Commit-then-reveal on 'the same public file' needs the two copies compared by one digest. The paper and the Mac's records give the Zenodo md5; the holder is asked for a sha256; the manifest tool records a sha256 only if --h5ad-sha256 is passed and otherwise prints 'not given', so nothing may tie the manifest's eligible list to the file the holder scores.
findings.evidence: tools/replogle_slice_manifest.py:322 ap.add_argument("--h5ad-sha256", default=None, ...); :290 File sha256: {h['sha256'] or 'not given'}; docs/PLAN_R_FRESH_TEST.md:177.
findings.fix: Make --h5ad-sha256 required (or compute it in the tool), require the holder to post both md5 and sha256, and state both digests in PAPER 178 and PLAN_R section 8.

findings.title: The HGNC mapping file is not pinned in the manifest
findings.claim: tools/replogle_slice_manifest.py reads only the file's obs and var tables ... A target is eligible when it has at least 20 cells, names exactly one gene, is not among the Adamson or Norman bundle targets and is inside the frozen gene universe.
findings.problem: Eligibility, the exclusion sets and the common gene panel depend on the HGNC complete set's retired-to-current mapping, which changes between releases. The manifest records only whether mapping was on, not which file; the paper's eligibility paragraph does not mention the mapping. A later reader cannot recompute the eligible list from the manifest and the seed alone.
findings.evidence: tools/replogle_slice_manifest.py:267 "gene_universe_size": len(universe), "hgnc": hgnc is not None,; :328 --hgnc help 'HGNC complete set, tab-separated, to map retired symbols'; docs/PLAN_R_FRESH_TEST.md:75-78.
findings.fix: Record the HGNC file's name, download date and sha256 under rules in manifest.json (and the frozen manifest's sha256 beside it), and add one sentence to PAPER 'Eligibility' naming the mapping and its pinned file.

findings.title: In-distribution rule: 'training panel' wording vs the whole 88-target list; coverage unbounded
findings.claim: An in-distribution subset is pre-registered from metadata alone: targets sharing a Reactome or CORUM class with a target of the Adamson bundle (its whole target list; no split file is read); under 30 such targets in R2 ... not powered.
findings.problem: The tool's docstring and rendered manifest call the panel the 'training panel', while the code and the paper use targets.json, the whole 88-target list including the 17 visible and 21 sealed targets the frozen models never trained on; the rationale holds for 50 of the 88. The plan fixes a floor (30) but no ceiling: the clean bundle keeps sets up to 500 genes within the 2,055-gene universe, so the out-of-distribution subset may be near empty and nothing says how that is read.
findings.evidence: tools/replogle_slice_manifest.py:8-9 'holds a target of the training panel'; :302-303; :355 panel=load_symbols(args.panel) with :93 (every target of targets.json); genemila/data/knowledge.py:37-38 MIN_SET_SIZE = 3 ... MAX_SET_SIZE = 500; genemila/data/knowledge_clean.py:30.
findings.fix: Rename 'training panel' to 'bundle target list' in the tool and manifest, or pass the 50 training targets (from public.npz train_perts) as the panel and say so; pre-register the set-size cap and a rule for reading the subsets when the in-distribution share exceeds, say, 80 percent of eligible targets.

findings.title: The frozen batch names 'the additive rule', which Adamson lacks; the baselines are not enumerated in one place
findings.claim: PLAN: 'per arm its three system models, at most three single features ..., plus the additive rule and C0, listed with sha256 on #41'; PAPER: 'plus P0 (the built-in start; Adamson has no additive rule) and C0'.
findings.problem: Block H is Adamson only; its parent is control_mean, mean_response, is_target with no additive_response (a pair-bundle builtin), and the tool reports no additive baseline on this bundle. The plan's reading 3 and PLAN_R section 4 list a batch member that cannot be built while the paper lists P0, so the set of baselines, and hence the Holm family, differs between the documents; B.4's 'beats each baseline' does not enumerate the Adamson baselines (P0, C0, C2?).
findings.evidence: tools/feature_compare.py:1035 p_feats = list(BUILTIN_FEATURES) + (["additive_response"] if data.pair_ids else []); genemila/features/registry.py:12 BUILTIN_FEATURES = ["control_mean", "mean_response", "is_target"], :15 PAIR_BUILTIN_FEATURES = ["additive_response"]; docs/results/adamson_cf_g_sealed_summary.md:5 'The tool reports no additive baseline on this singles bundle.'; docs/PLAN_R_FRESH_TEST.md:103-104; docs/GOAL_CRITERIA.md:40.
findings.fix: In PLAN reading 3 and PLAN_R section 4 replace 'the additive rule' with 'P0, the built-in start (the additive rule only on a bundle with pairs)', add the same parenthesis to ROADMAP D8, and list the Adamson baselines the arm rule reads against with the resulting number of paired comparisons.

verdict.evidence_checked: docs/PLAN_H_COMPARISON.md:20 '## Arms, all on Adamson'; :224-226 '3. **The frozen batch for the fresh test** (D8): per arm its three system models, at most three single features with a development verdict and the largest OOF gain, plus the additive rule and C0, listed with sha256 on #41 before any contact with the holder'; the dated notes (lines 235-384) grep'd for batch/frozen/reading 3/D8/PLAN_R: no hit, so no note amends reading 3; the PR #70 branch adds only the 22:00 UTC note on the probe reset and run_biomni.py. docs/PAPER_COMPARISON.md:76-80 'Every arm starts from the same parent P0 ... `additive_response` only on a bundle with pairs ...; Adamson has no pairs, so its parent has no additive rule.'; :184 'Norman gets no fresh test'; :199-200 'plus P0 (the built-in start; Adamson has no additive rule) and C0'; :207-211 'An arm beats a baseline under `tools/arm_reading.py`'s rule ... Every paired comparison in the batch enters one Holm correction at 0.05.'; :263 Table 1 row 'P0, the built-in start (no additive rule on Adamson)'. docs/PLAN_R_FRESH_TEST.md:101-104 'On Adamson these are block G's G1 and G0 runs ..., the one-worker lab row, the two foreign arms of block H, CellForge's translated ideas (C2), the scripted no-LLM control and the additive rule.'; :153-157 'each arm's three system models against each baseline under `tools/arm_reading.py`'s rule ... Holm over the batch: every paired comparison in the batch, features and arms, enters one Holm correction at 0.05; nothing outside the posted batch is tested.' docs/ROADMAP.md:108-109 D8 'The frozen batch for the fresh test (three system models per arm, at most three single features per arm, the additive rule, the scripted control)'; :184-185 B.4 'otherwise the paper reports what wins, the additive rule included.'; :347 'on Adamson the parent has no `additive_response` column'. docs/GOAL_CRITERIA.md:40-41 '4. Our arm's mean over seeds beats each baseline on the fresh test by more than twice the paired standard error, with wins on more than half the perturbations.' (baselines unnamed). genemila/features/registry.py:12 'BUILTIN_FEATURES = ["control_mean", "mean_response", "is_target"]'; :13-15 'built in on a bundle whose targets include a pair of genes only ... every other bundle (Adamson's) keeps the three above' / 'PAIR_BUILTIN_FEATURES = ["additive_response"]'. tools/feature_compare.py:1035 'p_feats = list(BUILTIN_FEATURES) + (["additive_response"] if data.pair_ids else [])'. tools/sealed_reading.py:7-9 'the built-in additive start (baseline_ridge_additive) on a bundle with pairs since c6fadc0, else the starting model the run reports (Lab.best_baseline)'. docs/results/adamson_cf_g_sealed_summary.md:5 'Each already selected model against its own recorded fresh start EXP_0003. The tool reports no additive baseline on this singles bundle.'
verdict.note: Confirmed on every point, and one more place carries the same error than the finding lists. Block H and the fresh test are Adamson only (PLAN_H line 20; PAPER 184; PLAN_R 101), and on Adamson the lab has no additive model: the parent is the three built-ins (registry.py:12-15; feature_compare.py:1035) and the sealed-reading tool reports no additive baseline there (sealed summary line 5). Yet PLAN_H reading 3, PLAN_R section 4, ROADMAP D8 and also ROADMAP section 5 B.4 (line 185, 'the additive rule included') name the additive rule as a batch member or baseline, while the paper substitutes P0 (lines 76-80, 199-200, 263). No dated note in PLAN_H or PLAN_R amends this. The baseline set that B.4's and PLAN_R 153's 'each baseline' reads against is enumerated nowhere (P0? C0, which PLAN_R 101-103 also lists as an arm? C2, a one-set row with no repeats, to which the arm rule's sd_g over R runs cannot apply?), so the number of paired comparisons entering the one Holm correction (PLAN_R 156) is not fixed by any document. The finding calls this minor; I grade it major because the plan says the batch is posted before contact with the holder and nothing is added after (PLAN_R 105-106), so the baseline set and the Holm family must be settled before that posting, which precedes submission; as written, posting the batch per the plans would either name a model that cannot be built or silently substitute one, a reading change at pre-registration time. It is not needed before block H's first paid session, only before the batch is listed. The wording drift itself is minor; the un-enumerated confirmatory family is what makes it major.
verdict.corrected_fix: In PLAN_H reading 3 (line 225), PLAN_R section 4 (lines 103-104), ROADMAP D8 (line 109) and ROADMAP section 5 B.4 (line 185) replace 'the additive rule' with 'P0, the built-in start (`control_mean`, `mean_response`, `is_target`; the additive rule only on a bundle with pairs, which Adamson is not)', as the paper already says at lines 76-80, 199-200 and 263. Then, in PLAN_R section 7 and the paper's reading-rule paragraph, enumerate the Adamson baselines that B.3/B.4's 'each baseline' reads against (P0 and C0; say whether C2, one set without repeats, is a baseline, a reported row, or both, and how the arm rule handles R = 1) and give the resulting count of paired comparisons that enter the single Holm correction (per arm: at most three features against P0, plus the system models against each named baseline), fixed on #41 together with the batch and its sha256 before any contact with the holder. Since PLAN_H, PLAN_R and ROADMAP are amended by dated notes, add it as a dated note at the end of PLAN_H, a line in PLAN_R section 8 and a ROADMAP note, not an edit of the earlier text (PAPER 228).
verdict.reviewer_sentence: The frozen batch for the fresh test is defined inconsistently: PLAN_H reading 3, PLAN_R section 4 and ROADMAP D8 (and B.4 at line 185) include 'the additive rule', a model that does not exist on Adamson (registry.py:12-15; feature_compare.py:1035; the sealed summary reports no additive baseline on this singles bundle), while the paper substitutes P0; and 'each baseline' in GOAL_CRITERIA B.4 and PLAN_R section 7 is never enumerated, so the number of paired comparisons entering the single Holm correction is not pre-registered. Name the Adamson baselines (P0, C0, and whether C2 counts) and the resulting comparison count before the batch is posted on #41.

findings.title: GOAL_CRITERIA B.4's rule differs from the paper's arm rule
findings.claim: An arm beats a baseline under tools/arm_reading.py's rule: the mean gain G over the R runs exceeds k·SE with SE = sqrt(S² + sd_g²/R)
findings.problem: B.4, which the paper serves, says the arm's mean over seeds beats each baseline 'by more than twice the paired standard error, with wins on more than half the perturbations': no sd_g term, no Welch k, no same-sign condition. Two rules now define the same criterion; the paper should name the registered one and that B.4 was restated.
findings.evidence: docs/GOAL_CRITERIA.md:40-41; docs/ROADMAP.md:184-185 'B.4: our arm beats a baseline only under tools/arm_reading.py's rule on the fresh test after correction'.
findings.fix: Add: 'B.4 is read under the arm rule (ROADMAP section 5), which restates GOAL_CRITERIA B.4 with the run-to-run term and the same-sign condition'.

verdict.evidence_checked: docs/GOAL_CRITERIA.md:40-41 B.4 'Our arm's mean over seeds beats each baseline on the fresh test by more than twice the paired standard error, with wins on more than half the perturbations. If it does not, the paper reports what wins.'; the whole file (44-157) carries no dated restatement of B.4 (contrast A.1 at :13-15, which carries the inline note 'first written as the pooled Holm p, restated 2026-10-17 to the statistic the tool decides on, as ROADMAP section 5 says'). docs/ROADMAP.md:168 '## 5. Stop and continue rules'; :184-185 'B.4: our arm beats a baseline only under tools/arm_reading.py's rule on the fresh test after correction; otherwise the paper reports what wins, the additive rule included.' docs/PLAN_R_FRESH_TEST.md:153-154 'B.3 and B.4 (arms): each arm's three system models against each baseline under tools/arm_reading.py's rule (G above k·SE, SE = sqrt(S² + sd_g²/R), one sign, most wins)'. tools/arm_reading.py:12-14 'SE = sqrt(S² + sd_g²/R). The gain counts when G exceeds k·SE with k = max(2, Student t at 0.975 on Welch–Satterthwaite's degrees of freedom), every g_r has G's sign, and summed over the runs the side G favours wins on more than half the perturbation-run pairs'; :61-65 RULE string, the same. docs/PAPER_COMPARISON.md:4 'serving goal b of docs/GOAL_CRITERIA.md (B.1 to B.5)'; :207-210 'An arm beats a baseline under tools/arm_reading.py's rule: the mean gain G over the R runs exceeds k·SE with SE = sqrt(S² + sd_g²/R), S the mean of the runs' paired standard errors and sd_g the spread of the runs' gains, k = max(2, Student t at 0.975 on Welch-Satterthwaite degrees of freedom), every run's gain has G's sign, and the favoured side wins on more than half the perturbation-run pairs'; grep 'B\.4' over the paper: no hit (only 'B.1 to B.5' at line 4). PR #70 branch: no change to GOAL_CRITERIA, ROADMAP or PAPER.
verdict.note: Seen as described: GOAL_CRITERIA B.4 is the registered rule (2 × paired SE, more than half the wins), ROADMAP section 5 and PLAN_R re-express it as tools/arm_reading.py's rule (SE widened by sd_g²/R, k ≥ 2 by Welch t, every run the same sign, wins over perturbation-run pairs), GOAL_CRITERIA carries no note of that restatement although A.1 got exactly such a note, and the paper states the arm rule without naming B.4 or the restatement. One qualification the finding omits: under the natural reading of B.4 (per-run paired SEs averaged), the arm rule is strictly stricter (SE ≥ S, k ≥ 2, two extra conditions), so a pass under the paper's rule is a pass under B.4 as registered and the mismatch cannot flip a verdict in the authors' favour. That keeps it minor: a wording and drift gap, to close before the fresh test is scored.
verdict.corrected_fix: In docs/PAPER_COMPARISON.md after line 210 add: 'This is GOAL_CRITERIA B.4 as restated in ROADMAP section 5 and PLAN_R: the registered rule (gain above twice the paired standard error, wins on more than half the perturbations) with the run-to-run term sd_g²/R in the standard error, k = max(2, Welch t) and the same-sign condition added, so it is stricter than B.4 as first written.' In docs/GOAL_CRITERIA.md give B.4 the same inline dated restatement A.1 carries at lines 13-15 ('restated <date> to tools/arm_reading.py's rule, as ROADMAP section 5 says'), before any fresh-test deposit.
verdict.reviewer_sentence: The paper's arm rule (standard error widened by the run-to-run spread, Welch k, same-sign condition) is not the rule registered as B.4 in GOAL_CRITERIA (twice the paired standard error, most wins); the authors should name the registered criterion, say where and when it was restated, and note that the applied rule is the stricter of the two.

findings.title: Table 1's 'ΔM1 ± SE_adj' is undefined for a three-session arm row
findings.claim: | arm | n sessions | OOF M1 | ΔM1 ± SE_adj vs P0 | wins | ...
findings.problem: SE_adj is a per-session paired quantity; an arm row with n = 3 has three. The block G precedent reports the arm's ΔM1 as mean ± sample sd over runs, and the arm rule's SE is sqrt(S² + sd_g²/R). The template does not say which the cell holds, so the ± convention changes between the header, the caption ('mean ± sd over three sessions') and the abstract ('± adjusted paired SE').

findings.title: pkg_checks accepts a package exported from the tier-3 bundle adamson_cf
findings.claim: the scripts require the package to match the file either way (pkg_checks)
findings.problem: The clean bundle's manifest name is adamson_cf_clean_tables, but pkg_checks also accepts the bare name adamson_cf, the original CellForge bundle with different knowledge files. A package exported from the wrong --data would pass every scripted check and only the printed bundle name and the operator's hash would show it.
findings.evidence: docs/mac/block_h/block_h_common.sh:82 (m.get("bundle") or "") not in ("adamson_cf_clean_tables", "adamson_cf"); tools/build_clean_bundle.py:106 new["name"] = f"{manifest['name']}_clean_tables" if tables else ...; tools/export_task_package.py:242 "bundle": manifest.get("name").
findings.fix: Accept only adamson_cf_clean_tables in pkg_checks.

verdict.evidence_checked: docs/mac/block_h/block_h_common.sh:82 `(f"bundle {m.get('bundle')}, split {m.get('split_id')}: not adamson_cf_clean_tables", (m.get("bundle") or "") not in ("adamson_cf_clean_tables", "adamson_cf"))` (the message names one bundle, the test accepts two; the split is printed at :84 but never checked, and both bundles share it). Same line unchanged on the PR #70 branch (its block_h_common.sh:98). tools/build_clean_bundle.py:15 `manifest with the name '<name>_clean' (or '<name>_clean_tables' when tables are included)`; :106 `new["name"] = f"{manifest['name']}_clean_tables" if tables else f"{manifest['name']}_clean"`; :111 `"from_bundle": manifest["name"]`. genemila/data/real.py:429 `return write_bundle(Path(out_dir), name, ...)` and genemila/data/bundle.py:195 `"name": name` (the source bundle's manifest name is its dataset key, adamson_cf). tools/export_task_package.py:242 `"bundle": manifest.get("name")`; :253 the export record holds `"bundle": package["bundle"]` and the output path, never the `--data` path. PLAN:20 `bundle data/adamson_cf_clean_tables (split split_450515be1a0d8d2e: the clean bundle keeps data/adamson_cf's split`; PLAN:39 `python tools/export_task_package.py --data <MAIN>/data/adamson_cf_clean_tables --out $HOME/gm_packages/adamson_cf_clean_tables`; PLAN:54-55 `the scripts require the package to match the file either way (pkg_checks)`. docs/PLAN_G_CLEAN_ARM.md:418 `== adamson_cf_clean_tables` listing seven knowledge files (gene_annotation, gene_constraint, gene_sets, ppi_network, prior_network, protein_annotation, targets) against adamson_cf's five. docs/mac/block_h/block_h_a2.sh:21-45: the lab arm's bundle check compares knowledge files and split_id against `$MAIN/data/adamson_cf`; pkg_checks has no equivalent for the package's data.
verdict.note: Confirmed as written. The clean bundle's manifest name is `adamson_cf_clean_tables` (build_clean_bundle.py:106 appends the suffix to the source's name, which real.py sets to the dataset key), the exporter copies that name into MANIFEST.json['bundle'] (export_task_package.py:242), and pkg_checks accepts the bare `adamson_cf` as well while its own PROBLEM message says 'not adamson_cf_clean_tables'. Nothing else scripted distinguishes the two: the split_id is shared by construction (PLAN line 20), the export record stores the output path and bundle name but not the `--data` source, and no check reads the package's knowledge list. A package exported from `data/adamson_cf` would therefore pass every scripted check, and only the printed bundle name and the operator's reading of the sha256 on #41 would show it. The hazard is small (the plan's command names the clean bundle, and the package directory carries its name) and the fix is one token, so minor. Not changed by PR #70.
verdict.corrected_fix: In pkg_checks accept only `adamson_cf_clean_tables` (`(m.get("bundle") or "") != "adamson_cf_clean_tables"`), and also check `m.get("split_id") == "split_450515be1a0d8d2e"` so the printed split is a test, not just a print. Optionally record the exporter's `--data` path in the .export.json record so the package's source bundle is on the record.
verdict.reviewer_sentence: pkg_checks admits a package whose MANIFEST.json names the tier-3 bundle `adamson_cf` as well as the clean `adamson_cf_clean_tables`, although its own error message names only the latter and the two bundles share a split_id, so a package exported from the wrong `--data` would pass every scripted check; the accept list should hold the clean bundle's name only.

verdict.note: The two operational objections stand: the plan's "exact command" for C0 uses a relative `.venv/bin/python` from the pinned checkout `gene-mila-baa7dfd`, which by PLAN_G's own rule (141-143) has no venv (every block script, G and H alike, runs `cd $WT` then `$MAIN/.venv/bin/python run_research.py`), so the line as written fails with no such file unless the operator corrects it by hand; and C0 is the one Table 1 arm with no script, no place in block_h_chain.sh, and so none of the pre-run checks (commit, clean tree, bundle, no other run) or the after-run summary.json check that block_h_a2.sh gives A2. Severity minor: the runs are free and deterministic, the records needed to check them after the fact exist, and the failure mode is a wasted free run, not a wrong number; but C0 is a row of Table 1 and the plan calls these its exact commands. Not touched by PR #70.

findings.title: The claude probe call does not use the flags run_autoresearch.sh uses
findings.claim: then one one-turn claude -p call on ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=<proxy>/anthropic (run id h_probe_claude, the flags run_autoresearch.sh uses)
findings.problem: The probe's claude command omits --permission-mode acceptEdits, the --allowedTools list and --output-format stream-json --verbose, and passes --disallowedTools as one comma-joined argument where the runner passes three words. A probe that passes under these flags does not show that the arm's own invocation starts.

findings.fix: Give run_autoresearch.sh a --probe flag like run_codex.sh and have the probe call it, so the arm and the probe share one command.

findings.title: The 30-minute hard stop does not reach the agent's process group in account mode
findings.claim: the agent for 20 minutes, the runner's own clock (--minutes 20), with a hard stop at 30 minutes from the script
findings.problem: In account mode the script kills the backgrounded sudo, which relays SIGTERM to the runner process only. run_biomni.py's parent has no SIGTERM handler and starts its child in a new session, so the parent dies and the Biomni child keeps running; the same holds for bash running run_codex.sh, whose python watchdog the signal never reaches. proxy_down stops the money, but the surviving agent can still write into the work copy while collect_handback reads it, and nothing records that a process was left behind.
findings.evidence: docs/mac/block_h/block_h_common.sh:160-164 ... [ "$MODE" = docker ] && docker kill h_agent ...; kill "$AGENT_PID" 2> /dev/null; tools/baselines/run_biomni.py:175 subprocess.Popen(..., start_new_session=True) and no signal.signal in parent(); tools/baselines/run_codex.sh:199-201 (watchdog as a background job, SIGTERM handler at :194 only inside it).
findings.fix: After the kill in account mode run sudo -u "$ACCOUNT" pkill -TERM -u "$ACCOUNT" (then -KILL after 20 s) and record 'hard stop' in the session's check file; or give run_biomni.py's parent a SIGTERM handler that forwards to the child's group.

findings.title: The val1 scan counts the package's own features/README.md, so the read count is never zero
findings.claim: the session script counts the files the agent wrote or printed (...) that name val1.npz or harness/val1, the package's own MANIFEST.json and program.md left out
findings.problem: With the harness tier shipped, the exporter writes 'the visible validation labels are under harness/val1.npz' into features/README.md, which lives in the scanned $W/features and is copied again into the runner's out directory. The scan therefore reports at least two files for every session whether or not the agent read the tier, and reading 4 starts from a false positive.
findings.evidence: docs/mac/block_h/block_h_common.sh:184-185 grep -rIl ... --exclude=MANIFEST.json --exclude=program.md -e 'val1\.npz' -e 'harness/val1' "$O" "$W/features" ...; tools/export_task_package.py:132-134 labels_note(tier), :150-151 features_readme uses {labels_note(tier)}; tools/baselines/run_biomni.py:203-205 copies features/ into out/.
findings.fix: Add --exclude=README.md to the scan, or diff the scanned tree against the pristine package copy and count only files that are new or changed.
